x: The Geländewagen began as a military truck, commissioned in the early 1970s after the Shah of Iran — then one of Mercedes-Benz’s largest shareholders — pre-ordered some 20,000 of them. Mercedes engineered it; Steyr-Daimler-Puch built it in Graz, Austria, and production began in 1979. The utilitarian W460 and later W461 served armies, border police and farmers. In 1990 the civilian W463 moved upmar

W460 230 GE 280 GE 300 GD The original military-derived G, in short and long wheelbase, petrol and diesel. The original Geländewagen: built for a Shah, bought by armies, blessed by a Pope and slower up a motorway on-ramp than most tractors. It is the purest G there is, and it will happily outlive you if you keep the rust and the hydraulics in check.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: About a 32-inch 235/85R16 on the stock steel wheels. An Expedition Portal owner runs 235/85R16s on standard steel wheels on a short-wheelbase G. The original fitment was a skinny 205 R16, and many owners stay close to 215/85R16 because a naturally aspirated diesel struggles to turn a bigger tire up hills. For 33s and up, plan on lift springs.

t: Is the W460 full-time four-wheel drive?
x: No. It's part-time: you engage the front axle by lever through the transfer case, with high and low range. Permanent 4WD arrived with the 1989–90 W463. Don't drive a W460 in 4WD on dry pavement.

t: Do all W460s have locking differentials?
x: Not all of them. Mercedes made front and rear locks standard on every W460 from 1985, so earlier trucks may not have them. Look for the locker control on the dash and the slave cylinders on the axles. A W460 never had the W463's third (centre) lock.

The 300 GD was the most popular W460 and the 280 GE the most powerful. Auto Bild names the 230 GE and the 300 GD, with their long-lived manual gearboxes, as the ones to have. The OM617 five-cylinder in the 300 GD has a reputation for reaching huge mileages, but it's slow and was never turbocharged in a W460.

Not very. Factory figures for a 300 GD are 88 PS, 0–100 km/h in about 27 seconds and a 127 km/h (79 mph) top speed. An IH8MUD owner says his mildly modified OM617 ran out of power around 70 mph. A 280 GE is good for about 165 km/h.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Mercedes' cycle figures for the 300 GD run from 11.7 to 18.8 L/100 km, roughly 12.5–20 mpg US. The 280 GE is thirstier, at 14.0–22.4 L/100 km (about 10.5–17 mpg). Big tires, a roof rack and a lift make both worse.

t: Was the W460 sold in the US?
x: Not by Mercedes. Grey-market specialists federalised some in the 1980s until the 1988 Motor Vehicle Safety Compliance Act made it much harder. Official US sales didn't begin until the 2002 model year, and before that Europa International imported later W463s.

t: W460, W461 or W463 — what's the difference?
x: The W460 (1979–1991) is the original, with part-time 4WD and two lockers. The W461 kept the W460's body and chassis but used W463 running gear, and was built for armies, authorities and NGOs. The W463 is the civilian luxury G from 1990, with permanent 4WD, three lockers, ABS and wood trim.

In the US they're scarce and expensive, according to IH8MUD owners. In Europe, Auto Bild says Mercedes dealers still stock most parts at high prices and used parts are plentiful. Specialists such as Expedition Imports stock W460 axle, locker, steering and cooling parts, and some components are shared with Mercedes cars and vans.

Classic & Sports Car's 2023 guide put a pre-1990 hardtop at £5,000 as a project, £14,000 average and £27,000+ for a show truck. Soft-tops run £12,000 / £30,000 / £75,000+. For a US example, a rusty, re-engined 1986 300 GD project sold for $13,000 on PCARMARKET in January 2022.

t: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
x: No. A locked diff stops the wheels turning at different speeds, so on grippy surfaces the driveline binds and the tires scrub. Lock on dirt, sand, snow or rock at low speed, and unlock before you're back on tarmac.

x: The G 300 CDI Professional comes on 265/75R16s, about 31.6 inches. Beyond that you're into lift springs: GwagenParts' ROGUE spring listing talks about 33- and 35-inch tires, and warns that bigger tires can trigger ABS and ESP warnings.

t: What's the difference between a W461 and a W463?
x: The W461 uses the W460's narrow body and chassis with W463 running gear, plain trim, and barn doors and panel-van bodies you can't get on a W463. Military trucks also have 24-volt electrics. The W463 is the luxury civilian G with wood, leather and more electronics.

t: Is the 250 GD 'Wolf' a W460 or a W461?
x: Expedition Motor Company, which restores them, calls the 250 GD Wolf an ex-military W461, and Wikipedia lists the 1990–91 Wolf in the W461 table. The line between late military W460s and early W461s is blurry, so check the VIN and data card on the truck in front of you.

t: Could civilians buy a new W461?
x: Yes, in limited form. Mercedes sold the G 280 CDI EDITION.30 PUR in 2009, followed by the G 280 CDI Professional (2009) and the G 300 CDI Professional (2010–2019). In Australia the G 300 CDI Professional cab-chassis launched in 2016 at A$119,900, and the wagon followed in 2017 at A$109,900.

t: How much can it carry and tow?
x: 4X4 Australia's figures for the G 300 CDI Professional cab-chassis: 2,410 kg kerb weight, 4,490 kg GVM, about 2,080 kg payload and 2,210 kg towing capacity, with a 6,700 kg GCM.

Yes. The G 300 CDI Professional has permanent all-wheel drive with a 50:50 split, a two-speed transfer case and three locking diffs selectable on the move. Unusually, you can unlock the centre diff even in low range.

t: Does it really run on 24 volts?
x: Military W461s do. Wikipedia lists the 24-volt system as one of the W461's defining features, and parts suppliers stock 24 V components such as blower motors. The Australian civilian Professional wagon is described as carrying two 12-volt batteries. Check what your truck actually has before wiring in accessories.

t: Which engine should I look for?
x: For highway use, the 1998–2001 290 GD Turbodiesel or later: the G 270 CDI (156 PS, 400 Nm) and the OM642 V6 in the G 280/300 CDI (184 PS, 400 Nm). The naturally aspirated 290 GD (95 PS) and the 250 GD Wolf are charming and simple but very slow.

t: How big is the fuel tank?
x: 96–97 litres on the G 300 CDI Professional, depending on whether you read WhichCar or 4X4 Australia.

t: Why does the late W461 have a bonnet bulge?
x: It clears an air pump that's part of the emissions equipment, according to 4X4 Australia. The W460 doesn't have one.
No. Civilian production ended in 2019, and military production continued until 2022, when the W464 took over. Mercedes announced the W464 on 1 October 2021.

W463 The civilian G: full-time 4WD, three lockers, ever-more luxury — and still solid axles. Twenty-eight years and engines from four to twelve cylinders, all on the same ladder frame and two solid axles. It became a rapper's accessory and stayed a real off-roader the whole time. Buy one for the three lockers and keep a budget for the vacuum lines.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: About 33 inches. A 275/70R18 on the factory 18s fits an unlifted G 500/G 550, according to Expedition Portal owners. JWO designed its 4-inch springs specifically to clear tires bigger than 33 inches without rubbing. Some owners squeeze in more, such as one G 500 on 315/75R16s with no lift, and offset ET63 wheels help, but 35s on stock springs will usually rub somewhere at full compression or lock.

t: Which W463 engine is the most reliable?
x: Handsome Motors ranks it G 500 → G 55 → G 550 → G 63 for mechanical reliability, and calls the 2002–2015 V8s the safest bets. In Europe, Autocar names the G 320 CDI diesel V6 the best all-rounder. Avoid neglected G 63s unless you've budgeted for big brakes and cooling-system work.
2.16:1 through the two-speed transfer case.

t: How do the three lockers work, and in what order?
x: You press the dash buttons and a controller engages them in sequence: centre first, then rear, then front. Each one locks after the truck has rolled a short distance. Vacuum operates the centre lock and the valves; hydraulics move the front and rear locks. Unlock everything before you're back on pavement.

t: Was the W463 sold in the US before 2002?
x: Yes, but not by Mercedes. Europa International of New Mexico federalised and sold them from 1993, and became the exclusive US importer of the G 500 with small-volume-manufacturer status. Those trucks have US VINs. Mercedes took over with the 2002 model year.

t: When did the manual gearbox disappear?
x: In 1994, when the 200, 230 and 300 GE were dropped. From 1996 the automatic was an electronically controlled five-speed. The seven-speed came in for 2007 on the US G 500.

t: Which years have ESP and traction control?
x: ESP, Brake Assist and the four-wheel electronic traction system (4ETS) arrived with the 2001–02 update that coincided with the official US launch. Earlier W463s have ABS but rely on the lockers alone for traction.

t: How often should I service the automatic?
x: Toolsource cites a 40–60k-mile interval for the five-speed 722.6, using MB 236.14 ATF. Handsome Motors suggests every 40–50k miles for the seven-speed. If the history is unknown, do it now.

t: Are the 2016–2018 G 550s with the twin-turbo V8 a good buy?
x: Handsome Motors says yes. The M176 is a lower-stressed relative of AMG's M177, and by those years the early electrical gremlins were gone. Watch for a failed crankcase-vent oil separator causing rear-main-seal and valve-cover leaks. The same dealer personally recommends 3–5k-mile oil changes.
It's an enthusiast label for the 2018-on second-generation G, which kept the W463 chassis code. Mercedes doesn't use the term itself.

t: How do I spot a fake AMG?
x: Check the VIN and the factory data card. Bumpers, flares, wheels and badges are easy to bolt on, and Autocar specifically warns about Gs converted to look like AMGs.

t: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
x: No. Locked diffs stop the wheels turning at different speeds, so on grippy surfaces the driveline binds and the tires scrub. Use them on dirt, sand, snow or rock at low speed.

t: Was it sold in the US?

t: How is it different from the later G 500?

With only 446 built, restoring one to factory spec is worth more than modifying it. Use specialists who do sympathetic G restorations.
Fresh dampers sort out most of the ride on a tired truck. One documented 500 GE runs Bilsteins. Keep the comfort-oriented ride height unless you need the clearance.

t: Is a Europa G a gray-market truck?
x: No. Europa certified the trucks to US emissions and safety standards, including crash testing, sold them with US VINs, and gained Small Volume Manufacturer status, making them 50-state legal. Gray-market Gs were private imports cleared one at a time.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: About 33 inches. An Expedition Portal owner runs 275/70R18 on an unlifted 2000 G 500 and only rubbed on aftermarket ET63 wheels. Another runs 285/65R18 with a slight rub at full left lock. Another owner says up to about 32 inches should clear with no rubbing. Have the tire size re-coded with Mercedes diagnostics so the speedometer and ESP stay accurate.

t: Which Europa G should I buy?
x: Forum regulars usually prefer the G 500 for its much greater power at similar mileage. German Cars For Sale Blog prefers the 300 GE or G 500 to the inline-six G 320 because of its head-gasket issue. One owner found the V6 G 320 more economical than a G 500, though the gap narrows when towing.

t: Do Europa trucks have all three lockers?
x: Yes. Scott Brady's 1996 Europa truck had dash buttons for the centre, rear and front locks, plus ABS and airbags.

t: How is a Europa G 500 different from a 2002 Mercedes-Benz USA G 500?
x: It looks nearly the same outside, apart from black-painted bumpers. Inside it has a pre-facelift W210 E-Class steering wheel and cluster, no wheel-mounted radio controls, older climate control, and a 722.6 automatic without the tip-shift gate. It also avoids the COMAND electronics that German Cars For Sale Blog blames for early MBUSA trucks' electrical problems.

t: How much did they cost new?
x: Hagerty says some sold for up to $135,000. The 1999 Neiman Marcus Christmas-catalogue G 500 was $160,000, and six were sold.

Usually about the same as 2002-on trucks. t: What’s the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: It doesn’t need one — the portal axles are the lift. Stock tires are 325/55R22, about 36 inches tall. When Mercedes showed the truck, it said 37×12.5×18 mud-terrains would be available for production trucks, and the Geneva show car wore 37-inch mud-terrains on beadlocks. Check caliper clearance before going to 18-inch wheels, and re-code the tire size.

t: Was the 4×4² sold in the US?
x: Yes, for the 2017 model year, as the G 550 4×4². Mercedes-Benz USA listed it at $225,000 plus a $925 destination charge, with deliveries from early 2017.

t: How much ground clearance and wading depth?
x: 17.24 inches at maximum load and 39.4 inches of fording depth in US spec — up 7.9 and 15.8 inches respectively over a 2016 G 550. European figures are 450 mm and 1,000 mm.

t: What are its approach and departure angles?
x: 51.6° approach and 43.8° departure. Mercedes quoted breakover as 47.4° in its launch release and 44.6° at maximum load in the spec sheet.

t: Is it just a G 63 6×6 with an axle missing?
x: Partly. It uses a shortened version of the 6×6’s chassis and portal running gear, but with the five-door long-wheelbase body, the G 500/G 550’s 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 and a seven-speed automatic.

t: What fuel economy does it get?
x: Mercedes-Benz USA’s spec sheet lists 11 mpg city, 11 highway and 11 combined. The fuel tank holds 25.4 gallons.

t: Will it fit in my garage?
x: Maybe not. It’s 88.0 inches tall, 86.2 inches wide including mirrors and 177.1 inches long, with a 46.9-foot turning circle.
6,694 lb curb weight — almost a thousand pounds more than a regular G 550.
Mercedes-Benz USA’s 2017 spec sheet listed towing as “TBA,” so check the owner’s manual and hitch rating for your specific truck rather than assuming the regular G 550’s figure.

t: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
x: No. Locked diffs bind the driveline on grippy surfaces. Lock up on loose ground at low speed and unlock before tarmac.

t: How is it different from the newer G 63 4×4²?
x: The 2022-on G 63 4×4² is built on the second-generation G with independent front suspension, makes 585 hp and costs $350,050. It has less clearance (13.8 in) and wading depth (35.8 in) than the original, and weighs 379 lb less.

t: Does it still have three locking differentials?
x: Yes — centre, rear and front, 100% locks, on every gas model. The electric G 580 drops mechanical lockers in favor of per-wheel torque vectoring.

t: Is it still body-on-frame with a solid axle?
x: It’s still on a ladder frame — even the EV. The rear axle is rigid; the front is now independent double wishbones, the first time a G has had independent front suspension.
2.93:1, versus about 2.1:1 on the previous G. It engages at up to 25 mph with the transmission in neutral, and you can shift back to high range at up to 43 mph.

t: How much ground clearance and wading depth?
x: 9.5 inches between the axles (10.6 inches to the front axle), 27.6 inches of wading depth, and 31° / 30° / 26° approach, departure and breakover angles. The G 580 EV has 9.8 inches and wades 33.5 inches.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The V8 G 550 is EPA-rated 14 mpg combined for 2019–2020; the mild-hybrid inline-six G 550 is rated 18 mpg combined for 2025–2026.

The 2019–2024 G 550’s 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 makes 416 hp and 450 lb-ft; the 2025-on 3.0-litre mild-hybrid six makes 443 hp and 413 lb-ft and is rated about 4 mpg better combined. Same lockers, same clearance.

t: What can the electric G 580 do off-road?
x: Climb 100% grades on suitable surfaces, hold 35° side slopes, wade 33.5 inches, crawl in three settings, and turn on the spot with G-Turn. It has a 2:1 low range in each axle’s transmission.
It’s an enthusiast label for the 2018-on truck. Mercedes-Benz doesn’t use it officially.

t: Are there recalls I should know about?

t: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
x: No. Locked diffs bind the driveline on high-grip surfaces. Use them on dirt, sand, snow or rock at low speed and unlock before tarmac.

It started as a 1951 prototype called the BJ, went into regular production in 1953, and picked up the name Land Cruiser in June 1954 — coined by Toyota's Hanji Umehara. What followed is one of the longest-running nameplates in the business and a lineage that splits, roughly, into two tribes: the utilitarian short- and long-wheelbase workhorses, and the station wagons that slowly learned to carry f

FJ40 BJ40 The two-door, short-wheelbase icon on leaf springs and F/2F straight-sixes — the truck that made the Land Cruiser name in America. The FJ40 is a farm implement that accidentally became a fashion icon: leaf springs, a straight-six with the manners of a tractor and steering vague enough to count as a suggestion. It is also the reason anybody outside Japan cares what a Land Cruiser is.

Grease and gear oil oozing from the knuckle wiper seals, a mix of grease and 90-weight inside the knuckle, or play when you lift a front wheel and shove it. Hub socket · brass drift · spring scale · seal driver · torque wrench · Cruiser Corps knuckle kit 514-108 (1958–9/1975) or 514-109 (9/1975–1/1990) · OEM knuckle wiper kit · moly grease

Loud ticking from the top end (loose valves), or poor running and burned valves (tight valves, which are the ones to worry about). Feeler gauges (fresh ones; soft gauges bend) · 17 mm wrench (a 17/19 mm socket-ended flex wrench helps) · new valve cover gasket and acorn-nut washers

Hesitation, stumbling, rough idle or stalling at low rpm on a truck with an original carburetor. Screwdrivers · carb cleaner · correct Keyster rebuild kit (by carb number, e.g. 21100-60280 for 9/1973–9/1975)

Sagging springs, cracked leaves, or a rear shackle that flips over center on a lifted truck. Jacks and stands · breaker bar · welder (anti-inversion plates) · ARB/OME kit (e.g. ARB-103 for 1975–8/1980) · urethane bushing kit A216
Soft or holed floors, often found with rotten body mounts on 1979–84 trucks. Cut-off wheel · MIG welder · clamps · seam sealer · Cruiser Corps 605-111L (left front, 1979–1984 FJ40/FJ45)

Excessive play or backlash at the wheel after tie rods and the center arm have been checked, or fluid weeping from a factory power-steering box. Pitman arm puller · seal kit 520-139 (1979–10/1984 FJ40/45) or conversion kit 524-117
Screaming highway rpm on 33s with a 1:1 top gear. Transmission jack · H55F (input shaft to suit the engine) · oiler pipe · shifter · linkage kit · gaskets

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The 'old tried and true' answer on IH8MUD is 31x10.50R15 on stock wheels and suspension. 33x9.50R15 is a popular size on stock 15-inch rims too, but owners report rubbing at the rear over bumps or at full flex. One fixed it with 1-inch spacers under the bump stops, and another had to adjust the front steering stops. One member said 33x10.50s looked 'pretty stuffed.'

t: Which years should I look for?
x: Most buyers prefer 1976-and-later trucks for front disc brakes and the 4.2 L 2F. 1979 added optional power steering and A/C and taller 3.70 gears in the US. IH8MUD veterans like the '78 and would consider 1979–83 at the right price, but note that 1980-and-later bodies seem to rust more readily.

The four-speed arrived with the 2F in 1975 in the US. Most owners prefer it, especially on 33-inch tires. If you want overdrive, the H55F five-speed swap is well documented, though it takes floor, crossmember, linkage and driveshaft work.

t: Did the US get diesel FJ40s?
x: Not for the general public. Diesel 40s were never sold to US retail buyers, though some arrived as mine trucks. Canada was the exception in 1984, when it got the BJ42 diesel with an overdrive five-speed for about CA$14,000.

Only optionally, on F-engine trucks from 1979. Earlier trucks have manual steering, and many owners fit a GM Saginaw power-steering conversion. It isn't a casual bolt-on, and Cruiser Corps recommends professional installation.

They work, but they need constant adjustment. Front discs came on US trucks in 1976. Bolt-on conversion kits exist for 1970–75 trucks, and IH8MUD has a write-up using mini-truck knuckles with later Land Cruiser calipers and rotors.

The common choice is an Old Man Emu 2-inch kit with greaseable anti-inversion shackles. For bigger lifts, some owners go spring-over-axle, which IH8MUD members say gives roughly 6 inches and is usually paired with power steering.

t: Should I swap in a V8?
x: Plenty of owners have. Hagerty notes many FJ40s got small-block Chevy V8s on the secondary market. The stock six is durable, though, and a healthy 2F with good compression will run a long time.

Yes. Toyota announced GR Heritage Parts reproductions for the 40 Series in 2021, starting with engine, driveline and exhaust parts. Specialists such as Cruiser Corps, CruiserTeq, Cool Cruisers of Texas and JT Outfitters stock everything from knuckle kits to floor pans.

It depends heavily on condition and originality. In 2019 Hagerty put the average #2-condition FJ40 at $47,375, after a 7.6 percent drop since 2016, with a 1968 at $49,100 and a 1975 at $44,800. Retro Rides says tidy Australian examples run roughly AU$30,000–50,000 and that US prices are far higher.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: We couldn't find a solid FJ55- or FJ45-specific consensus. They use 40 Series axles, and for the stock FJ40, IH8MUD's 'tried and true' size is 31x10.50R15, with 33x9.50R15 fitting but rubbing at full flex. Try any size on your own truck before committing.

t: What's the difference between an FJ45 and an FJ55?
x: The FJ45 is the long-wheelbase version of the 40 Series: pickups and cab-chassis on 2,950 mm and an early four-door wagon on 2,650 mm. The FJ55 (1967–80) is a purpose-built four-door wagon on a 2,700 mm wheelbase with its own fully boxed frame.

t: Why is it called the Iron Pig?
x: Hagerty traces the name to the FJ55's narrow front with headlamps set into the grille opening, which does resemble a pig's snout. Wikipedia also records 'Moose.'
1975–80 trucks have the 4.2 L 2F, a four-speed and front disc brakes. Earlier trucks use the 3.9 L F and a three-speed whose first gear has no synchro, which some collectors prefer for originality.
Generally not for the FJ55. Hagerty says replacement panels usually don't exist and have to be fabricated, and trim and weatherstripping are hard to find. Buy the most solid truck you can afford.

t: Are the drum brakes good enough?
x: Hagerty says stock drums are adequate if they're in good order and the powertrain is stock. Disc conversions are common and parts are easy to find.

Old Man Emu makes 2-inch kits for the FJ45 (1963–80 and 1980–84), sold through specialists such as Cruiser Corps, with greaseable shackles and a steering damper. Confirm fitment for an FJ55 before ordering.
Yes, with basic care. Hagerty calls the F and 2F durable with basic maintenance and periodic valve adjustments, and says mechanical repairs are easy and cheap compared with rust repair.

In Hagerty's FJ55 buyer's guide (first published in 2021 and updated in 2023), the median value for all conditions was $34,500 and for #2 condition $46,300, with quoted values up 65.8 percent since 2020. Its earlier wagon-values piece mentioned private sales approaching six figures.

t: Were FJ45s really used by armies?
x: Yes. Truck Encyclopedia describes the super-long-wheelbase FJ45 as a major military export used as a troop carrier, and the Irish Army took 77 FJ45s in 1977.

2F: 7.8 L (≈8.2 qt) with filter · F: 7 L · factory spec API SC/SD (use a modern oil suited to a flat-tappet engine) One IH8MUD owner warns the owner's manual figure led him to overfill; another always uses 8 qt in a 2F with a filter change. Fill to the dipstick, not the book. New drain-plug washer every time.
Paper element in the factory air cleaner Replace it before you judge how the carburetor runs.
Plugs, points (where fitted), cap & rotor · gap and dwell [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Check fuel and ignition basics before blaming the carburetor.

Adjustable rockers · clearances [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Hagerty notes the F and 2F want periodic valve adjustments; tight valves are the ones that burn. Valve layout front to back is E-I-I-E-E-I-I-E-E-I-I-E.

Ethylene-glycol coolant · 2F: 16.5 L (the original F table lists 15.2 L) The early F-engine table even lists plain water; use proper ethylene-glycol coolant now, flush until it runs clear, fit a fresh thermostat and check the bypass hose.
API GL-4, SAE 90 · J30 3-speed 1.7 L · H41 4-speed 3.1 L A swapped-in H55F five-speed takes 4.9 L (60/70-series table) and needs its fifth-gear oiler.
API GL-4, SAE 90 · 1.7 L (2.1 L with PTO) A PTO winch also has its own gearbox: front winch GL-4 SAE 90, 600 cc.
API GL-5 hypoid 80W-90 · 2.5 L each · LSD oil for limited-slip Gear oil mixed into the knuckle grease points to failed inner axle seals.
Molybdenum-disulfide lithium-base grease, NLGI-2 Weeping at the wiper seals or a mix of grease and 90-weight inside means a knuckle rebuild.
Manual box: API GL-4 SAE 90, 600 cc · power steering (1979–84): ATF Dexron, 0.8 L total Top up the manual box through its fill plug; most play is in the box, center arm and tie-rod ends.
DOT 3 (SAE J1703) Bleed every corner and look for weeping wheel cylinders on drum-brake axles.
Chassis: moly lithium NLGI-2 · driveshafts & wheel bearings: lithium multipurpose NLGI-2 Grease the spring pins/shackles (greaseable pins if fitted), driveshaft U-joints and slip yokes.
Inline filter Do it before or with any carburetor rebuild.
V-belts and radiator hoses · gear-driven camshaft, so no timing belt The F-series engine drives its camshaft by gears, so there's no timing belt or chain to schedule.

FJ60 2F 4.2 I6 The first four-door wagon Land Cruiser for the US: carbureted 2F six, manual gearboxes, round headlights. The FJ60 is the Land Cruiser that learned to carry a family and a cooler without forgetting it was a truck. A carbureted 2F, a four-speed, leaf springs and round headlights make it slow, thirsty and wonderful, provided you can find one whose rear frame rails are still there.

Stumbling, hesitation, sputtering, rough running or stalling at low rpm. If it only runs with the choke off, suspect the EGR valve. Carb rebuild kit · vacuum hose · vacuum diagram · vacuum gauge · carb cleaner

t: Compression test before you buy or rebuild
x: Low power, blow-by or an unknown engine history on a truck past 200,000 miles. Compression gauge · spark-plug socket · remote starter switch

Grease sludge leaking from the steering knuckles where axle grease has got past the seals. Spring scale · seal driver · Cruiser Corps kit 595-102 or 514-109 · knuckle shim and gasket kit 595-101 · moly grease

Violent front-end shake after a bump, especially on lifted trucks; or a shake you feel in the truck but not the steering wheel. Impact wrench · Old Man Emu steering damper (OMESD24 in OME's 60 Series kits)
About 3,250 rpm at 75 mph in fourth gear. Transmission jack · 32 mm and 36 mm sockets · clutch alignment tool · clutch kit · gaskets · fifth-gear oiler
Coolant smell in the cabin, a damp passenger carpet, poor heat or unexplained coolant loss. Basic hand tools · coolant · Cruiser Corps 520-127 front heater core (8/1980–8/1987)
Sagging leaf springs, worn shocks or a nose-down stance. Jacks and stands · breaker bar · ARB/OME kit (pre- or post-4/1985) · grease gun

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: 33x9.50 fits on stock suspension; one IH8MUD member runs them on a stock 60 Series with 240,000 miles. 33x10.50 might fit, but 33x12.50s won't without a lift: an FJ60 with a 2.5-inch lift still rubbed its inner wheel wells at full lock. 31x10.50R15 is the common 'looks right at stock height' choice, though some shops won't mount it on the 6-inch-wide stock wheel.

The FJ60 (US 1981–87) has round headlights, the carbureted 4.2 L 2F and a four-speed manual. The FJ62 (1988–90) has fuel injection, an automatic, square headlights and a plusher cabin. Hagerty calls the FJ60 the more collectible. The FJ62 is easier to live with in traffic.

t: Did US FJ60s get a five-speed?
x: No. US trucks used the H42 four-speed. The H55F five-speed went into most other markets from around 1983, and swapping one in is direct on post-April-1985 US trucks.

t: What's the High Altitude Compensation system?
x: It's emissions equipment on 1981–87 trucks that adjusts the mixture above about 3,930 feet. A Weber carburetor bypasses it and costs performance, so Corsetti recommends keeping the factory carb.
Corsetti lists 3,500 lb.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Corsetti lists 11 mpg city and 18 highway with a 23.8-gallon tank. In practice, bigger tires and a roof rack make it worse.

t: How do I tell if the engine is tired?
x: Do a compression test. Corsetti's benchmarks for a 2F are about 160–165 psi when excellent, caution under 120 and walk away under 100, with no more than 10 percent spread. The 2F reportedly reaches 300,000 miles with care.

The classic setup is an Old Man Emu 2-inch kit with greaseable shackles and a steering damper. Kits are split by build date (before or after April 1985) and load rating. Corsetti fits an OME steering damper even on unlifted trucks.

t: Can I import a diesel HJ61?
x: None were sold new in the US, but the 25-year rule now covers every 60 Series. Silodrome calls the 12H-T-powered GX the most desirable 60. Check EPA and state registration rules before buying.

Hagerty's wagon-values piece put the median quote for 60 Series trucks at $18,500, with FJ60s the more collectible and demand overtaking Jeep Grand Wagoneers. Rust-free restored and restomod trucks sell for much more.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu FJ60 kit, 1980–1985 (via Cruiser Corps), Old Man Emu FJ60/62 kit, 1985–1990
x: New springs restore ride height and ride quality, and 2 inches makes 33s much easier to live with.

t: Five-Speed Swap — IH8MUD — H55F swap guide
x: The H55F's overdrive fifth cuts highway rpm by about 500 at 75 mph.

t: Knuckles & Steering — Cruiser Corps — knuckle rebuild kit (1979–1990), CruiserTeq (Cruiser Outfitters) — 60 Series
x: Fresh knuckle seals stop the sludge, and a good damper calms the front end.

t: Oem & Restoration Parts — Cruiser Corps — 60 Series, CruiserParts LLC
x: Weatherstrip, bumpers, heater cores and trim keep a 40-year-old wagon tight and dry.
For a modern drivetrain and interior in the FJ60 body, specialist shops build complete trucks.

2F: 8 L (≈8.5 qt) with filter · factory spec API SF (use a modern oil suited to a flat-tappet engine) Fill to the dipstick rather than the book figure; one IH8MUD 2F owner uses 8 qt with a filter change.
Paper element Check the air cleaner's vacuum hoses while the lid is off.
Plugs, cap, rotor & wires · gap [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Corsetti's first check for a stumbling FJ60 is a loose or broken vacuum hose or wiring connection, so do ignition and vacuum before the carb.
Adjustable rockers · clearances [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Like every F-series engine, the 2F wants periodic valve adjustments (Hagerty).
Ethylene-glycol coolant · 16.5 L Coolant smell or a damp passenger carpet points to the front heater core.
API GL-4/GL-5, SAE 90 · H41 4-speed 3.5 L · H55F 5-speed 4.9 L H55F swap guides call for the fifth-gear oiler to be fitted; confirm it's there.
API GL-4/GL-5, SAE 90 · 2.2 L (with H41/H55F) Check the front output seal for weeping.
API GL-5 hypoid 80W-90 · 3.0 L Fill to the bottom of the fill hole.
API GL-5 hypoid 80W-90 · 2.5 L · LSD oil for limited-slip
Molybdenum-disulfide lithium-base grease, NLGI-2 Corsetti's tell: grease sludge leaking from the knuckles where axle oil has got past the seals.
ATF Dexron / Dexron II · 0.81 L total (0.39 L reservoir only)
DOT 3 (SAE J1703) Bleed all four corners; inspect the rear hoses and hard lines.

Steering link ends: moly lithium NLGI-2 · driveshafts & wheel bearings: lithium multipurpose NLGI-2 A shake you feel in the truck but not the wheel is usually driveshaft balance or U-joints (Corsetti).
Inline fuel filter · V-belts · gear-driven camshaft, so no timing belt Corsetti says trucks past 200,000 miles will likely need a full set of vacuum hoses too.

FJ62 3F-E 4.0 I6 The 60 grows up: fuel-injected 3F-E, automatic gearbox, square headlights and the first push upmarket. The FJ62 is where the Land Cruiser put on a collared shirt: fuel injection, an automatic, square headlights and power everything, all on the same leaf-sprung frame that crossed the Outback. It is the easiest old Cruiser to drive every day, and one of the hardest to find without r
Rough or hunting idle, hesitation, or a hiss under the hood. Vacuum gauge · smoke tester or carb cleaner spray · vacuum diagram · hose and clamps

t: Diagnose oil leaks before pulling the transmission
x: Oil drips at the bellhousing or under the engine. Degreaser · torque wrench · valve cover gasket · UV dye (optional)
Grease sludge leaking from the steering knuckles. Spring scale · seal driver · Cruiser Corps kit 595-102 or 514-109 (to 1/1990) · knuckle shim and gasket kit 595-101 · moly grease
Sagging springs, worn shocks, or front-end shake after bumps. Jacks and stands · breaker bar · ARB-111 (medium load) or equivalent kit · grease gun
Fluid on the driver's-side axle and spring, low fluid, or a groaning pump. Line wrenches · Pitman arm puller (box removal) · power-steering fluid · drain pan

t: Rust repair at the rear wheel wells
x: Bubbling at the rear wheel arches, a patched-feeling inner well, or a mud flap that sits unevenly. Cut-off wheel · MIG welder · seam sealer · rust converter and cavity wax

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: On a stock FJ62, one IH8MUD member runs 33x9.50s with no problems. 33x10.50 might fit, but 33x12.50s won't without a lift. Many owners choose 31x10.50R15, which looks right at stock height or with about 2.5 inches of lift, though some shops won't mount it on the stock 15x6 wheel.

The FJ62 has fuel injection, 155 hp, an automatic and a plusher cabin, so it's easier to drive every day. The FJ60 has the carbureted 2F, a four-speed manual and round headlights. Hagerty calls the FJ60 the more collectible of the two.

t: Is the 3F-E the same engine as an early 80 Series?
x: Yes. IH8MUD members note the 3F-E was used only in the FJ62 and the 1991–92 FJ80, so parts and knowledge carry across.

t: Can I convert it to a manual?
x: Yes, with an H55F five-speed, but it's a big job. You'll need a manual bellhousing, flywheel, clutch, pedal and hydraulics, crossmember and floor modifications, shift linkage, driveshaft changes and some wiring.
Corsetti lists 3,500 lb, the same as the FJ60.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Corsetti lists 12 mpg city and 19 highway with a 23.8-gallon tank. Real-world numbers on bigger tires are lower.

t: Is a little oil leak normal?
x: On a truck this age, mostly yes. As one IH8MUD member put it, 'any '88 Cruiser is going to leak some oil, from somewhere.' Check the pan bolts and valve cover gasket before assuming it's the rear main seal.
The common setup is an Old Man Emu 2-inch kit for 4/1985–1/1990 trucks, in light, medium or heavy load ratings, with greaseable shackles and a steering damper.
The Japanese-market version introduced in 1987 with the 3F-E. Wikipedia says it let the Land Cruiser be sold in Japan as a passenger vehicle rather than a commercial one.
Hagerty's wagon-values piece put the median quote for 60 Series trucks at $18,500, with the FJ60 the more collectible. Restomod FJ62s from specialist shops sell for far more.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu FJ60/62 kit (via Cruiser Corps)
x: Fresh springs and shocks restore ride height and quality; 2 inches makes 33s easier to fit.

t: Manual Conversion — IH8MUD — H55F swap guide
x: An H55F five-speed swap for owners who want three pedals.

t: Knuckles & Driveline — Cruiser Corps — knuckle rebuild kit (1979–1990), CruiserTeq (Cruiser Outfitters) — 60 Series
x: Knuckle seals and bearings stop the sludge and keep the front end tight.

t: Oem & Restoration Parts — Cruiser Corps — 60 Series, CruiserParts LLC
x: Weatherstrip, liftgate struts, bumpers and trim keep the cabin dry and quiet.
Complete builds with modern drivetrains, interiors and suspension.

3F-E: 7.8 L with filter change (Toyota publications via IH8MUD); IH8MUD owners quote 8.2 qt as the official figure · viscosity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Fill to the dipstick, not a number: the oil cooler holds some oil, and IH8MUD owners report 7–8.5 qt depending on how fully it drained. Pre-filling the filter helps.
Paper element for 3F-E Check the rubber intake hose for cracks while the lid is off; an air leak after the meter can upset the EFI.

Plugs, wires, cap, rotor and PCV valve The F-series is an OHV engine (Wikipedia), so there is no timing belt to budget for. IH8MUD members start rough-idle hunts with a tune-up and a full set of vacuum hoses.

Ethylene-glycol coolant · 16.5 L (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Replace any hose that is hard or swollen, and check the upper thermostat housing and radiator for old repairs; overheating history matters on a big iron six.

Dexron II ATF · 5 L drain-and-refill, 15 L dry fill (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) A drain-and-refill only changes about a third of the fluid, so do two or three a few hundred miles apart on unknown fluid rather than a pressure flush. Drop the pan and change the strainer once.
API GL-4 or GL-5, SAE 90 · 2.1 L with the A440F (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Fill until it runs out of the fill hole, and remove the fill plug before the drain plug.
API GL-5 hypoid gear oil, SAE 80W-90 · 3.0 L (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Milky oil means water got in through the breather or seals, common after deep crossings.
API GL-5 hypoid gear oil, SAE 80W-90 · 2.5 L; LSD oil if fitted with a limited-slip (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Check the pinion seal and axle-end seals for weeps while you're under there.

Molybdenum-disulfide lithium-base grease, NLGI-2 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Grease weeping from the knuckle wipers is the classic 60-series leak (Corsetti). If the knuckle grease is runny, gear oil is getting past the inner axle seal.

Dexron or Dexron II ATF · 0.81 L total, 0.39 L reservoir only (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Check the box, pump and hoses for weeps at the same time; leaks often show on the driver's-side axle and spring.
DOT 3 / SAE J1703 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Old fluid in a 30-year-old system means sticky calipers and corroded lines; inspect the hard lines while bleeding.

Driveshafts: lithium-base NLGI-2 · steering link ends: moly lithium NLGI-2 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Grease the U-joints and slip yokes. Greaseable shackles and pins, like those in OME kits, need regular grease too.
EFI in-line filter for FJ62 An old filter starves the EFI and can mimic a rough-idle or vacuum problem.

J70 76 78 79 The heavy-duty workhorse — wagons, troop carriers and pickups — still built for Africa, Australia, Latin America and the Middle East, and back on sale in Japan since 2023. The 70 is the Land Cruiser Toyota forgot to stop building, and nobody who needs one has ever complained. Leaf springs, a part-time transfer case, manual hubs and a cabin with all the sound deadening of a grain silo:

t: Adjust or replace the front wheel bearings
x: A hum from the front that becomes a growl, then a howl, and gets louder with speed. With the wheel off the ground, there's play when you rock it at 12 and 6 o'clock. 54 mm hub socket · torque wrench · bearing grease · new tapered roller bearings and seals if replacing.

t: Stop dust getting past the airbox (1VD V8)
x: Red dust on the clean side of the filter, MAF sensor faults, limp mode in the middle of a dusty trip, or a noisy turbo. Screwdriver · torch · MAF cleaner · replacement seal or aftermarket airbox.

Wind noise that gets worse with age, whistling at town speeds, diesel fumes in traffic, and a dusty dash after a day on dirt roads. Trim tool · bulb-type door seal kit · adhesive if the kit calls for it.

t: Refill the manual gearbox with the right oil
x: Crunching shifts, especially between second and third. Drain and fill plug wrenches · fluid pump · GL-4 75W-90 gear oil.

t: Repair a cracked rear spring hanger
x: A clunk from the rear under heavy load, such as towing up a hill, and a wandering feel in corners if the crack has grown. Welder and grinder (or a fab shop) · bracing plates · GVM-rated springs.

t: Upgrade the clutch on a tuned V8
x: Revs climb while acceleration stays the same or drops off, the clutch bites only near the top of the pedal, and shifts start grinding. Transmission jack · clutch alignment tool · heavy-duty clutch kit.
Hard starting, slow charging of auxiliary batteries and charging warnings on the dash. Basic hand tools · low-pressure hose · uprated alternator if needed.
The cabin never gets cool on a hot day, and the back seat of a 79 dual-cab is miserable. Soft brush and hose · plug-in AC controller.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The IH8MUD consensus for a stock-height long-wheelbase 70 is 235/85R16, about 31.7 inches. 285/75R16 (33 inches) will go on, but on factory steel wheels it rubs on the inside at full lock unless you change wheel offset. On a short-wheelbase truck, one owner rates 255/85R16 as the biggest he'd run comfortably, and that's with a lift. Sagging old springs make everything rub sooner.

t: Can I buy one in the US?
x: Not new. Toyota never sold the 70 in the United States. Canada got a few BJ70s for the 1985–87 model years and, as of 2022, Canadian mining companies could still buy them. Americans import older trucks under the rule NHTSA set in 1989 exempting vehicles more than 25 years old.

Body and wheelbase. Since 1999, 78 is the long-wheelbase troop carrier and 79 the long-wheelbase pickup (single and, from 2012, dual cab); the 76 is the four-door wagon. Earlier, 70/71 were short wheelbase, 73/74 medium, 75 long, and 77 a semi-long wagon.

t: Which years and engines are best?
x: Unsealed 4X4 says many enthusiasts prefer the 2007–2016 V8s, which don't have a DPF, but that service history matters more than the year. For US imports, the age rule means older trucks, typically with the 1HZ, 2H, 3B or 13B-T diesels or the 3F and 1FZ petrol sixes.
Selectable front and rear lockers were factory options in some markets. Otherwise ARB Air Lockers and Harrop electric lockers are the common add-ons; one IH8MUD owner runs Harrop E-lockers in a BJ74.

Rarely. Most 70s are manual, but a four-speed auto was offered on a few versions: FJ73 (1985–1992), BJ74, HZJ73/77 (1990–1999) and HZJ74/76K (1999–2004). The 2.8 L four that arrived in 2023 came with a six-speed automatic.
Australian V8s got a diesel particulate filter from September 2016 to meet Euro 5. Earlier V8s don't have one. Unsealed recommends a good highway run every 1,000–2,000 km to let it regenerate.

t: Why are the rear wheels inboard of the fronts on V8 trucks?
x: To make room for the 1VD-FTV, Toyota fitted a wider front axle and frame in 2007, which left the front and rear tracks different. Superior Engineering's coil conversion is one of the aftermarket fixes Unsealed mentions for equalizing them.

In Australia, yes. V8 wagon and troop carrier production ended in September 2024, and the GXL pickups were the last V8s, shipping until late 2025. The 2.8 L four (201 hp, 332 lb-ft) replaced it, with an automatic or a five-speed manual.

Overall, yes, says Unsealed: a strong engine and a tough driveline, with many trucks running very high mileage. The known weak points are mostly about use and comfort: DPFs on late V8s, clutches on tuned trucks, gearbox synchros, front wheel bearings, dust past the airbox, leaky door seals, weak AC and frame cracks on overloaded pickups.

t: Leaf springs or coils up front?
x: Leaf springs up to the 1999 facelift, then coils with leading arms. The rear stayed on leaf springs.

t: Suspension & Gvm — Old Man Emu (ARB), Superior Engineering — coil conversions
x: Many 70s are either overloaded or riding on springs rated for loads they never carry. Matching the springs to the real load, or fitting a GVM upgrade, fixes ride and safety. A coil conversion is the expensive way to fix both ride and track width at once.
Factory lockers were only offered in some markets. Selectable air or electric lockers turn an open-diff 70 into a proper rock truck.

t: Seats & Sound Deadening — Black Duck seat covers, Carbuilders (sound deadening)
x: Unsealed's fix for the cabin: thicker seat covers (Black Duck's add about 20 mm of padding), or full replacement seats, plus sound-deadening mats.

t: Bumpers & Armor — Cruiser Outfitters — 70 Series front bumper, Cruiser Outfitters — 70 Series dual swing-out rear bumper
x: A winch bumper up front and a swing-out at the back are the standard build for a working or touring 70.
Raises the intake for water crossings and dusty roads, and pairs well with a properly sealed airbox on the V8.

t: Oem & Rebuild Parts — Cruiser Outfitters (CruiserTeq) — 70 Series, Cruiser Corps — 70 Series
x: For imported trucks in North America, specialist Land Cruiser parts houses are the easiest route to genuine and OEM-supplier parts.

1VD-FTV: ≈9.5 L with filter, SAE 5W-30 ACEA C2 (Roughtrax; its table mislabels the engine, so confirm) · 1HZ: 9.5 L with filter, API CD (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) On post-2016 DPF trucks a low-ash C-spec oil matters; don't fill one with old-school high-ash diesel oil.
Inspect the clean side of the filter Unsealed: the 1VD airbox seal lets dust past the filter, causing MAF faults and turbo wear. Dust on the clean side means fit a sealed aftermarket airbox now.
Diesel filter element; drain the separator Imported or outback-fuelled trucks may have seen dirty diesel; cheap insurance for injectors.

VDJ79: 14.8 L Toyota pink Super Long Life (Roughtrax) · 1HZ: 11.6 L ethylene-glycol with front/rear heaters (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Don't mix coolant types; check the radiator for packed dust and grass, since a blocked core also kills the AC.

GL-4 75W-90 (Unsealed) · VDJ79 2.7 L (Roughtrax) · 1HZ 4.9 L (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Unsealed: GL-5's extreme-pressure additives attack the brass synchros, so crunchy 2nd–3rd shifts can be the wrong oil.
VDJ79: 1.5 L, SAE 75W-90 GL-4/GL-5 (Roughtrax) · 1HZ: 2.2 L, SAE 90 GL-4/GL-5 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Part-time two-speed case; check for weeps at the output seals.
VDJ79 with diff lock: 2.8 L, 75W-85 GL-5 (Roughtrax) · 1HZ: 2.6 L, GL-5 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Check the breathers after any water crossing; milky oil means water got in.

VDJ79: 2.4 L, 75W-85 GL-5; LSD axles take Toyota-specific LSD oil (Roughtrax) · 1HZ: 2.5 L, GL-5 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) If the truck has a factory rear locker, test it on a low-traction surface.

Steering knuckles: moly-disulfide lithium grease NLGI-2 · wheel bearings: lithium multi-purpose NLGI-2 (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) Unsealed: the tapered-roller hubs often just need the 54 mm locknut nipped up and fresh grease, and owners do the swivels at the same time.
Dexron-II ATF on older 70s (Toyota publications via IH8MUD) · V8: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Check the box and hoses for weeps, and the drag link and tie-rod ends for play while you're there.
DOT 3 or 4, SAE J1703 (Roughtrax) A soft or high-biting clutch on a tuned V8 is the clutch itself (Unsealed), not the fluid; test it under load.
Propshaft U-joints: lithium-base NLGI-2 (Roughtrax) Unsealed says to check the rear spring hangers for cracks at every service, especially on utes that have been run over GVM.

t: Timing belt (1HZ and other belt-driven diesels)
x: The 1HZ drives its camshaft with a timing belt (Wikipedia) · interval [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Confirm whether your engine uses a belt before budgeting; kits with the water pump are available for the 1HZ.

Late-2016-on V8s have a DPF (Unsealed) Unsealed: short-trip DPF trucks clog. Rinse the low-mounted alternator with a low-pressure hose after muddy trips, and fit a DC-DC charger for big auxiliary batteries.

FJ80 FZJ80 HZJ80 HDJ80 Coil springs, full-time 4WD, solid axles at both ends and optional triple lockers — for many owners, the last 'real' Land Cruiser. The 80 is what happens when an engineering team is told to build a family wagon and quietly builds an expedition vehicle instead. Coil springs, solid axles, full-time four-wheel drive and, if you found the right one, three lockers — it is the las

Gear oil and grease caked on the outside of the knuckles, runny grease at the knuckle fill plug, wheel-bearing play or noise, or a seal that started weeping after the last service. 54 mm (2-1/8") hub socket · torque wrench to 100 ft-lb · brass drift · seal puller and driver · snap-ring pliers · 6–12 lb spring scale · Cruiser Outfitters FA9097 kit (Koyo knuckle bearings, NOK inner axle and hub seal

A coolant leak low on the driver's side of the engine, or an original-looking hose clamp on a high-mileage truck. Members warn a failure on the trail can leave you completely stranded, which is why many replace it before it fails. Basic hand tools · hose pick · coolant · new hose (owners report using Gates heater hose) and clamps; aftermarket bypass kits are also available.

Intermittent no-crank: you turn the key and get a click, or nothing, until the third or fourth try. 10, 12, 14, 17 and 19 mm spanners · 8 mm for the contact cover · starter contact set and plunger. The intake manifold does not need to come off.

t: Power-steering leak? Check the reservoir first
x: Power-steering fluid weeping around the top of the system. It's often blamed on hoses or the pump, but Unsealed 4X4 says the usual culprit is the rubber seals inside the reservoir. Basic hand tools · small pry tool and crimping pliers · replacement reservoir seals · power-steering fluid.

t: Rear axle seals and bearings (1991–92 semi-float)
x: Gear oil soaking the rear drum brake, cracked or contaminated shoes, and grabby rear brakes at low speed. Slide hammer or bearing puller · seal and bearing drivers · bearing 90365-47013 and seal 90311-47001 (as listed in the IH8MUD thread) · rear shoes and hardware · gear oil. Later full-float trucks use a different hub-and-seal procedure.

t: Diagnose coolant in the oil before tearing down
x: Milky oil, a dropping coolant level, coolant weeping where the head meets the block, or a radiator that's already been replaced. Compression and leak-down testers · cooling-system pressure tester · combustion-leak (block) tester · if needed, an OEM head gasket set and the service manual.

t: Reinforce the frame at the steering box
x: Cracks in the frame around the steering-box mounts, a loose-feeling steering box, or wandering steering on a truck with big tires. Welder and grinder (or a fab shop) · reinforcement plate · torque wrench.

t: Re-set the rear brake proportioning valve after a lift
x: Weak rear braking or a changed pedal feel after lifting the truck, because the load-sensing proportioning valve (LSPV) now reads the truck as lightly loaded. Wrenches · ruler or calipers · paint pen to mark the start point.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The safe answer from IH8MUD is 285/75R16, about 33 inches, which fits a stock 80 without drama. Owners also report 305/70R16 and 295/75R16 fitting, though wheel width and offset matter as much as the tire size. 35s 'fit, but rub like mad' on a stock truck. Christo Slee's advice is that 35s work with a 2-inch Old Man Emu lift, but you'll probably rub at full flex unless you lower the bump stops. St

t: FJ80 or FZJ80 — which should I buy?
x: For most people, the 1993–1997 FZJ80. Its 4.5 L 1FZ-FE makes 212 hp against the 3F-E's 155, it could be ordered with front and rear lockers, and ABS trucks got a full-float rear with disc brakes. The 1991–92 FJ80 is simpler and cheaper but slower, with a semi-float rear and drum brakes. Collectors like 1994: big engine, lockers, and the last of the TOYOTA-lettered grilles.

Factory electric front and rear lockers were an option on US trucks from 1993 to 1997; 1991–92 trucks didn't offer them. Every 80 has a center differential that can be locked. Retrofitting factory lockers means welding, the locker ECU, harnesses and new axle shafts, so Slee says ARB Air Lockers are usually the cheaper route.

t: Can I lock the center diff in high range on a 1993–97?
x: The center diff lock switch was standard on 1991–92 trucks and dropped in 1993, but the wiring stayed in the harness. Slee says adding the switch lets you lock the center diff in 4HI again.

Kelley Blue Book lists a 5,000 lb maximum for the 1997 model. IH8MUD members quoting the owner's manual cite 3,000 lb normally and 5,000 lb with the tow package. Don't tow from the four bolt holes in the rear crossmember: Slee notes they aren't rated for towing in the US, so use a frame-mounted receiver.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Not much. KBB lists the 1997 at 12 mpg city and 14 highway (13 combined) on a 25.1-gallon tank. Bigger tires, armor and a roof rack only make it worse.

t: Should I re-gear for bigger tires?
x: 1FZ-FE trucks came with 4.11 gears on stock 275/70R16 tires. Slee says to drop to 4.56, 4.88 or 5.29 if you go up in tire size, and suggests driving a truck with the setup you're considering first. Slee's own 4-inch, 35-inch-tire build uses 4.88s with ARB lockers.

The classic choice is an Old Man Emu kit of about 2 inches. Slee's own 4-inch kit, with coils, machined radius arms and an adjustable Panhard bar, is designed for up to 35-inch tires. Bigger lifts usually need extended brake lines (Metal Tech sells them for 3–6 inch lifts), adjustable rear links, and a proportioning-valve reset.

t: What fluids and capacities does it take?
x: Rough Trax 4x4's FZJ80 data lists 7.4 L of engine oil with the filter, 13 L of coolant, 1.4 L in the transfer case, 2.7–2.8 L in the front diff, about 3.0–3.25 L in the rear diff, and 6.0 L for an automatic drain-and-fill. Check against your service manual, since figures vary by market and equipment.

t: Is it reliable? What actually breaks?
x: It's a tough truck, but now it's a 30-year-old one. The usual list: head gaskets on the 1FZ-FE, leaking knuckle seals, wheel bearings, frame cracks around the steering box, worn starter contacts, the 'pesky heater hose,' power-steering leaks, power windows, fraying seat belts and cracked dashes. Pre-1993 brakes are notably weaker.

t: Is a Lexus LX 450 the same truck?
x: Mechanically, yes. The LX 450 (1996–97 US) is an FZJ80 with softer suspension, a plusher cabin, body cladding and its own grille and wheels, with the same 1FZ-FE engine.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), Slee Off-Road, Metal Tech 4x4 — 80 Series rear links
x: A 2–3 inch lift with fresh coils and shocks restores ride height lost to sag and armor, and clears 33s. Bigger lifts need correction parts such as adjustable links and longer brake lines.
Only some 1993–97 trucks got factory lockers. Air lockers are the usual way to add selectable lockers to an open-diff truck, and are cheaper than retrofitting the factory ones.

t: Armor: Sliders & Bumpers — Slee Off-Road — sliders, Slee Off-Road — front bumpers, Metal Tech 4x4
x: The factory running boards dent on the first rock, and the long rear overhang drags. Sliders, a winch bumper and a swing-out rear bumper are the standard build.
The stock intake is in the passenger front fender. A snorkel moves it to the roofline for water crossings and dust.

t: Storage & Sleeping — Slee Off-Road — drawer systems
x: Many owners pull the third row and fit drawers with a fridge slide. Add a bed extension and Slee's guide says you get a flat bed of roughly 180 × 145 cm.

t: Oem & Rebuild Parts — Cruiser Outfitters (CruiserTeq), Cruiser Corps
x: Knuckle kits, seals, bearings, steering and driveline parts in OEM or OEM-supplier quality, which is what keeps a 30-year-old 80 on the trail.

1FZ-FE: API SH grade, 7.4 L (≈7.8 qt) with filter · 3F-E: 7.8 L (≈8.2 qt) with filter Timmy the Toolman's FZJ80 service uses Toyota filter 90915-YZZD3 and drain-plug washer 90430-12031, with the drain plug at 20 ft-lb.
Paper panel element Cheap insurance on a truck with unknown history — a dirty element is one of the 'owner neglect' signs Slee tells buyers to look for.
FZJ80: Denso/OEM plugs · FJ80: NGK · gap [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Both engines are distributor-fired, so do cap, rotor and plug wires at the same time.

Ethylene-glycol Toyota coolant · FZJ80 13.4 L / FJ80 19.5 L (with front & rear heaters) Timmy the Toolman refills with Toyota Red and lists thermostat 90916-03117 and gasket 16346-66020 for the FZJ80. Slee says to check the overflow bottle for deposits and look for a replaced radiator as overheating clues. Inspect the PHH while it's drained.

ATF Dexron II spec (Dexron III / Valvoline MaxLife used as backward-compatible substitutes) · FJ80: ≈6 L drain-and-refill, 15.4 L dry A pan drain only replaces a fraction of the fluid. FZJ80 drain-and-refill quantity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]; Timmy the Toolman buys three gallons for a full cooler-line flush and torques the drain plug (gasket 12157-10010) to 20 ft-lb. Avoid a pressure-machine flush on a

API GL-4/GL-5 SAE 75W-90 · 1.7 L (HF2AV) / 1.3 L (HF2A) The fill plug is the 24 mm plug at about 8 o'clock looking from the rear (IH8MUD). Drain/fill plugs 27 ft-lb, gasket 90430-18008 (Timmy the Toolman).

API GL-5 hypoid 80W-90 · 2.8 L listed — fill to the bottom of the fill hole Owners on IH8MUD report a locking front diff drains close to 4 qt and takes about 3.75 qt, more than the book figure, so buy extra. Drain/fill plugs 36 ft-lb (Timmy the Toolman). Milky or very high oil can mean water or knuckle-seal trouble.

API GL-5 hypoid 80W-90 · 3.25 L (FZJ80); FJ80 table lists 2.8 L · LSD oil if limited-slip Factory-locker trucks: if the locker won't engage, Slee's guide points to an actuator rebuild rather than the diff itself. Semi-float 1991–92 axles leak gear oil onto the brakes when the outer seals go.

Molybdenum-disulfide lithium-base grease, NLGI-2 Slee's check: pull the square knuckle fill plug and sample the grease. Runny grease means diff oil is getting past the inner axle seal, and caked grease outside the knuckle means the seals failed long ago — plan a full knuckle rebuild.
ATF Dexron II · 0.75 L total (FJ80 table) If it's weeping at the top, Unsealed 4X4 says the reservoir's internal seals are the usual culprit before hoses or the pump.
DOT 3 (SAE J1703 / FMVSS 116) Re-check the rear LSPV setting if the truck has been lifted (see the repair above).
Lithium-base multipurpose grease, NLGI-2 Grease the U-joints and slip yokes and check them for play.
Toyota canister filter Different filters for 1991–92 FJ80 and 1993–97 FZJ80.

Accessory belts and coolant hoses · the 1FZ-FE uses a timing chain, not a belt Replace the PHH and the bypass hose next to it while you're there; IH8MUD notes the OEM replacement (99556-30100) is just cut-to-fit 16 mm heater hose, so use the best hose you can find.

UZJ100 FZJ105 HZJ105 HDJ100 The big wagon goes upmarket: V8 power (and, for the US, independent front suspension) and the basis for the Lexus LX 470. The 100 is the Land Cruiser that went to finishing school: a V8, independent front suspension and a cabin you could take to the opera. The purists sulked, and it turned out to be one of the most durable big wagons on the trail. Budget for the timing

t: Timing belt, water pump and thermostat (the 90k service)
x: No symptoms until it breaks. It's on the service schedule at 90,000 miles, so a truck without receipts is due. 3/4-in drive breaker bar and cheater · crank-holding tool · pulley puller · seal puller · thread locker · FIPG gasket maker. IH8MUD parts list (check fitment for your year): water pump 16100-59275-83, timing belt 13568-09070, serpentine belt 90916-02586, thermostat 90916-03100 + gasket 16
None until a brittle tee cracks and you lose coolant, possibly a long way from home. Step stool · pliers · flat screwdriver · soapy water · Toyota pipe tee 87248-60460 (x2).

t: Press in new lower ball joints
x: Clunks over bumps, play at the bottom of the knuckle, or simply a high-mileage truck with original joints. 20-ton shop press · 22, 19, 14 and 24 mm sockets · snap-ring pliers · sledge or pickle fork · lower ball joint (e.g. Cruiser Outfitters SUS43340) · factory manual section SA-73.

The solenoid clicks but the starter doesn't turn, usually on a cold start, then it fires after two or three tries. 10, 12 and 14 mm wrenches and sockets · camera for reference photos · starter contact and plunger kit · new intake gaskets.

Old, dark fluid, a truck that's slow to level, or a lift via the height-sensor links that has left the reservoir low. 10 mm wrench · clear tube and catch bottle · fluid extractor or turkey baster · Toyota AHC fluid.

t: Check spark plugs for walking out
x: A tick-tick or pop-pop at cold start that sounds like an exhaust leak and, as the plug loosens, doesn't go away when warm. Premature coil-boot and coil failures. Spark-plug socket and extension · torque wrench (inch-pound range) · dielectric grease for the coil boots.

t: Set the front ride height at the torsion bars
x: A front end that has settled or sits lower than the rear, or new tires that need more clearance. Socket and long extension · tape measure · anti-seize · Old Man Emu torsion bars (303001) and rear coils (2865) if upgrading.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The 100-series FAQ answer on IH8MUD is 285/75R16 on 16-inch wheels or 285/65R18 on 18s, both about 33 inches. 295/75R16s do fit, with half an inch to an inch of clearance at full turn, but owners call it tight. Even 285/75s can be snug at the rear: one owner measured 3/4 inch to the plastic wheel-well liner.

Every 100 has a center differential you can lock. A rear electric locker was a factory option only for 1998 and 1999. From 2000 Toyota relied on A-TRAC traction control instead, so ARB Air Lockers are the usual retrofit.

t: What's the deal with the 1998–99 front differential?
x: Those years have a two-pinion front diff, and Wikipedia says the pinion could flex away from the ring gear under shock loads. Most reported failures are on 1998–99 trucks. Toyota fitted a four-pinion diff from the 2000 model year, and failures dropped.

t: When is the timing belt due?
x: At the 90,000-mile service. Owners replace the belt, water pump, thermostat and often the idlers, tensioner and cam and crank seals at the same time. IH8MUD has a full parts list and several step-by-step write-ups.

It depends what you want. 2003 and later trucks have the five-speed A750F, stronger driveshafts and 4.10 gears, and late trucks have the 275-hp VVT-i engine. 1998–99 trucks are the only ones with the optional rear locker, but they also have the weaker front diff and, Slee notes, throttle-sensor faults that can stop the truck responding to the pedal.
Kelley Blue Book lists 6,500 lb for 2002–2006 models (5,500 lb for a 1999). From 2003 a bolt-on factory hitch was offered, and the rear crossmember was changed to take it.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: KBB lists 12 mpg city and 15–16 highway, with a 25.4-gallon tank on a 2005. Lifts, 33s and a roof rack make that worse.

The LX 470 had Active Height Control and adaptive damping as standard from 1998, and it became a Land Cruiser option late in the run. It works well when maintained. Keep up with fluid flushes (owners cite 60,000 miles), and to lift an AHC truck you can adjust the height-sensor links, as IH8MUD's FAQ covers.

Yes, the 105 (FZJ105 and HZJ105), with coil-sprung solid axles at both ends and straight sixes carried over from the 80. It was never sold in the US; it went to Africa, Australia, Russia and South America.

t: Is the Lexus LX 470 the same truck?
x: Mechanically, yes: same chassis and drivetrain. The LX 470 adds body cladding, a plusher cabin and standard AHC with adaptive damping. Slee notes that it often got features before the Land Cruiser did.

The common setup is Old Man Emu: uprated torsion bars up front, matching coils at the rear and new shocks, sold as a kit of about 1.5 inches. The torsion-bar adjusters handle front height. IH8MUD's FAQ also links a thread on Slee's front diff drop, and any height change needs an alignment.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), Cruiser Outfitters — OME 100 Series kit with torsion bars, Slee Off-Road — suspension
x: Fresh torsion bars, coils and shocks undo years of sag and clear 33s. Getting the front and rear heights to match the truck's load is most of the job.

t: Rock Sliders & Armor — Metal Tech 4x4 — 100 Series sliders, Slee Off-Road — sliders, Slee Off-Road — front bumpers
x: The factory running boards bend on the first rock, and the IFS front end appreciates a skid plate.
Only 1998–99 trucks offered a factory rear locker. Air lockers add front and rear lockers to the rest.
The stock intake is in the passenger front fender. Slee notes that on US trucks the power antenna has to be swapped for a whip antenna to fit a snorkel.

t: Storage & Sleeping — Slee Off-Road — drawer systems
x: Pull the third row, fit drawers with a fridge slide and add a bed extension: the same recipe as the 80.

t: Oem & Rebuild Parts — Cruiser Outfitters (CruiserTeq) — 100 Series, Cruiser Corps — 100 Series
x: Timing-belt kits, ball joints, wheel bearings and suspension in OEM or OEM-supplier quality.

SAE 5W-30 · ≈6.8 L with filter (Roughtrax); Amsoil lists 7.2 qt for 2005–07 VVT-i trucks The IH8MUD 90k list gives the dealer filter as 90915-YZZD3 and says a larger JDM filter (90915-20004) is available and preferred by some owners.
Air filter 17801-50040 (IH8MUD 90k list) The cabin filter is easy to forget; IH8MUD's 100-series FAQ links an LX 470/Land Cruiser cabin-filter DIY.
Iridium 90080-91180 ×8 · factory torque 13 ft-lb (IH8MUD) While the coils are out, check every plug for tightness: a tick or pop at cold start can be a plug walking out of the head.

t: Timing belt, tensioner, idlers & water pump
x: Belt 13568-09070 · tensioner 13540-50030 · idlers 13503-0F010 / 13505-0F010 · pump 16100-59275-83 (IH8MUD 90k list) Do the thermostat (90916-03100), cam seals and crank seal while you're in there. IH8MUD members say the cam seals are more work on the 2005–07 VVT-i engine.

≈15 L (Roughtrax). 1998–2003: Toyota red Long Life Coolant · 2004–07: pink Super Long Life Coolant, premixed (Slee) Replace the plastic heater-hose tees (87248-60460) preventively; IH8MUD says they go brittle and can dump the coolant. Radiator hoses 16571-50150 / 16572-50150 and the bypass hose are worth doing with the timing belt.
Serpentine belt 90916-02586 · belt tensioner 16620-0W101 (IH8MUD 90k list) The serpentine belt comes off for the timing belt anyway, so replace it and spin-check the idler and tensioner.

A343F (1998–2002): Toyota T-IV, ≈2.0 L per drain-and-fill · A750F (2003–07): ≈3.0 L per drain-and-fill, ≈10.6 L dry; ATF WS on trucks without a dipstick (Roughtrax) Slee: from 2004 the dipstick was deleted (level is set at the overflow plug) and ATF WS is not interchangeable with T-IV or Dexron. A drain-and-fill only swaps the sump portion, so repeat it rather than doing one big flush on unknown f

GL-5 75W-90 · 1.4 qt (IH8MUD DIY); Roughtrax lists 1.5 L HF2A full-time case, no viscous coupler (Slee). Crack the 24 mm fill plug before the drain, torque the drain plug to 27 ft-lb and don't overtighten: the case can crack. Synthetic can quiet cold-morning whine.

GL-5 80W-90 hypoid · 1.8 qt (IH8MUD write-up); Roughtrax lists 1.6 L The IFS front diff has Allen-head plugs and too little clearance for squeeze bottles, so bring a pump. Two-pinion on 1998–99, four-pinion from 2000 (Slee).

GL-5 80W-90 hypoid (LSD-rated per the write-up) · 3.5 qt (IH8MUD); Roughtrax lists 3.2 L, 3.3 L for LSD 9.5-inch ring gear. 1998–99 trucks could have the optional electric rear locker, so test that it engages (Slee).
Dexron-III ATF (Amsoil lookup) · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Rack-and-pinion IFS; Slee notes variable-gear steering arrived later in the run.

DOT 3 (Amsoil lookup; Roughtrax allows DOT 3 or 4) The 100 has a hydraulic brake booster with an electric pump: bleed with the key on and expect the pump to run. IH8MUD members bleed all four corners, cycle the ABS on dirt, then bleed again.

Toyota AHC fluid 08886-01805 (2.5 L can) · ≈4.5 L system, forum estimate (Roughtrax) Never top up with brake fluid; one IH8MUD owner's truck went soft after a dealer did. Bleed each corner with the engine off and the suspension in N.
Lithium-base NLGI No. 2 for the U-joints (Roughtrax) IH8MUD's FAQ links a driveshaft lubing schematic; any hand grease gun fits the zerks.

UZJ200 VDJ200 The V8 flagship and the last full-size Land Cruiser wagon sold in North America before Toyota pulled it after 2021. The 200 is a nearly three-ton bank vault with a 5.7-liter V8 and a crawl-control button, and it is far better in the dirt than anything with a heated steering wheel has any right to be. It was also the last of its kind in America: when it left after 2021, the big V8 Lan

Dried pink coolant trailing down the front of the engine from the water-pump weep hole, and a slowly dropping coolant level. Basic metric sockets · belt tool · coolant catch tub · Aisin water pump and gasket · Toyota long-life coolant · fan bracket if contaminated.

A check-engine light, often with the slip light flashing and 'Check VSC' on, that may come and go, especially in cold or damp weather. Codes such as P2438 (pressure sensor circuit high, bank 2). Owners on Tundra sites also report P2440–P2443. OBD-II scanner with Toyota enhanced codes · multimeter · factory wiring diagram.

t: Close the KDSS valves after suspension work
x: Alarming body roll on uneven roads, or a truck that feels wrong right after a lift or shock install. 5 mm hex key · wheel chocks · torch.
A clunk when you come to a stop, as if you'd nudged the car ahead, and another clunk when you pull away. Grease gun with a needle or angled coupler · quality chassis grease · creeper.

t: Swap to an aluminum oil filter cap
x: A plastic cap that rounds off, lets the wrench slip, warps or cracks after many heat cycles. Flat screwdriver · cap-type filter wrench · aluminum cap 15620-31060 (as listed in the IH8MUD thread).

t: Add rear air helper springs for towing
x: Almost 4 inches of sag at the hitch with a 5,000 lb trailer and about 600 lb of tongue weight, even with weight distribution set up. Jack stands · long pry bar · Firestone 4164 air-bag kit · Air Lift 25804 compressor · Air Lift 21838 union tee · RTV · zip ties · marine grease.
Red dust on the clean side of the filter, MAF faults, limp mode and, in bad cases, a failed right-hand turbo. Screwdriver · torch · MAF cleaner · grease or an aftermarket airbox.

Rough idle, smoke, poor fuel economy, sludge in the intake and DPF trouble, often caused by leaking injector seat washers. Workshop manual · injector puller · new injectors and updated washers (all eight) · a diagnostic tool to code the injectors.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: On IH8MUD, 285/65R18 'will fit fine with zero rubbing' on a stock truck, and 285/70R18 'will rub a bit but should be manageable', One owner running 285/70R17s on aftermarket wheels reported light rubbing on the plastic liner, which he fixed with a heat gun. 275/70s are described as 'tried and true'. For anything bigger, check the forum's 200 Series Tire and Wheel Size Database.

KBB lists 8,500 lb for 2008, 8,200 lb for 2015 and 8,100 lb for 2016–2021. An IH8MUD owner with a 2013 quotes 8,500 lb with an 850 lb maximum tongue weight. Weight distribution helps the short 112-inch wheelbase, and rear air helpers fix sag.

2008–2015 trucks have the AB60F six-speed with 3.90 gears. 2016–2021 trucks have the AE80F eight-speed with 3.30 gears and bigger front brakes. If you plan big tires on an eight-speed truck, re-gearing (Nitro's 4.88s are a common choice) restores the lost low-end response.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: KBB lists 13 mpg city and 18 highway (15 combined) for most years, and 13/17 for 2021, on a 24.6-gallon tank. It needs regular unleaded, not premium.

US trucks have full-time four-wheel drive with a lockable center differential, plus A-TRAC, CRAWL and (from 2013) Multi-Terrain Select. Front and rear lockers are aftermarket; ARB Air Lockers and Harrop E-lockers are both common in IH8MUD build signatures.

t: What is KDSS, and does it complicate a lift?
x: The Kinetic Dynamic Suspension System lets the wheels articulate more off-road while controlling body roll on the road. It complicates lifts a little: the KDSS valves are opened during suspension work and must be closed afterward. IH8MUD has a warning thread from an owner whose shop left them open.

t: Was there a diesel in the US?
x: No. North America only ever got the 5.7-liter 3UR-FE petrol V8. The 4.5-liter twin-turbo 1VD-FTV diesel was sold in Australia, Europe, the Middle East and elsewhere.

On US 3UR trucks: water pumps around 100,000 miles, secondary air-injection faults, plastic oil filter caps and dry U-joints. On diesels: injectors, the DPF and EGR on 2015-on trucks, and dust past the airbox. Unsealed also notes some 200s have a vibration that owners argue about.

t: What's special about the Heritage Edition?
x: Built for 2020 and 2021 to mark 60 years since the FJ40: two rows of seats, black or white paint, bronze BBS forged wheels, a Yakima MegaWarrior basket, no running boards or side moldings, and a vintage Land Cruiser badge. Slee counts 1,202 for 2020.

t: Why did Toyota stop selling it in the US?
x: In December 2020 Toyota told Road & Track that the Land Cruiser would end in North America after 2021. The name came back in 2024 on the smaller 250 Series, and the 300 Series flagship isn't sold in the US.

t: Is the Lexus LX 570 the same truck?
x: It shares the platform and the 3UR-FE (Lexus rates it at 383 hp and 403 lb-ft), but the LX 570 adds standard AHC height control and adaptive damping, 20-inch wheels and a lot more leather.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), ICON Vehicle Dynamics, Slee Off-Road — suspension
x: A two- to three-inch lift with better shocks clears 285/70s and bigger. On KDSS trucks, close the valves afterward. Many IH8MUD builds pair a lift with aftermarket upper control arms.

t: Rock Sliders & Skids — Metal Tech 4x4 — 200 Series sliders, Slee Off-Road — sliders
x: The running boards are decoration. Sliders protect the rockers, and a full skid set protects the IFS, engine and transmission.

t: Gears & Lockers — Nitro Gear & Axle, ARB Air Locker, Harrop
x: Bigger tires dull the 3.30-geared eight-speed in particular. Re-gearing to 4.88 and adding selectable lockers is the classic 200 build.

t: Bumpers & Winch — Slee Off-Road — front bumpers
x: A winch-capable front bumper, plus a rear bumper with a tire carrier to free up cargo space.

t: Snorkel — Safari 4x4 Engineering, Slee Off-Road — snorkels
x: Raises the intake for water crossings and dust; IH8MUD's technical FAQ includes a Safari snorkel install. On diesels, pair it with a properly sealed airbox.

t: Oem & Rebuild Parts — Cruiser Outfitters (CruiserTeq) — 200 Series, Cruiser Corps — 200 Series
x: Water pumps, air-injection parts, filters and suspension in OEM or OEM-supplier quality.
SAE 0W-20 · ≈7.9 qt with filter · drain plug 30 ft-lb Cartridge filter under a plastic cap that's easy to round off. See the aluminum-cap swap above. Replace the cap O-ring with every change.
OE-type panel filter Check that the airbox lid seals and look for dust on the clean side.
OE-type

Toyota Genuine ATF WS · 8-speed AE80F ≈10.7 qt total fill There's no dipstick. The level is set at a specified fluid temperature through the overflow (check) plug. A drain-and-fill replaces only part of the fluid, so repeat it rather than pressure-flushing. 2008–2015 trucks use the 6-speed AB60F: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] for capacity.

Toyota Genuine Transfer Gear Oil LF, SAE 75W · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Use the 75W LF spec. One IH8MUD owner got a center-diff error after filling with 75W-90, and it went away when he went back to 75W. His first change at 60,000 mi came out almost black.
Toyota Genuine Differential Gear Oil LT 75W-85 GL-5 · front ≈4 pt, rear ≈8.9 pt Always crack the fill plug before draining. Fit new plug gaskets.
Lithium chassis grease at every U-joint and slip yoke Dry U-joints cause a clunk on stop and take-off. See the U-joint repair above.

DOT 3 (FMVSS 116)
Serpentine belt with automatic tensioner Replace the belt if you're doing the water pump and the fan is already off.
