J250 The Prado-based 'light-duty' Land Cruiser that brought the name back to the US: TNGA-F platform, 326-hp i-FORCE MAX hybrid, full-time 4WD with center and rear lockers standard. Toyota took the Land Cruiser away from America, thought about it for a few years, and brought back a Prado in a 1980s costume, which turns out to be exactly what most of us wanted. It's smaller, cheaper and boxier than

Scheduled service. Many owners also change the factory oil early, at around 1,000–1,500 miles. Socket set · drain pan · filter wrench · 0W-20 oil · OEM filter 90915-10009 (as reported by an owner) · new drain-plug gasket · optional Fumoto valve.
Scheduled service, or after deep water crossings or heavy towing. Socket set · fluid pump · drain pan · 75W-85 GL-5 gear oil · 75W transfer-case fluid · new plug gaskets.
Squealing from the front brakes when backing up, especially at low speed. Basic hand tools · brake grease · TSB anti-rattle springs (and pads/shims if following the full TSB).
A 'battery cooling fan maintenance' message, or a fan running louder than usual. Vacuum · trim tool if removing covers.

t: Keep the 12 V battery alive at camp
x: The truck won't go into Ready after the doors or hatch have been open for a while with the engine off. Battery tester · jump pack · battery monitor · 10 mm wrench.

Rubbing at full lock or compression after fitting tires over about 33 inches. Socket set · trim tools · heat gun · cutting tool · 17-inch or 18-inch wheels with the right offset (6x139.7, 95.1 mm bore, M14x1.5 lugs).

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Threepiece's fitment guide puts the no-modification limit at about 31.5 inches on the 1958 and 32.6 inches on the wider-wheeled grades. Owners go a bit bigger: 275/70R18s (about 33 inches) on stock 1958 wheels, and 285/70R18s (about 33.7 inches) on stock suspension, including one owner on 18x9 +40 wheels who reported no rubbing on gentle trails. An LT275/70R18 KO3 (33.2 inches) just fits in the sp

6,000 lb, according to Toyota, and the 1958 grade comes with a trailer brake controller. Owners note that a small engine doesn't give much engine braking, so on long grades use the transmission and low range rather than the service brakes alone.

t: What fuel economy and range should I expect?
x: The EPA rates it at 22 city, 25 highway and 23 combined. Car and Driver averaged 20 mpg, and Flexmotor saw about 21 off-road and 24 on the highway. The tank holds 17.9 gallons, which is why long-range tanks and jerry cans are popular.
Every US grade has a locking center differential and an electronic locking rear differential. There's no factory front locker. Slee's AT37 build added an ARB Air Locker up front.

t: Why only a four-cylinder hybrid? Can I get the diesel?
x: North America and China only get the 2.4-liter i-FORCE MAX hybrid. The 2.8-liter diesel, the 2.7 petrol and the non-hybrid 2.4 turbo are sold elsewhere. If you want a V6 on this platform in the US, the Lexus GX 550 has a 349-hp 3.4-liter twin-turbo.

t: Is it a 'real' Land Cruiser or just a Prado?
x: It's a Prado, and the Prado has always been a real Land Cruiser: ladder frame, live rear axle, full-time 4WD with low range. It shares the GA-F platform with the 300 Series, and its 112.2-inch wheelbase is the same figure the 80 Series introduced. It's smaller than the 200 Series it replaced in the US and seats two rows, not three.

t: Which grade should I buy for off-road use?
x: The 1958 is the cheapest way into center and rear lockers, but it doesn't offer the Stabilizer Disconnect Mechanism, which gives the front axle more articulation. The Land Cruiser grade (and the 2024 First Edition) can have SDM and comes on wider 265/70R18 tires. For 2027 the 1958 starts at $58,180 and the Land Cruiser at $64,255 (base MSRP).

t: What oil and fluids does it take?
x: 0W-20 engine oil (owners report about 5.9 quarts with the filter), 75W-85 GL-5 in the differentials according to the manual, and Toyota 75W 'LF' in the transfer case. Check the owner's manual for your truck's exact figures.

ICON sells 1.25–3 inch systems for the 250, Dobinsons offers a 2-inch kit, and Slee's dealer build used an ADS 2.5-inch system. Threepiece tested a 1.5-inch Tuff Country leveling kit with 285/70R17s and reported no rubbing.

t: Is the new raised air intake a snorkel?
x: No. The $980 factory raised intake offered for 2027 isn't watertight, so Motor1 notes it doesn't improve wading the way a sealed snorkel would. It helps with dust.

It's early days. Recalls so far are an instrument-cluster software update, a corrected load-capacity label, a rear-camera fix, and an interim fuel-pipe connector notice. Common owner complaints are front-brake squeal in reverse (fixed by a TSB), 12 V battery drain, and hybrid-battery fan warnings. The US 250 doesn't use the V35A V6 involved in the LX and Tundra bearing recalls.

t: Suspension Lift — ICON Vehicle Dynamics — LC250 1.25–3" systems, Dobinsons
x: A 1.25–3 inch lift with better dampers clears 33s easily and 35s with some trimming, and it handles the weight of armor and gear.

t: Armor: Sliders & Skids — Dissent Off-Road — LC250 step sliders, Addictive Desert Designs — 250 skid plate, C4 Fabrication — LC250 front skid, Slee Off-Road — sliders
x: The 250 is long and low between the axles. Frame-mounted sliders and a proper front skid protect the rockers and the radiator area.

t: Winch Bumper — Dissent Off-Road — LC250 modular winch bumper, Slee Off-Road — front bumpers
x: A winch bumper gives you recovery points and a place for a winch. Slee says its LC250 bumper keeps the Safety Sense sensors working (except front cross-traffic).
17.9 gallons is the 250's biggest limit for remote travel. The tank on Slee's AT37 build holds 29 gallons and has an integrated skid.
Center and rear lockers come standard. Adding a front locker gives you all three, which only the top 300 Series and LX trims get from the factory.

x: If you'd rather buy it done, Slee builds complete LC250s, from bolt-on dealer packages to the Arctic Trucks AT37 conversion.

VJA300 FJA300 GRJ300 The current global flagship, unveiled in June 2021 — and not sold in the US or Canada. This is the Land Cruiser the rest of the world gets and America has to admire from a distance. It's lighter, stiffer and quicker than the 200, and its engineers used a 30-year-old 80 Series as the benchmark. The only way to buy one in the US is with a Lexus badge on the front.

t: Transfer case and front diff fluid service
x: Scheduled service. One IH8MUD owner also reported less low-speed 'rocking' in traffic after changing the transfer-case fluid at 19,500 miles. Socket set · torque wrench · fluid pump · Toyota LF 75W (transfer) and the specified gear oil · new washers: copper for the front drain, flat for the transfer case, collapsible for the front fill and rear drain/fill (as identified by an owner) · grease gun.

t: Early oil change and oil analysis
x: A new or new-to-you V35A truck, especially one built before the recall fixes. Socket set · filter wrench · 0W-20 oil (owners report running 0W-20; check your manual) · oil-analysis kit.

Rough or erratic shifts on a truck with 'lifetime' fluid, or towing and hard off-road use. Socket set · fluid pump · scan tool (Techstream or similar) to read ATF temperature · Toyota WS or a WS-compatible fluid · service manual.
You press the hatch button, it beeps once as if it's going to close, then beeps twice and doesn't move. Trim tools · replacement pinch sensor (left or right as diagnosed).
A rattle at the bottom corner of the windshield. Shop vacuum · closed-cell foam strip.
Delayed or missing throttle response, or a clunk into first, when accelerating from a rolling stop. Owners say it's worse in Sport and Sport+ modes. None, or an OBD-II dongle with Carista.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: IH8MUD owners report 275/70R18 (about 33.3 inches) and 285/70R18 KO3s (about 33.7 inches) with no rubbing on stock suspension. One LX owner with 275/70R18s had no rub at any AHC height, at full lock, in drive or reverse. 295/70R18s on stock wheels have been reported on an LX 700h Overtrail, and Dissent Off-Road told a member that 35s on a +40 mm offset wheel fit with minimal to zero trimming.

t: Can I buy a 300 Series in the US?
x: Not new. It isn't sold in the US or Canada, and the 25-year import rule rules out bringing one in for decades. The Lexus LX 600 and LX 700h are the same truck under the skin and are sold in North America.

t: Why didn't Toyota sell it in America?
x: Wikipedia cites slow sales of the 200 Series and limited production capacity. The smaller 250 took over the Land Cruiser name in the US for 2024.

It depends on the market: a 3.4-liter twin-turbo petrol V6 (409 hp), a 3.3-liter twin-turbo diesel V6 (304 hp), a carried-over 4.0-liter V6 in some places, and since 2025 a 457-hp V6 hybrid. All but the 4.0 use a 10-speed automatic.

Every 300 has a lockable center differential. The GR Sport adds front and rear lockers. On the Lexus side, the LX 700h Overtrail has all three, and Wikipedia also lists a Japan-only LX 'Offroad' trim with three.

t: How much lighter is it than the 200?
x: About 200 kg (440 lb), thanks to the redesigned GA-F frame and laser-welded mixed-metal construction. The V6s are also lighter than the V8s they replaced and sit further back.

The US LX 600 shares the V35A with the Tundra, and both are covered by recalls 24V381 and 25V767 for machining debris that can ruin the main bearings. Later engines were built with improved processes or an improved main bearing, and some are still under investigation. Owners routinely do early oil changes and oil analysis.

t: What did Toyota use as the benchmark?
x: The 80 Series. Chief engineer Takami Yokoo said the 80 still had 'the best rough road performance of any Land Cruiser,' and the 300 keeps the wheelbase the 80 introduced.

t: How long was the waiting list?
x: In January 2022 Auto Bild reported Toyota Japan quoting waits of up to four years for new orders.
ANCAP's 2022 rating, aligned with Euro NCAP, scored 89% for adult occupants, 88% for child occupants, 81% for vulnerable road users and 77% for safety assist.

t: What fluids and capacities does it take?
x: From service data posted by an IH8MUD owner: transfer case 1.89 qt of Toyota LF 75W, front diff 1.23 qt. Owners also report using 0W-20 engine oil. Check your own service manual, since markets and drivetrains differ.

x: Skids and rock sliders are the first job on any 300 or LX that leaves the pavement. Make sure sliders match your suspension (AHC or not).

The extreme route to 37s: portal hubs lift the truck without touching the suspension geometry. IH8MUD has several LX builds on portals, and Slee runs one.
Standard 300s and LX 600s have only a center lock. Adding front and rear lockers matches a GR Sport or LX 700h Overtrail.

x: Owners pull the third row and fit drawers and a fridge slide for overland trips.

Lexus got into the off-road business the way a rich kid gets into punk rock: by borrowing a band that was already good. The first LX 450, which reached US buyers as a 1996 model, was almost entirely the J80 Land Cruiser with leather, wood and a new grille. Every LX since has been built on the Land Cruiser of its day, from the 100 Series-based LX 470 through the 200 Series-based LX 570 to today's 3

J80 FZJ80 1FZ-FE The first Lexus truck, a lightly disguised 80 Series Land Cruiser with a 215-hp 4.5-liter straight-six. Sold for two US model years only. An 80 Series Land Cruiser that went to the tailor and came back with cladding, softer springs and a $7,000 premium. Under the leather it still has solid axles at both ends, which is exactly why people want one.

t: Front knuckle rebuild and birfield repack
x: Grease and oil caked on the outside of the knuckle balls, runny grease at the knuckle fill plug, and diff oil migrating into the knuckles. Torque wrench · brass drift · 54 mm hub socket · seal puller · snap-ring pliers · spring scale · moly and MP grease · knuckle rebuild kit (Cruiser Corps SKU 595-106; bearings 595-184)

A coolant leak low on the driver's side of the engine, or a sudden loss of coolant that leaves you stranded. Old original clamps are a warning sign on their own. Hose pliers · long extensions · drain pan · coolant · replacement hose and constant-tension clamps, or a PHH bypass kit

Coolant loss, overheating, combustion gases in the coolant (confirm with a block test kit) and coolant weeping at the head-to-block joint. Full metric socket set · torque wrench · engine hoist (optional) · combustion leak tester · FSM · gasket set and FIPG
You want to lock the center differential in high range on snow, sand or washboard, but US trucks only lock it automatically in low range. Trim tools · screwdriver · CDL switch kit
A steady power-steering fluid leak that has been blamed on the hoses or the steering box. Flat screwdriver · pliers · replacement seals · ATF

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The stock size is 275/70R16. On a stock-height 80 Series or LX 450 with healthy springs, the usual answer is 285/75R16, about 33 in. Owners report it works, with some rubbing possible at full flex or full lock. Anything bigger starts rubbing. Slee's guide notes that 35s are possible with a 2-in Old Man Emu lift, but expect to rub when crawling unless you lower the bump stops.

A 1997 spec sheet lists a 2,268 kg (5,000 lb) maximum trailer weight. Slee warns that the four bolt holes in the black rear crossmember (covered by trim on the LX) aren't rated for towing in the US, so use a frame-mounted receiver hitch.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates both years at 12 mpg city, 14 highway and 13 combined on regular fuel. Bigger tires and a roof rack push that lower.

t: What fluids and capacities does it take?
x: According to AMSOIL's 1997 LX 450 lookup: engine oil 7.8 qt with filter (10W-30 above -18°C, 5W-30 below 10°C). Coolant 14.8 qt with the front heater only, or 15.9 qt with front and rear heaters. The A343F transmission takes 11.6 qt total. The transfer case takes 3.6 pt of GL-4 or GL-5 gear oil. The front diff takes 5.5 pt (with locker) or 5.9 pt (without) and the rear diff 7 pt, both GL-5 90-weig

Every LX 450 has a center differential that locks automatically in low range. Electric front and rear axle lockers were a factory option, and BaT listings describe triple-locked trucks. If yours has them there are locker controls on the dash. Test them in low range on a loose surface before you buy. For unlocked trucks Slee recommends ARB Air Lockers, which cost less than retrofitting the factory

t: Can I lock the center diff in high range?
x: Not from the factory. US trucks from 1993 on had the switch deleted but kept the wiring. A plug-in CDL switch (Slee TOY1002 for 1995–1997) adds high-range locking in under an hour.

t: How worried should I be about the head gasket?
x: Worried enough to budget for it, but not enough to panic. Expedition Portal regulars say 1995–1997 1FZ-FEs are the ones to watch, and that risk climbs past 150k and especially 200k miles, with overheating in hot climates as a trigger. A properly done gasket job with receipts adds about $1,500–$2,000 in value. Others note plenty of unreplaced gaskets go past 200k without trouble.

t: Should I regear for bigger tires?
x: The 1FZ-FE trucks come with 4.11 gears. Slee suggests regearing to 4.56, 4.88 or 5.29 when you go up in tire size. Opinions vary on the right ratio, so its advice is to drive a truck with the setup you're considering first.

t: What's the difference between an LX 450 and a 1996–1997 Land Cruiser?
x: Mechanically, very little. The LX has softer suspension, extra sound deadening, softer leather, auto climate control, a console subwoofer, body cladding, larger rear bumper corners and two-tone mud flaps. The LX mud flaps don't swap onto a Toyota. Parts and aftermarket kits for the FZJ80 fit both.

Old Man Emu coil-and-shock kits are the classic answer. Slee's guide mentions OME 2-in lifts with 35s, and owners run OME 850/864-series coils. Metal Tech 4x4 sells 1.5-in and 2-in front spacer plates, adjustable rear upper and offset lower links, sway-bar drop brackets and caster plates for the 80 Series and LX 450. If you lift the truck, readjust the load-sensing brake proportioning valve.

There are only two, and they're nearly the same. The 1996 and 1997 trucks both have the A343F, airbags and OBD-II. Buy the one with the best records, the healthiest knuckles and working lockers. Factory lockers add about $2,500 in value according to forum regulars, so a locked truck is worth the wait.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu, Metal Tech 4x4 (spacers, links, caster plates)
x: A mild lift with better shocks gets you on 33s without rubbing. Adjustable rear links and caster plates keep the geometry right as you go taller.
If the truck didn't come with factory lockers, air lockers are cheaper than retrofitting the electric ones, and the OEM switch and dash lights can be wired to run them.

t: Rock Sliders — Metal Tech 4x4 (80 Series / LX 450 sliders), Slee Off-Road
x: The cladding and running boards are fragile and the rocker panels are expensive. Frame-mounted sliders protect both and still work as a step.

t: Bumpers & Swing-Outs — Dissent Off-Road (LC80), Slee Off-Road
x: A real front bumper carries a winch and protects the radiator. A rear bumper with a swing-out carrier lifts a full-size spare off the ground.
The stock air intake is in the passenger front fender. A snorkel moves it to roof height for water crossings. Slee says to fit one for wading, not for the debated performance gains.

t: Maintenance Parts — Cruiser Corps (80 Series), Cruiser Outfitters / CruiserTeq (80 Series & LX 450)
x: At this age the knuckles, hoses and seals matter more than the accessories. Specialist shops stock kits by chassis.
10W-30 (above −18°C) or 5W-30 (below 10°C) · 7.8 qt with filter Drain plug torque is 18 ft-lb. An oil analysis on the first drain gives a useful head-gasket baseline. Look for coolant in the oil.
1FZ-FE panel element Check the intake hose and boot for cracks. IH8MUD regulars list a worn intake hose as a common 80 Series fault.

Denso OEM plugs [CONFIRM GAP IN MANUAL] The 1FZ-FE uses a distributor and plug wires, so replace the wires with the plugs on an unknown truck. Spark plug tube seals stop oil pooling in the plug wells.

Toyota red coolant · 14.8 qt (front heater) / 15.9 qt (front + rear heaters) Overheating is what kills 1FZ head gaskets. Expedition Portal regulars say to use Toyota red only and to check the water pump, fan clutch and thermostat. A replaced radiator or crud in the overflow bottle are clues to past overheating (Slee).
Rubber hoses under the intake, driver's side The PHH and the bypass hoses above it can strand you when they fail. Original clamps mean original hoses.
ATF [CONFIRM TYPE IN MANUAL] · 11.6 qt total fill A pan drain only replaces part of the 11.6 qt, so repeat the drain-and-fill a couple of times rather than pressure-flushing an old transmission.
GL-4 or GL-5 gear oil · 3.6 pt The center diff is viscous-coupled on these trucks. Note any binding or clunks in tight turns on pavement.

GL-5 90 (80W-90 below −18°C) · front 5.5 pt with locker / 5.9 pt without · rear 7 pt If the truck has factory lockers, test them in low range on a loose surface (Slee). Water in the gear oil means bad breathers or seals.

DEXRON-III ATF Persistent leaks are often the reservoir seals, not the box or the hoses (Unsealed 4X4).

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The IH8MUD 100 Series FAQ answer is 285/75R16 or 285/65R18, both about 33 in, with no lift. An owner with a stock '99 found 295/75R16 a tight fit that might not clear at full bump and full lock. Stock sizes were 16-in wheels to 2002 and 275/60R18 from 2003.

t: How much can an LX 470 tow?
x: 6,500 lb with the towing package.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates a 2002 truck (four-speed) at 12 city, 15 highway and 13 combined. Five-speed trucks are rated 12 city, 15–16 highway and 13 combined. All run on regular fuel.

t: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
x: A belt. The 2UZ-FE is due every 90k miles. Owners replace the water pump, idlers, tensioner and thermostat at the same time, and often the starter or its contacts too, since the intake is already half apart.

If it's healthy, yes. It gives you adjustable ground clearance a spring truck can't match, and a fluid flush is a one-hour job. Owners whose AHC failed have switched to conventional suspension instead. One IH8MUD member went to Old Man Emu 2.5-in heavy springs and called it much cheaper than replacing AHC sensors and actuators, which another member described as very expensive.

t: How do I lift an LX 470?
x: The cheapest way is to adjust the AHC height-sensor links. That gives about 2 in up front (2.5 in with a trimmed heim joint) and about 1.75 in at the rear, or more with an extended bracket. Keep at least 70 mm of front droop for CV boot life, add a diff drop and get an alignment. The other route is removing the AHC and fitting conventional torsion bars, springs and shocks.

US trucks have a lockable center differential, plus brake-based A-TRAC from 2000. A factory rear locker was only offered on Canadian LX 470s in 1998–1999. Aftermarket air lockers are the usual upgrade.

Forum regulars favor 2000 and later for the stronger 4-pinion front differential, and 2003 and later for the A750F five-speed, which one member says makes a big difference. The 2006–2007 trucks add VVT-i and more power. The 2003–2007 trucks should also have had the steering-shaft recall done.

t: What's different from a 100 Series Land Cruiser?
x: The LX has the same drivetrain but different styling and equipment. It had AHC and AVS standard from 1998 (the Land Cruiser only got AHC as an option in 2006), front and rear automatic climate control, a power tilt and telescoping column, projector lows and fogs, body cladding and its own gauges and wheels.

t: Are there recalls I should check?
x: Yes. The big one is the July 2010 recall of about 39,000 2003–2007 LX 470s, which replaced the steering-shaft snap ring and added a retainer. There was also a 2004 US recall that added a resistor to dim daytime running lights that were too bright. In Australia, front rotor bolts and a dash wiring harness were recalled too.

t: What's that tick from the engine?
x: It could be either of two common 2UZ problems. A cracked driver's-side exhaust manifold ticks when cold and fades as it warms. A spark plug working loose makes a similar sound and is far more dangerous, because it can blow out of the head. IH8MUD members recommend checking the plugs first.

x: Adjust the AHC sensors for a lift, refresh the fluid and globes, or convert to conventional springs. Whichever route you take, adjustable rear links keep the rear axle centered once the truck is lifted.

t: Rock Sliders — Metal Tech 4x4 (100 Series / LX 470 sliders), Slee Off-Road
x: The cladding and running boards are expensive to replace. Sliders that bolt to the frame protect the rockers and can still work as steps.

x: A modular front bumper protects the radiator and carries a winch, which matters on a truck this heavy. A rear bumper with swing-outs moves the spare up and out of the way.

x: The IFS front differential and the transfer case sit low and exposed.
The stock intake is in the passenger fender. On US-spec trucks Slee notes the power antenna has to be swapped for a whip antenna.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The stock size is 285/50R20. The practical limit is about 33 in, and even that meant moving the front fender liner forward about an inch on one IH8MUD member's LX. His 35x12.5R20 build needed the liner moved further, the sidestep return trimmed and the body mount reshaped, with spacers giving about +35 mm effective offset. The LX is easier to fit than a Land Cruiser because it doesn't have the KDS

t: How much can an LX 570 tow?
x: Up to 8,500 lb. The hitch receiver is built into the frame.

t: What fuel economy should I expect, and does it need premium?
x: Yes, the EPA lists premium fuel. The six-speed 2008 is rated 12 city, 18 highway and 14 combined. The eight-speed 2016 is rated 13 city, 18 highway and 15 combined.

The US LX 570 has a lockable Torsen center differential plus A-TRAC, Crawl Control and, from 2013, Multi-Terrain Select. It has no factory front or rear axle lockers. Owners who want them fit aftermarket units such as ARB Air Lockers.

t: Is the AHC going to bankrupt me?
x: Probably not, if you buy a healthy one. One long-time IH8MUD poster wrote that after ten years in service the LX 570's AHC had turned out to be well engineered, without the expected horror stories. But leaks at line junctions and actuators are expensive, so inspect the system carefully before you buy.

They share the same frame, V8, transmission and transfer case. The LX swaps coil springs and KDSS for AHC, adds more luxury equipment and 20-in wheels, and over time got its own styling, with unique front and rear ends from 2016. DrivingLine noted that used LX 570s were typically priced below comparable Land Cruisers.

The 2008–2010 trucks have the most radiator-crack reports, and owners say 2008s had water-pump issues. The 2013–2015 trucks add Multi-Terrain Select and Turn Assist. The 2016 and later trucks get the eight-speed and a new interior. There is no 2012 model year in the US.

t: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
x: A chain. The 3UR-FE is a chain-driven DOHC V8, so there's no 90k belt service like the LX 470's.
Not in the US. Production of the 2011 model ran late and the 2013 started early, so the 2012 model year was skipped.

t: What does Crawl Control actually do?
x: It works like an off-road cruise control. It controls throttle and brakes to hold a slow, steady speed over obstacles, forward or in reverse. From 2013 you can choose from five speeds, and Turn Assist brakes the inside rear wheel to tighten low-range turns.

t: Rock Sliders — Metal Tech 4x4 (LX 570 sliders), Slee Off-Road

t: Rear Links — Metal Tech 4x4 (200 Series / LX570 links)

US trucks came without axle lockers. Air lockers add front and rear locking without touching the AHC.

x: The factory size on 22s is 265/50R22, about 32 in. Owners on aftermarket 20s run 275/60R20 (about 33 in) and 285/55R20 without rubbing, and 275/70R18 fits on Toyota TRD 18-inch wheels. 285/50R22 on factory wheels needed cutting and spacers. Without a lift, plan on about 33 in.

t: Is my LX 600 part of the engine recall?
x: If it's a 2022–2024, possibly. Recall 24V-381 covered 3,524 LX 600s built from July 30, 2021 to November 25, 2022, with engine replacement as the remedy. Recall 25V-767 (Lexus 25LA07) covers 9,895 LXs built from February 26, 2022 to April 2, 2024. Check your VIN at lexus.com/recall or nhtsa.gov.

t: Is the LX 600 just a 300 Series Land Cruiser?
x: Underneath, yes: same GA-F platform and 112-in wheelbase. Toyota didn't sell the LC300 in North America, which made the LX 600 the US version.

There's a lockable center diff, but no US LX 600 has front or rear lockers. The F Sport gets a Torsen limited-slip rear. Triple locks came on Japan's LX Offroad grade and, in the US, on the LX 700h Overtrail.

t: How do I use 4L and the diff locks?
x: Owners say the center diff lock can be engaged while moving slowly in Drive. Shifting into 4L requires the truck to be stopped and in neutral. On trucks with axle lockers, the front and rear lockers need 4L and the center lock engaged first, at very low speed. If you switch off the engine in 4L, MTS won't come back on automatically.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: For 2027, Lexus lists the LX 600 at 17 mpg city, 22 highway and 19 combined.

t: How much lighter is it than the LX 570?
x: Lexus says 441 lb (200 kg) lighter, with a frame it calls 20 percent more rigid.
At normal ride height, 25° approach, 23° breakover and 20° departure. Lexus hasn't published figures for the Hi1 and Hi2 heights. Maximum wading depth is 700 mm (27.5 in).

t: Why does it clunk into first gear?
x: Owners report a clunk into first on rolling stops, and sometimes on 6–5 downshifts, in 2022–2024 LX 600s. There's no known fix. Gentle throttle while the transmission decides helps, and larger tires make it less noticeable. Owners say the LX 700h hybrid doesn't do it.

t: Should I buy one without AHC?
x: If you plan to lift it, maybe. Slee Off-Road's LX 600 build was a Premium custom-ordered without AHC so it could run Dobinsons suspension. AHC trucks keep the adjustable ride heights but limit your lift choices.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The stock size is 265/65R17. On a stock or nearly stock GX 470, the safe consensus is about 31.5 inches. Owners report 265/70R17 working with little or no rubbing (one reports a slight rub at full lock in reverse), and 255/75R17 with zero rubbing. Going to 33 inches (285/70R17, or the narrower 255/80R17) generally means a 2–3 in lift and some liner trimming.

t: How much can a GX 470 tow?
x: 2003 models are rated for 5,000 lb. Midway through the 2004 model year, Lexus fitted a stronger frame-bolted tubular hitch and raised the rating to 6,500 lb.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates it at 14 mpg city, 18 highway and 15 combined (2007), and it calls for premium fuel. Bigger tires typically cost owners another 1 to 1.5 mpg.

t: Is it a timing belt or a chain?
x: It's a belt. Toyota's interval for UZ V8s is 90,000 miles, and the belt drives the water pump, so most owners replace both together.

t: What fluids and capacities does it take?
x: Engine oil is 5W-30, about 6.6 qt with filter. The A750F 5-speed automatic uses Toyota WS fluid (about 11 qt total, roughly 3.2 qt on a drain-and-fill). The transfer case takes about 3 pints, the front diff about 3 pints and the rear diff about 6.6 pints, all GL-5 gear oil. Coolant is about 13.6 qt. Confirm against your owner's manual.

t: When should I lock the center diff?
x: Lock it whenever you're off pavement with loose traction. Many owners leave it locked for all trail driving, because it cuts down how much A-TRAC has to work on climbs. Unlock it for very tight turns on grippy surfaces and back on pavement. VSC is disabled while the center diff is locked.

t: Should I keep the rear air suspension?
x: It works well while healthy, and Expedition Portal's build kept it for load leveling. But aging bags leak where they fold over rusty perches, compressors wear out chasing those leaks, and a failure can leave you on the bump stops. Many owners convert to coils for well under the cost of new air parts.

t: How do I tell if a GX 470 has KDSS?
x: Watch for a momentary KDSS light when you turn the key, or look for the noticeably large front sway bar. It was optional from late in the 2004 model year. It helps both stability and articulation, but it complicates some armor installs.

2005 and later get the VVT-i engine (rated 270 hp, then restated as 263 hp from 2006). Trucks from mid-2004 on get the 6,500 lb hitch. 2008–2009 trucks have the facelift. In practice, condition beats model year: rust, timing-belt records, air suspension, steering rack and manifold matter more than the build date.

Common choices are Icon's 0–3.5 in systems (sold by Metal Tech 4x4), ToyTec kits, and Old Man Emu BP-51 coilovers, which Expedition Portal used. ARB doesn't list the GX as an approved application, so check warranty terms first. Pair any front lift with a rear coil conversion or an air spacer to level it.

On 17s, GXOR's database has 275/65R17 on stock suspension with only a slight liner rub at full turn. t: Is it a timing belt or chain?

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Wikipedia lists the EPA estimate at 17 mpg combined. It's a 5,100-plus-lb truck with a V8, so bigger tires and roof racks pull that down.

t: Which trims have rear air suspension?
x: The 2010–2013 Premium, and the 2014-on Luxury, which is the equivalent trim after the reshuffle. Those trucks also get AVS adaptive dampers. Lifting one means converting the rear to coils first.

t: Can I add Crawl Control or Multi-Terrain Select?
x: Yes, on 2010–2019 trucks of any trim, using factory switch panels and a zero-point calibration. Part numbers differ by year and by whether the truck still has AVS/RAHC. Retrofit details for 2020-on trucks are unknown.
Yes. KDSS is standard, so buy KDSS-specific front skids (ARB and ASFIR both make versions). Expect some lean after a rear coil conversion. Southern Style Offroad's kit includes spacers to correct it.

t: Which years should I buy or avoid?
x: 2010–2013 trucks have the air-pump issue (confirm the updated parts or warranty work) and the 38.1-ft turning circle. 2014-on trucks get the facelift but turn wider, at 41.4 ft. 2020-on Off-Road package trucks have Crawl Control, MTS and a transmission cooler from the factory. 2022–2023 trucks add CarPlay. Mechanically, Lexus changed little, so condition and records matter more than year.

t: What was the Consumer Reports 'Don't Buy' about?
x: In April 2010, the stability control was slow to catch a lift-off oversteer slide. Toyota recalled the trucks for a VSC software update, and Consumer Reports lifted the label on May 7, 2010.

The core drivetrain has a good reputation. The well-documented failures are leaks and accessories: water pumps, the coolant valley, the timing cover, early air pumps and, on some trucks, the cold-start P2714/P0761 shift fault. Budget for those, and a 200k-mile GX 460 is not unusual.

Often, yes. IH8MUD's build guide notes that 5th-gen 4Runner KDSS-compatible front skids and gas-tank skids usually swap over, and some 4th-gen V8 4Runner transmission and transfer-case skids have been used. Bumpers and body parts are GX-specific.

At launch, Lexus quoted up to 8,000 lb. Current Lexus specs list it by grade: 9,063 lb (Premium), 9,041 lb (Premium+), 7,844 lb (Luxury), 7,601 lb (Luxury+) and 9,096 lb (Overtrail).

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: The EPA rates it at 15 mpg city, 21 highway and 17 combined. Expedition Portal called the combined figure a surprise, even though it beats the GX 460.

t: Is my GX 550 part of the engine recall?
x: Possibly, if it's a 2024. Recall 25V-767 (Lexus 25LA07) covers 3,717 US-market 2024 GXs built between May 31, 2023 and April 10, 2024, for machining debris that can damage the engine. Check your VIN at lexus.com/recall or nhtsa.gov.

t: What does the Overtrail get that other grades don't?
x: An electronically locking rear differential, E-KDSS that disconnects the anti-roll bars, standard 33-inch A/T tires on 18s, and a wider body. Seven seats are listed only for the non-Overtrail grades.

It's full-time 4WD on every GX 550, with a Torsen limited-slip center differential that locks and splits torque 50:50. A two-speed transfer case gives you low range. Multi-Terrain Select offers Auto, Sand, Mud and Rock in low range, and Auto, Dirt, Sand, Mud and Deep Snow in high. Crawl Control works in low range at five speeds.

t: Is it a Land Cruiser underneath?
x: Yes. It shares the GA-F platform with the Land Cruiser Prado, sold in the US as the Land Cruiser 250, and with the LX 600. The GX was revealed first, on June 8, 2023.
Lexus quotes up to 26° approach, 24° breakover and 21° departure.
At launch, Lexus said a hybrid powertrain would come to the US later. US GX 550s use the 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6.

t: V6 or the old V8: which is stronger?
x: On paper, the V6. It makes 349 hp and 479 lb-ft, compared with 301 hp and 329 lb-ft from the GX 460's 4.6 V8. The V8's advantage is its long track record, while the V35A is still early in its story and has had recalls.

The 4Runner started life in 1983 as a Hilux pickup with a removable fibreglass top, sold in the US from the 1984½ model year. It has been body-on-frame ever since, through six generations, which in this segment makes it something close to a living fossil — and that is exactly why people buy it. The pickup DNA faded generation by generation: a steel body in 1989, an all-new Prado-shared chassis wit

N60 A Hilux pickup with a removable fibreglass lid — solid front axle until the 1986 switch to independent front suspension. A Hilux pickup with a removable fibreglass hat, a four-cylinder that refuses to die and — for 1984–85 only — a solid front axle. Slow, rusty, uncomfortable and utterly charming, which is exactly why the prices went up.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Owners' consensus is 31x10.50R15 — Toyota-4Runner.org members say 31s fit with no lift and you can get away without regearing. 33x12.50s on a stock truck rub the front valance, wheel-well corners and rear pinch weld; IH8MUD owners estimate about 1.5 in of lift (plus some trimming) for 33s, and say the 22R-E will want lower gears.

t: Which years have the solid front axle?
x: 1984 and 1985. Toyota switched to independent front suspension with a three-inch-wider track for 1986, so 1986–89 trucks are IFS. Solid-axle trucks are the off-roader's favourite; IFS trucks ride better on the road.

Most enthusiasts prefer the 22R-E four-cylinder — Hagerty says so, and Expedition Portal members advise skipping the V6. The 3.0 V6 (1988–89) has more power but carries the 3VZ-E's head-gasket reputation and is harder to work on; the 22R-E is slow but famously simple.

t: Can I take the roof off?
x: Yes. The rear fibreglass top is held on by 14 bolts, and a rear roll bar was standard. Owners note the open-top experience mostly benefits rear passengers — and that ageing tops are a common leak point.
Not in the US. Diesel engines were offered in Hilux pickups, but Wikipedia records that no diesel 4Runners were imported to the US.

The 22R-TE turbo four arrived for 1986 with 135 hp, mostly paired with the four-speed automatic in SR5s. It's much rarer than the 22R-E, and LC Engineering still sells dedicated 22R-TE short blocks and turbo parts.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Trail4Runner quotes stock ratings of 19 mpg city and 23 highway. Expect less with bigger tyres, a lift or an old, tired engine — and don't expect to be quick doing it.

t: Is a 1988–89 V6 covered by Toyota's head gasket campaign?
x: Not any more. An October 1996 Special Policy Adjustment extended head-gasket coverage for 1988–1994 V6 trucks; the later V06 campaign covered 1/90–10/94 production and expired on 24 September 2018. Today a blown 3VZ-E head gasket is on you.

Hagerty's write-up on rising 1984–89 values gave averages of $8,400 (#3 Good), $13,700 (#2 Excellent) and $21,100 (#1 Concours), and cited Bring a Trailer sales of $19,250 for a 100,000-mile 1984 SR5 and $17,500 for a 168,000-mile 1986 SR5. Expedition Portal members reckoned a maintained 22R-E truck under about 170,000 miles could still be found for under $5,000.

t: Should I solid-axle swap an IFS truck?
x: IH8MUD members are split. Some say the 1986–95 Toyota IFS is 'pretty stout' unless you rock-crawl hard; others who broke IFS shafts say to 'spend the money on a SAS and never look back'. Kits for 1979–85-style solid axles, long-travel IFS and stronger axles are all still sold.

Mechanical parts, yes — the 22R family is shared with Toyota pickups and LC Engineering runs a dedicated 1984–1989 4Runner catalogue. Body panels, floors and interior trim are the hard part; Hagerty notes reproduction seats and floors generally don't exist.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: 31s — IH8MUD members call 31s the right size for a stock 2nd gen, and Toyota-4Runner.org owners agree 31x10.50R15 fits without a lift or regear. A narrow 33x10.50R15 can be squeezed in with some pounding and trimming, but expect rubbing at the valance and pinch weld; about 1.5 in of lift is the usual recommendation for 33s.

t: Was my V6 covered by Toyota's head-gasket campaign?
x: Special Service Campaign V06 covered 3VZ-E trucks, 4Runners and T100s built from 1/90 to 10/94, replacing head gaskets regardless of whether they leaked. Completed trucks got a label on the left front door hinge post. The campaign expired on 24 September 2018, so any repair now is at your cost.

The V6 makes 150 hp and 180 lb-ft against the four's 116 hp and 139 lb-ft, which matters in a heavier four-door. The 22R-E is simpler, more durable and outside the head-gasket saga. Owners generally say a maintained 3VZ-E is fine — but it must never overheat.
Yes, built from 1989 to May 1993. US sales ended in August 1992 and Canada continued through 1993. They cost more than the four-door because of the US chicken tax, so they're rare.

t: How often does the timing belt need doing?
x: A 4Runners.com member recalls four years or 96,000 km (about 60,000 miles) as the typical interval for the 3VZ-E. Do the water pump at the same time and use a quality kit.

t: What fuel economy does it get?
x: Not much. Wikipedia lists an EPA city rating of 15 mpg for the V6 with the four-speed automatic, with observed testing at 14.28 mpg. Bigger tyres and a lift make it worse.

t: Does it have ABS or a locker?
x: Rear-wheel ABS was standard on the SR5 V6 from 1990 and four-wheel ABS was optional. There was no factory locker in the US — differentials were open, with a limited-slip only offered in Japan and Europe. Aftermarket lockers are the usual fix.

The common recipe is a 2 in lift: ToyTec sells a kit with rear coils for 1990–95 4Runners, Old Man Emu sells 2 in rear coils in standard and HD rates, and ball-joint spacers or torsion-bar adjustment lift the front. Total Chaos makes long-travel IFS kits for 1986–95 trucks if you want more.

t: Should I do a solid-axle swap?
x: Only if you need it. IH8MUD members describe the 1986–95 Toyota IFS as 'pretty stout' unless you rock-crawl hard; those who break IFS shafts tend to go solid axle. Long-travel IFS and SAS conversions can cost similar money.

t: Can I get a diesel one?
x: Not from a US dealer — US trucks were 22R-E or 3VZ-E only. Japan's Hilux Surf offered the 2L-TE, 3L and 1KZ-TE diesels, and every 2nd gen is now old enough for the US 25-year import exemption.
By modern standards, not very. Wikipedia lists a one-to-two-star frontal crash rating for the driver; side-impact door beams were only added for the 1994 and 1995 model years.

t: Spare-tire crossmember and frame rust repair
x: Flaking scale where crossmembers meet the frame, holes behind the rear axle, a spare carrier that won't release or sags. Welder · angle grinder · Rust Buster crossmember · rust paint · inhibitor spray

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The Toyota-4Runner.org consensus is 265/75R16 (roughly a 31.6-inch tire) on stock suspension. Some owners see rubbing at full compression off-road with wide, aggressive tread or wheel spacers; if you want zero drama, 265/70R16 or 265/70R17 are the conservative picks. Anything bigger is lift territory.

t: Does my 4Runner have the factory rear locker?
x: Only if it's a 1996–2000 4WD truck that was ordered with it — it was an option on Base, SR5 and Limited 4WD models, never standard, and it wasn't common. For 2001–02 the rear E-locker was dropped in favour of VSC, traction control and a centre diff lock.

t: How should I use the E-locker?
x: The owner's manual guidance quoted on the forums is to engage it only in 4Lo and keep speed below about 5 mph. It locks both rear wheels together, so it'll fight you in turns on high-traction surfaces — use it for the obstacle, then switch it off.

t: When does the timing belt need doing — and is the 3.4 an interference engine?
x: Plan on about every 90,000 miles, and do the water pump, thermostat and seals while you're in there. The 5VZ-FE is non-interference, so a broken belt shouldn't destroy valves, but it will leave you stranded.
Up to 5,000 lb when properly equipped — a big jump from the 3,500 lb of the previous generation. Owners on Expedition Portal report fuel economy dropping to roughly 11–13 mpg when towing.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: EPA ratings were around 17 city / 19 highway for the 1996 V6 and 16/19 for a 2002 SR5 4x4; owners typically report 16–18 mpg. The 18.5-gallon tank and a notoriously inaccurate fuel gauge mean range is modest, so carry a jerry can on long trips.

Per Toyota-Club's US-spec 180-series data: 5VZ-FE oil with filter 5.2 L (3RZ-FE 5.4 L); front diff 1.15 L of GL-5 80W-90; rear diff 2.45 L (2.75 L with diff lock) of GL-5 80W-90; transfer case 1.0–1.2 L of 75W-90; automatic transmission drain-and-fill about 2.0 L (4WD) of Dexron II/III.

t: Which years should I buy or avoid?
x: Forum favourites are 1999–2000 trucks, especially Limiteds or SR5s with the Multi-Mode case and E-locker. 1996–98 trucks are simpler and cheaper to fix. 2001–02 get VSC and traction control but lose the locker and manual, and owners grumble about the early VSC and the late automatic. Condition and rust matter far more than model year.

Most owners steer you toward the 3.4 V6: 183 hp and 217 lb-ft versus 150 hp and 177 lb-ft for the 2.7 four, for similar running costs. The four is a durable engine, but it'll struggle with big tires and a loaded roof rack.

The classic is an Old Man Emu kit of about 2–3 in, with ICON, Total Chaos and others offering springs, coilovers and control arms. As a lift grows, aftermarket upper control arms help restore alignment range; Total Chaos makes both UCAs and a bolt-on lower ball joint conversion for this truck.

t: How long will a 3rd gen last?
x: With maintenance, a long time. SlashGear notes it consistently ranked among the SUVs most likely to pass 250,000 miles, and 8020 Automotive puts a well-maintained 5VZ-FE at 300,000–400,000 miles. Frame rust and neglected ball joints usually kill these trucks before the engine does.

t: Steering — Total Chaos urethane rack bushing kit
x: Urethane rack bushings take the slop out of tired steering, especially on bigger tires.
183 hp feels thin with 32s and a loaded roof. Superchargers for the 5VZ-FE are the classic fix (premium fuel and extra upkeep included).

The 4Runner in a suit: Prado 120 bones, a third row, cushy X-REAS dampers and — for the only time in its life — a V8. Softer than the trail purists like, but a 4.7 V8 with a lockable Torsen centre diff still hits harder than anything wearing the badge since.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: 265/70R17 (about 31.6 in) is the size the GX 470 community — same chassis and fitment — says fits with no modification, and owners on both platforms report no rubbing on factory wheels. 255/75R17 may need a front fender-liner bolt repositioned. 285/70R17 (about 33 in) needs a body-mount chop and fender-liner work even with a small lift.

The V8 is the reason many buy a 4th gen: 268 hp and 315 lb-ft from 2005, full-time 4WD and up to 7,000 lb of 4WD towing. The V6 has a timing chain instead of a belt, part-time Multi-Mode 4WD and better EPA numbers (17/20 vs 15/19). The V8's air-injection pump and exhaust manifolds are its known expensive faults.
All 4WD trucks have a lockable Torsen centre differential. A factory rear locker only came on the 2009 Trail Edition, along with an A-TRAC switch and Bilstein dampers.

t: What is X-REAS, and should I keep it?
x: It links diagonally opposite shocks through hydraulic lines and a centre valve to reduce body roll. It was standard on the Sport Edition and optional on SR5 and Limited. It works, but the shocks are costly and replaced in pairs, so many owners swap to conventional shocks such as Bilstein 5100s when they wear out.
5,000 lb with the V6; 7,300 lb with a rear-drive V8 and 7,000 lb with a 4WD V8.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Wikipedia lists EPA estimates of 17 city / 20 highway for the V6 and 15/19 for the V8. A 4Runners.com owner reported 17–18 mpg combined and 18–19 on the highway from a stock 2003 V8 4WD over 12 years, less when towing.

t: What fluids do the diffs and transfer case take?
x: 75W-90 gear oil. A 4Runners.com write-up quoting the owner's manual gives roughly 1.5 qt for the front diff, 1.5 qt for the transfer case and 3.2 qt for the rear diff; fill each until it drips from the fill hole.

t: Why are my VSC and TRAC lights on?
x: Often nothing is broken: after a battery disconnect, alignment or sensor work the system can need a zero-point calibration, done on level ground with a paper clip across the diagnostic connector. If the lights stay on, scan for codes.
Not a safety recall. Toyota's ZE6 warranty enhancement covered cracked or sticky dashboards on 2003–2005 4Runners, but coverage was time-limited and has expired. A dash cover is the usual fix now.

t: Which years should I look for?
x: 2005-on trucks get the five-speed automatic on the V6 and the VVT-i V8; 2006-on have the refreshed styling and projector headlamps; 2008–09 add standard curtain airbags; and 2009 offers the Trail Edition with a rear locker. Condition, rust and maintenance history matter more than any model year.

t: Does it have a third row?
x: It can. A third-row seat became optional on SR5 and Limited from late 2003 (the 2004 model year), making the 4th gen the first 4Runner offered with seven seats.

N280 1GR-FE Fifteen model years on the J150 Prado/GX/FJ Cruiser platform with the 4.0 V6 — TRD Pro from 2015. Fifteen model years with the same V6, the same five-speed and roughly the same dashboard — and it sold better at the end than at the start. The most successful act of automotive stubbornness of the century.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Trail4R's short answer is 32 inches. Stock is 265/70R17 (31.6 in). A 275/70R17 or 255/75R17 (about 32.1 in) shouldn't rub; a 285/70R17 (32.7 in) is 'questionable' and may need a body-mount chop; 255/80R17 (33 in) and anything bigger needs a lift and trimming. Tire brand and wheel offset change the outcome.

t: Which trims have the rear locker?
x: The Trail (2010–2016) and its renamed successor, the TRD Off-Road (2017–2024), which pair the electric rear locker with Crawl Control and Multi-Terrain Select. SR5 and Limited owners who want one retrofit an aftermarket unit — Trail4R documents an Eaton E-Locker install in an SR5.

If you'll stay stock or near-stock, yes: owners praise the reduced body roll and slightly better articulation. If you plan a big lift or long travel, it's a complication — Trail4R puts the practical lift limit at about 3 inches and lists bracket, sway-bar and panhard fixes for lifted KDSS trucks. Leaking KDSS cylinders are an expensive repair.

SR5, Trail and TRD Off-Road 4x4s use a part-time two-speed transfer case with no centre differential, so 4H locks the front and rear driveshafts together. The Limited used full-time 4WD. All trucks have A-TRAC.
5,000 lb, per Car and Driver. The 6th gen raised that to 6,000.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: EPA-rated 16 city / 19 highway (17 combined) in later years. Car and Driver's 2022 TRD Pro averaged 15 mpg overall and 17 mpg on its 75-mph highway test, good for about 390 miles of highway range.

t: Does the 4.0 V6 have a timing belt?
x: No — the 1GR-FE uses a timing chain with no scheduled replacement interval, meant to last the life of the engine. The serpentine belt is the wear item: Toyota calls for inspection at 63,000 miles and every 18,000 thereafter.

Per Toyota-Club's N280 data: engine oil with filter 6.2 L (Trail4R refills with about 6.6 qt of 0W-20); ATF WS 10.7 L total; front diff 1.55 L (part-time) / 1.40 L (full-time); rear diff 2.70 L without locker / 2.65 L with; transfer case 1.00 L (part-time) / 1.40 L (full-time); coolant 10.5 L. Diff oil is Toyota LT 75W-85 GL-5.

t: Which years should I buy or avoid?
x: There's no bad engine year, so buy on condition. 2014+ gets the facelift and upgraded brake lines; 2020+ adds TSS-P safety tech and CarPlay. SlashGear singles out 2013–2016 for higher complaint and recall counts. Whatever the year, confirm the Takata airbag (2010–2016) and fuel pump (2018–2019) recalls are closed.

Trail4R's shortlist runs from Old Man Emu (2.5–3 in) and Bilstein 6112/5160 to Eibach, Falcon, OME BP-51, Dobinsons MRR, ICON, Fox and King. Beyond about 2.5–3 in, plan on aftermarket upper control arms and, on KDSS trucks, sway-bar and panhard corrections.

t: Why does my truck lean to the driver's side?
x: Toyota puts heavy items — battery, driveshafts, transfer case, fuel tank — on the driver's side, leaving that side typically ¼ to ¾ in lower. Trail4R fixed it with a thicker top spacer on the driver's-side coilover than on the passenger side.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: TRD Off-Road, TRD Pro and Trailhunter trucks already run 33-inch tires (265/70R18) from the factory. SR5 owners on 4Runner6G.com report 285/70R17 (about 33 in) on stock height without rubbing, though they argue about whether the stock 17×7 wheel is too narrow for that tire; one owner saw the tread balloon and moved to 8.5-in-wide wheels.

It's the only choice on the TRD Pro, Trailhunter and Platinum. Elsewhere, Car and Driver says the extra cost isn't worth it: the gas truck is lighter, keeps the optional third row and is rated 21–22 mpg combined against the hybrid's 23. The hybrid's real gain is torque — 465 lb-ft against 317.

t: Which trims have a locker and the sway-bar disconnect?
x: The electronic rear locker comes on the TRD Off-Road, TRD Pro and Trailhunter; other trims get a limited-slip rear differential. The disconnecting front anti-roll bar is standard on the TRD Pro and Trailhunter and optional on the TRD Off-Road.
No. Car and Driver confirms KDSS is gone, replaced by the electronic front bar disconnect, and Wikipedia notes that from 2025 KDSS is exclusive to Lexus.
6,000 lb, hybrid or not — 1,000 lb more than the 5th gen.

t: What fuel economy and range should I expect?
x: EPA: up to 20 city / 26 highway / 22 combined for the gas truck (21 combined in 4WD), 23 combined for the hybrid. Car and Driver's 4WD Limited returned 21 mpg on its 75-mph highway test; its Trailhunter averaged 17 mpg. Owners complain about range, with one reporting about 280 miles between fill-ups.

t: Is the transmission overheating issue real?
x: Car and Driver saw the eight-speed's temperatures approach the red zone after repeated acceleration runs, and some owners report warnings on long, slow off-road climbs. Owners' advice: use 4Lo at low speeds or hold a lower gear in S mode, and report it to Toyota if it happens.

t: What are the oil change and fluid intervals?
x: Oil and filter every 10,000 miles or 12 months, or 5,000 miles / 6 months if mostly on dirt or dusty roads; differential oil at 15,000-mile intervals under severe use. Owners cite 5.9 qt of engine oil, about 1.4 qt front and 5.9 qt rear diff oil (6.9 qt on the Trailhunter), and 1.2–1.5 qt in the transfer case.

t: Can I get a third row?
x: Only on the SR5 and non-hybrid Limited, and Car and Driver describes the rearmost seats as little more than floor-mounted jump seats. The hybrid's battery lives under the cargo floor, so no hybrid gets a third row.

t: What lift options are there yet?
x: The aftermarket moved quickly: leveling and lift kits from ReadyLift and TORQ, Total Chaos kits with King shocks, Dirt King coilovers, plus upper control arms from Total Chaos, Peak and Westcott. Forum members are still waiting for news of an OEM TRD lift.

t: Did it keep the roll-down rear window?
x: Yes. Motor1 reported the engineers almost lost it, and only kept it by trimming weight from each part of the mechanism.

x: Non-Trailhunter trims need sliders and a proper bumper before the rocks find the rockers.

Land Rover started in 1948 as a stopgap: Rover's chief designer Maurice Wilks proposed a light agricultural and utility vehicle, and the first prototype was skinned in Birmabright aluminium alloy because steel was rationed and aluminium wasn't. It was launched at the Amsterdam Motor Show that year, and the Series I, II, IIA and III that followed ran until 1985. In 1983 the One Ten arrived with coi

Series I Series II Series IIA Series III 88 109 Leaf springs, aluminium panels, selectable 4WD: the agricultural original that put the world's backcountry on wheels. A tractor that learned to do 55 mph, built from aluminium because steel was rationed, and still the vehicle that taught most of the world what a 4x4 is. Slow, loud, honest, and fixable with the tools in a farm shed.

Oil weeping past the swivel seal, pitted chrome on the swivel ball, wandering or heavy steering. Spring/fish scale, torque wrench, hub nut spanner · Rovers North RNA3181P swivel rebuild kit (IIA 1962–71 and Series III non-V8, one side, no ball) · 75-90 gear oil

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: 235/85R16 is the size most owners recommend: it's close to the factory-optional 7.50x16 and fits a stock 88 or 109 if you adjust the steering stops so the tyre clears the frame at full lock. 215/85R16 is a safer close fit. 265/75R16 on stock 5.5-inch rims rubbed about half to three-quarters of an inch on turns for one owner, and others think it's too wide. Use rims at least 5.5 inches wide for 7.5

t: What's the difference between a Series I, II, IIA and III?
x: Series I (1948–58) has flat sides and 80, 86/88 or 107/109-inch wheelbases. Series II (1958–61) brought the wider 'barrel side' body and the 2.25 petrol. Series IIA (1961–71) looks almost identical but added the 2.25 diesel and the 2.6 six, and late home-market IIAs have headlamps in the wings. Series III (1971–85) has a plastic grille, a plastic dash with instruments in front of the driver and an

t: Were Series Land Rovers sold new in the US?
x: Yes, but not many. Factory sales to North America ended in 1974. Only 811 of the long-wheelbase IIAs with the 2.6 six were NADA (North American Dollar Area) trucks, the only long-wheelbase models built for the US and Canada.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Owners on AULRO report roughly 14–17 mpg (imperial) for a 2.25 petrol in normal use, with a best of about 21 mpg at a steady 50 mph in a short-wheelbase truck. Loaded, hilly driving pulls it back toward 14. In US gallons, knock about a sixth off those figures.

Owners on the Rovers North forum put the comfortable cruise for a 2.25 petrol at 55–60 mph. With a Fairey overdrive, 60–65 on the flat is realistic. One owner advises 3,000–3,400 rpm for the four-cylinder petrol and warns that sitting at 4,000-plus wears engines out faster.

t: Why do Series rear half-shafts break?
x: Partly the design of the shafts and partly overloading in commercial use. Land Rover strengthened the axles and hubs in 1980 and increased the driveshaft spline count from 10 to 24 in 1982. Forum members say shafts usually break at the differential end, and worn drive flanges announce themselves with a clunk well before they strip.

t: Should I fit free-wheeling front hubs?
x: Rovers North advises against it on Series IIA/III swivels with the Railko bush: running the hubs unlocked stops the front driveline turning, which it says starves the swivel ball, Railko bush and front propshaft of lubrication. If you fit them anyway, lock them in regularly.

t: Petrol or diesel? Soft top or wagon?
x: On value, Hagerty found petrol trucks worth about 6% more than diesels and soft-tops about 2% more than wagons. In use, the 2.25 petrol is the more pleasant road engine; the early 2.0 and 2.25 diesels are slow even by Series standards.

The aluminium body doesn't rust but corrodes where it touches steel. The steel parts do rust: rear crossmember, outriggers, chassis box sections above the bump stops, the lower bulkhead and footwells, door hinge areas and door bottoms.

t: Can I put tubeless tyres on the original wheels?
x: Not properly. Original Series rims are tube-type. Tubeless radials need wheels with safety humps, which later Defender wheels have. Don't fit inner tubes in tubeless wheels.
Just under 600,000 by February 1968, more than 70% of them exported. The 1,000,000th Land Rover was built in 1976, and about 440,000 Series IIIs were made between 1971 and 1985.

t: Parts & Restoration — Rovers North, L.R. Series Ltd, Paddock Spares, John Craddock Ltd
x: Seals, swivel kits, brakes, wiring and panels: the catalogues Series owners actually order from on both sides of the Atlantic.
Worn first and second gears and tired transfer boxes are the classic Series drivetrain complaints; rebuilt units and uprated parts exist.
When the rear crossmember, outriggers and rails have all been patched, a hot-dip galvanised frame ends the argument.

x: Canvas, seats and door tops wear out; LRO has a video on fitting an Exmoor Trim soft top to an ex-military Series III.
A Series has no crash structure to speak of; external and internal cages are the sensible addition for trail use.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: 235/85R16 is the classic factory size on 110s and the 'sweet spot' most owners recommend; NAS D90s came on 265/75R16. 255/85R16 (about 33") is the popular upgrade and generally fits at stock height, but owners report rubbing on the front radius arms at full lock (fix by winding out the steering stops), against the 45 L auxiliary tank on 110s, and close to the spring brackets at full compression on

t: Can I import a Defender into the US?
x: Yes, if it's at least 25 years old counted from its date of manufacture: NHTSA lets those vehicles in without meeting FMVSS (declared under Box 1 on the HS-7). Newer trucks must comply, which a classic Defender can't. Check EPA and your state's emissions rules too, and make sure the VIN, chassis number and build date line up.

Everything built at least 25 years before the import date, so in late 2026 that's trucks built up to late 2001. That covers 200Tdi, 300Tdi, V8 and early Td5 Defenders (the Td5 arrived in 1998). The Ford 'Puma' Defenders from 2007 won't start qualifying until 2032.

North American Specification Defenders were the ones Land Rover sold new in the US and Canada: 525 1993 Defender 110s (500 US, 25 Canada) and Defender 90s from 1994 to 1997, all V8. About 7,059 were built in total.

t: Why did Land Rover stop selling the Defender in the US after 1997?
x: Regulations taking effect for 1998, including airbag and side-impact door requirements, made it too expensive to keep the old body compliant. The Defender name returned to US showrooms in 2020 on the all-new L663.

For a gray-market truck, the 300Tdi is the simple, mechanical favourite; check the revised timing kit has been fitted. The 200Tdi is cruder but similar. The Td5 is more powerful (122 hp) but electronically managed, so check for oil in the injector loom. In the US, NAS trucks are all 3.9/4.0 V8, which is thirsty but easy to service.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: ECD quotes 12–16 mpg for the factory V8 (12–14 in real-world use), 23–27 mpg for the 300Tdi, 22–26 mpg for the Td5 and 20–25 mpg for the Puma diesels. Roof racks, big tyres and a heavy right foot will take you well under those.

t: How much can a classic Defender tow?
x: CarsGuide lists 3,500 kg (7,716 lb) braked for 2004 Defender 90, 110 and 130 variants. Unbraked trailers are limited to 750 kg. Check your own truck's plate and handbook; the rear crossmember condition matters more than the brochure number.

t: When do I lock the centre diff?
x: Whenever you expect prolonged wheelspin: mud, snow, ice, sand, steep loose climbs. The LT230's stock centre diff has small gears that can fail if a front wheel spins for long, and the diff lock removes that risk. Unlock it on grippy surfaces to avoid driveline wind-up.

The aluminium panels don't rust, but they oxidise, lifting paint and eventually perforating. The steel parts rust: chassis rear crossmember, outriggers, bulkhead footwells and corners, door frames and hinge mounts. Budget for welding unless the truck already has a galvanised chassis.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), Terrafirma
x: Stock springs sag with age and accessories. Heavier springs and better shocks restore ride height and add an inch or two for 255/85 tyres.
Open diffs front and rear; an air locker or ATB limited-slip transforms progress on articulated ground.
Rebuilt or brand-new LT230s, taller ratios for big tyres, ATB centre diffs and heavy-duty 300M shafts.

t: Parts & Restoration — Rovers North, Atlantic British, Lucky8, Britpart
x: Seals, swivel kits, panels, NAS-specific trim, timing kits: these are the US and UK catalogues the community actually uses.
When the frame is past welding, a hot-dip galvanised replacement chassis is the permanent fix.
The NAS trucks wore cages from the factory; external and internal cages are a common addition for serious trail use.

NAS 3.9 V8: API SG/SH, SAE 5W-30 or 5W-40 · ≈6.7 L with filter. 300Tdi: ≈6.65 L with filter (Comma lists 10W-40). Td5 / Puma: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The V8 and Tdi engines use the short spin-on filter. The Td5 also has a centrifugal oil-filter rotor that needs servicing.
OE-type element for your engine Check that the dump valve at the bottom of the airbox isn't split, because it lets unfiltered air in.
Diesel: OE-type element (Tdi: AEU2147L). V8: inline EFI filter [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Diesel trucks that sat for a long time collect water and sludge, so drain the sedimenter as well.
Tdi: ETC8847 glow plugs ×4. V8: plugs and leads per manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] A cold start that smokes and stumbles on a Tdi usually means one or more glow plugs have failed.

Revised kit (flanged crank pulley, idler, tensioner). V8 and Td5 use timing chains, not belts Land Rover revised the 300Tdi tensioner, idler and bottom pulley because belts were wearing early. A yellow paint square on the timing cover was meant to show the fix had been done, but it isn't reliable.

50/50 ethylene glycol antifreeze and water · NAS V8 ≈12.8 L. 300Tdi ≈11.1 L The aluminium V8 can't take overheating. Check the radiator for blocked fins and the viscous fan for drag while the system is drained.

Handbook: ATF M2C33-F or G (as quoted on AULRO) · ≈2.4 L (Comma lists its 75W-80 MTF for the 300Tdi R380) Check the level at the side filler with the truck level. A notchy second gear or third-gear synchro problem on an R380 isn't fixed by changing the oil.
Dexron IID ATF · 9.1 L listed total fill Draining the pan only replaces part of the 9.1 L. Do two drain-and-fills rather than a pressure flush on an old box, and change the pan filter.

EP90 / 80W-90 gear oil, API GL-4 or GL-5 · ≈2.3 L The filler at the back of the case is tapered, so it feels tight before it is fully seated. Don't overtighten it. Use a new copper washer on the drain plug. The intermediate shaft and rear output seals are the usual leaks.

EP80W-90 GL-4/GL-5 · front ≈1.7 L. Rear ≈1.7 L on the Rover axle (one data set lists 2.3 L for the NAS D90). Salisbury 110 rear [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Fill each axle to the level plug on level ground. Defender2 members found the 1.7 L book figure close. Use a new drain-plug washer.

Early trucks: EP90 · 0.35 L per side (handbook). From about 1994: one-shot swivel grease STC3435, one sachet per side Lucky8 lists the STC3435 sachet for the NAS Defender 90 ('94–'97) and the Defender 110 ('93). An AULRO owner's 1994 swivel took about 450 ml to reach the level plug, so fill until it just dribbles out. Weeping seals mean the chrome ball is pitted. See the repairs above.

Dexron IID ATF · 2.8 L system (the 1993 US service checklist says ATF Type F, so [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]). Steering box: EP80W-90 Leaks from the box's input seal or sector shaft are common. Top up and watch the level.
DOT 4 The hydraulic clutch shares the fluid type. A soft clutch pedal usually means the slave cylinder is failing.
Multipurpose lithium grease on the UJs and sliding joints A clunk on take-up usually means a dry UJ or a worn sliding spline. Grease them before chasing the gearbox.

L663 90 110 130 The reboot: aluminium monocoque and independent suspension, unveiled September 2019 and launched as a 2020 model, officially sold in the US again. The Defender that shares nothing with the Defender: an aluminium monocoque on independent air springs that will out-climb its ancestor and then massage your back on the way home. Brilliant off-road, a little too clever for its own good i

Coolant dropping from max to min within 100–150 km with no obvious puddle. Cooling-system pressure tester, sockets · turbo coolant lines and O-rings, coolant to spec

x: Metallic clunk when steering or when the suspension articulates, at no particular angle. Ball-joint splitter, spanners, torque wrench · track rod end
The outer edge of a dealer-fitted arch extension peeling away from the body. Trim tools, cleaner, adhesion promoter · 3M 5925 VHB tape (25 mm)

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: 275/60R20 (about 33 inches) is the popular step up from the factory 255/60R20. A Defender2.net owner fitted it to a coil-sprung 110 on stock 8.5-inch 20s with no spacers and reports no rubbing, even off-road; others warn it can touch on some setups. 275/55R20 runs without rubbing on air suspension at full articulation, and Australian owners run 275/65R18 LT on 18s. The OCTA fits 33s from the facto
Land Rover quotes up to 3,500 kg (UK) and up to 8,200 lb (US). Owners describe the air-sprung 110 as a very stable tow vehicle because it self-levels.
900 mm (35.4 in), with Wade Sensing using the cameras to show water depth. The OCTA is quoted at one metre.

t: Can I put a rooftop tent on it?
x: Yes. Land Rover quotes a static roof load of up to 661 lb (300 kg) and a dynamic load of up to 370 lb on the 110 and 130 (260 lb on the 90) with off-road tyres and the Expedition Roof Rack. V8 models have no dynamic roof rating, and the OCTA's is zero in OCTA mode.
All 110 models have air as standard. The 90 can have coils or air. Coil 90s give 226 mm of ground clearance against 291 mm maximum for air, and lose the height-adjustable modes.
It has a lockable centre differential and a locking rear differential (Land Rover's Electronic Active Differential), plus brake-based torque vectoring and a two-speed transfer case.
Yes. A front-mounted 4,536 kg (10,000 lb) load-rated winch is officially supported, which is unusual for a unibody.

t: How often should I change the oil?
x: The headline service interval is up to 21,000 miles or two years, but Defender2.net members point out that oil changes are flagged by a separate condition-based counter, often around 15,000 miles for diesels in mixed use. Many enthusiasts change oil every 7,000–10,000 miles regardless.

US trucks launched with 2.0 four-cylinder and 3.0 six-cylinder engines, and Land Rover USA's current 110 spec page lists only the 3.0 six, with the OCTA sold as its own model. In Europe and Australia the D250/D300 diesels are the long-distance favourites, though the mild hybrids have had DC-DC converter failures and the diesels have DPF and EGR sensor faults.

It's better than its reputation off-road and worse than a Toyota in the workshop. A TFL review collected early-ownership faults, and common owner reports include DC-DC converters on MHEVs, PM/EGR sensor codes on diesels, steering knocks and several recall campaigns. Keep it on warranty or budget for a diagnostic tool and a good specialist.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Official NEDC figures range from about 7.6 L/100 km (31 mpg US) for the 3.0 diesels to 9.9 L/100 km (24 mpg US) for the P400 and 12.1 L/100 km (19 mpg US) for the P525 V8. One D300 owner reported 40 mpg (imperial) cruising at 110 km/h across France.

t: Rock Sliders, Ladders & Protection — Terrafirma — Defender 2020
x: Sills and rear corners are the first things a 110 hits; Terrafirma's sliders with tree bars and rear ladder are popular L663 fits.

t: Accessories & Spare-Wheel Kit — PowerfulUK — Defender L663
x: Spare-wheel mounting kits, security and trim parts aimed squarely at the L663.

t: Bull Bars & Radiator Protection — Offroad Animal
x: The auxiliary radiators behind the front intakes are vulnerable to stones; an Australian owner points to Offroad Animal's Toro bar as one that protects them.
BFGoodrich KO2 and General Grabber AT3 are owner favourites; the Grabber AT3 is listed in Land Rover's own iGuide and is 3PMSF-rated.
North America's big Land Rover parts house runs L663 builds, including an OCTA on 35-inch tyres with a winch bumper.

A Range Rover Classic in a cheaper suit, with Maestro switchgear, Marina door handles and two sunroofs that leak on schedule. Underneath it's the same coil-sprung, LT230-driven toolkit as a Defender, which makes it the bargain boxy truck nobod

x: Water dripping from the roof lining or rear vents, wet carpets, sagging or stained headlining. Torx T20, screwdrivers, trim tools, silicone sealant · sunroof drain tube EEH100720 (per LandyZone) · roof-rail foam pads
Clonk or jerk on take-off and gear changes, visible cracks or splits in the rear propshaft's rubber 'doughnut' coupler. Spanners and sockets, torque wrench · rubber propshaft coupler, nuts and bolts

High idle on start-up (1,100–2,000 rpm), hunting idle, or idle that won't drop despite the ECU asking for about 700 rpm. RoverGauge and cable, hose clamp, multimeter · idle air control valve, plenum gaskets as needed

Oil on the inside of the front wheels, pitted chrome balls, vague steering. Hub nut socket, torque wrench, spring balance · swivel ball (FRC7065 still stocked by Paddock Spares per LandyZone), seal and bearing kit
MOT advisories, soft metal at the sills or body mounts, daylight through the boot floor. MIG welder, grinder, joddler, bead roller (optional) · sill panels, boot floor panel, body mounts

t: Overheating: bleed and cap before head gasket
x: Coolant pushed out of the expansion tank, rising temperature after recent leaks or top-ups. Coolant, bleed procedure from the workshop manual, block tester · expansion tank cap
Due on interval, or belt debris inside the timing cover. Timing tool, torque wrench · STC4096L modified timing belt kit

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Factory sizes were 205R16 and 235/70R16, which are almost the same height. On a stock-height, stock-geared truck, a LandyZone owner recommends going no bigger than 245/75R16 (about 30.5 inches), which several members run. Owners do run 33s and bigger with lifts; one member says 35s want at least a 4.1 and ideally a 4.37 ring and pinion.

t: When was it sold in the US?
x: From the 1994 to 1998 model years, always with the V8: 3.9 litres with Lucas 14CUX injection at first, then the GEMS-managed '4.0' (same 3,946 cc) from 1996 for OBD-II.

t: How is it related to the Range Rover Classic and Defender?
x: It uses the Range Rover Classic's chassis, suspension and four-wheel-drive system, much of its body structure, and the same LT230 transfer box and Tdi engines as the Defender of the same era.

t: Can I import a diesel Disco 1 into the US?
x: Every Discovery Series I was built by 1998, so all of them are now more than 25 years old. NHTSA allows vehicles at least 25 years old (from date of manufacture) to be imported without meeting FMVSS; check EPA and your state's rules and make sure the VIN and build date line up.

The 300Tdi is the enthusiast favourite: mechanical, economical and shared with the Defender, though it needs the revised timing kit. The 200Tdi is cruder but similar. The V8 is smoother and easy to source in the US but thirsty and sensitive to cooling problems.

t: What fuel economy should I expect from the V8?
x: Not much. One owner of a 3.9 V8 reported about 10.5 mpg (imperial) at 100–120 km/h and was trying to get closer to 14. Tired V8s lose economy as the camshaft wears, according to experienced members.

Two inches is the common, sensible lift using longer springs and extended shocks; owners advise lowering the bump stops so the body isn't damaged at full compression. Owners running bigger lifts fit caster-corrected (6-degree) arms and wide-angle propshafts, and regear for big tyres.
Yes, badly. The usual places are the sills, rear floor and boot floor, inner wings, body mounts and the rear chassis around the crossmember. Three-doors are reported to be worse.

The plastic surround leaks where it meets the metal roof, the frame seal is flimsy, and the drain tubes and cups split with age. LandyZone owners call the drain installation 'appalling'. Resealing and new drains usually cure it.

t: Which Discoveries did the Camel Trophy use?
x: The Discovery was the main Camel Trophy vehicle from 1990 to 1997: 200Tdis from Siberia (1990, three-door) to South America (1994), then 300Tdis from 1995 to Mongolia in 1997. Japan and Germany also got Sandglow Camel Trophy special editions.
A badge-engineered Discovery 1 sold in Japan by Honda, a product of Rover's cross-holding with Honda that ended when BMW bought Rover in 1994.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu (ARB), Terrafirma
x: Springs sag after 25-plus years. Longer springs and shocks restore height and add room for 245/75s or 33s.
An ATB centre differential in the LT230 removes much of the driveline backlash; uprated shafts and lockers suit bigger tyres.

t: Rust Repair Panels — Froggatts — Discovery 1 sills
x: Sills, floors and body mounts are the Disco 1's weak point; repair panels are the difference between a project and a scrapper.

x: When the frame is thin everywhere, a galvanised replacement is the permanent fix; LandyZone members have priced Maer's 300Tdi frame.
