The Range Rover arrived in June 1970 as "A Car For All Reasons": a 100-inch-wheelbase, coil-sprung, permanently four-wheel-drive wagon with an all-alloy Rover V8 and aluminium panels hung on a steel frame. It was conceived as something a Land Rover owner could also drive to dinner, and it accidentally invented the luxury 4x4 in the process. Five generations later, the name has drifted steadily up-

RRC LSE / County LWB The original: two-door then four-door, coil springs, Rover V8, and a 24-year run that created the luxury 4x4. The original luxury 4x4, with the soul of a farm truck. Buy the rust-free one and you'll forgive it everything — buy the shiny rusty one and it'll teach you to weld.

t: Swivel ball seal replacement and regrease
x: Oil weeping from the swivel housings onto the chrome balls and wheels; the truck rolling while in park can mean a CV joint ran dry and failed. Dremel or heavy side cutters · basic sockets · new swivel seals · silicone · swivel grease

t: Viscous coupling replacement (Borg Warner transfer case)
x: Tyres scrub or chirp on tight, slow turns; premature tyre wear on the edges; the truck needs a lot of throttle in slow, tight corners; driveline wind-up. A jacked-up wheel won't turn by hand. Jack and stands · basic hand tools · viscous coupling RTC6044 (same part on Classic and P38A)

Truck sagging at one corner overnight, the compressor running constantly, height-sensor or valve-block faults, or a truck that won't rise to off-road height. Spring compressor · jack and stands · Rovers North RNK5105 or Atlantic British RRC 93–95 coil conversion kit

No heat, a sweet smell or fogged windows (core), or a dead or noisy blower — Atlantic British suggests replacing the blower around 150,000 miles. Phillips and flat screwdrivers · 10 mm deep sockets · trim and radio tools · drill · soldering iron and heat-shrink · new hose clamps · Atlantic British kit #8844 for blower upgrade

Vague or wandering steering, clunks over bumps, and cracked or perished rubber where the radius arms meet the chassis. Jack and axle stands · large sockets · pry bar · Terrafirma TF1003 (replaces NRC4514; also fits Defender and Discovery 1)

Rust holes in the boxed rear crossmember, a sagging or bulging rear floor, cracked welds, movement under load, or a tailgate that no longer lines up. Angle grinder · spot-weld cutter · MIG welder · clamps · squares and straightedge · rust treatment, primer, seam sealer · replacement crossmember

Creeping temperature gauge, coolant weeps, or simply unknown history on an aluminium V8 that hates overheating. Basic sockets · drain pan · radiator, viscous fan, water pump, thermostat, hoses, clamps · antifreeze

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The usual forum answer is 245/75R16 (about 30.5 inches) on stock coils, with the steering stops adjusted to stop rubbing at full lock. Some owners run 265/75R16 with slight chassis rub fixed by the stops. 235/85R16 generally needs a lift or some trimming on these 100-inch trucks.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Bad. The EPA rated a 1990 3.9 automatic at 11 mpg city and 15 highway (13 combined), and the 1995 County LWB 4.2 at 11/15 (12 combined). Hagerty says careful driving helps.
Towing capacity is quoted at 3.5 tons. Note that Hagerty says coil-sprung trucks are more reliable but less suited to towing than the air-suspension trucks.

t: Air suspension or coils — and should I convert?
x: Electronic air suspension arrived on late-1992 trucks for the 1993 model year, mainly the LWB. It rides beautifully but pumps, height sensors and valve blocks fail. Bolt-in coil conversion kits are widely available for 1993–95 trucks and take about 3.5 hours.

t: Does it have a centre diff lock?
x: It depends on the year. Earlier trucks have a manually lockable centre differential. From 1989 a chain-driven Borg Warner transfer case with a viscous coupling locks automatically. On those trucks, check that the viscous coupling hasn't seized.
Yes. ARB makes Air Lockers for Rover-type banjo differentials in both 10-spline (RD127) and 24-spline (RD128) versions. Check which axle shafts your truck has before ordering.

t: Which years or versions should I buy?
x: Buy the most rust-free truck you can afford; condition matters more than the year. Values run from Velar prototypes to two-doors to four-doors, and fuel-injected and LSE four-doors are worth more than carburettor trucks. In the US, choose between 1987–92 coil-sprung SWB trucks and the 1993–95 County LWB with the 4.2 and air suspension. The 1995 trucks get the soft dash.

It can be, if you look after it. Jalopnik's experts say rust is what kills Classics, not the engine. Refresh the whole cooling system, keep up with oil changes, and expect electrical gremlins. Treat it as a third car or a project rather than a daily driver unless it has been sorted.

Hagerty's specialist recommends good-quality 20W-50, changed every 6,000 miles or 12 months. Some owners change it every 3,000 miles. Separately, check the oil in the swivel housings — it is not shared with the front diff.

t: Was there a diesel, and did the US get one?
x: Yes, but not in the US. The VM Motori 2.4 turbo-diesel arrived in 1986 and grew to 2.5 in 1989. Land Rover's 200Tdi replaced it in 1992, followed by the 300Tdi at the end of 1994. US trucks were all petrol V8s.

t: Did the US get the two-door?
x: Not officially. Factory US imports from March 1987 were four-door only. Earlier two-doors in America came through grey-market importers.

t: Suspension Lift — Old Man Emu, Rovers North (OME kit OMERRK1)
x: Old Man Emu springs and shocks add about 1.5 inches of lift and support bumpers, a winch and bigger tyres on 1987–93 coil trucks.

t: Air-To-Coil Conversion — Rovers North (RNK5105), Atlantic British
x: Converting a tired 1993–95 EAS truck to coils makes it simpler and more reliable, and gives a modest lift.

t: Lockers — ARB Air Locker RD127 (10-spline), ARB Air Locker RD128 (24-spline)
x: Lockers make up for the open axles when the truck is crossed up and a wheel is in the air.
Rebuilt viscous couplings for the Borg Warner case, so the truck stops scrubbing tyres in tight turns.

t: Poly Bushes — Terrafirma, Terrafirma TF1003 radius arm bush kit
x: Polyurethane radius-arm and suspension bushes tighten up a wandering front end; the same parts fit the Defender and Discovery.

t: Roof Rack — Front Runner Slimline II (1970–1996)
x: A Classic-specific full-length cargo rack for overland gear, a spare and a shovel.

API SG, SAE 10W-40 or 10W-50 · ≈6.7 L (1991 3.9 V8 data). Later 3.9/4.2: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] These engines aren't fussy about oil, but a fresh filter matters. The ERR3340 filter covers the RRC, P38 and Defender V8s.
OE-type element Check the airbox dump valve and the intake hoses for splits. Unmetered air upsets the Lucas/GEMS fuelling.
OE-type EFI filter [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Old fuel lines and rusty tanks are common on trucks that have sat. Inspect the rubber lines while you're under there.
Plug type and gap per manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Fit new plugs, leads, a distributor cap and rotor as a set. Tired leads cause a lot of rough running on these V8s.
50/50 ethylene glycol antifreeze and water · ≈11.4 L Replace the hoses and thermostat at the same time. Check the viscous fan and the radiator core. See the cooling refresh in the repairs above.
Dexron IID ATF · ≈9.5 L total fill (1991 data) A pan drain only exchanges part of the fluid. Do two drain-and-fills and change the pan filter rather than pressure-flushing an unknown box.

Borg Warner chain case: Dexron IID ATF (M2C33G / Texaco 4291 also listed) · ≈1.7 L. Gear-driven LT230 trucks: EP90 GL-4/5 · ≈2.3 L Do the jacked-wheel viscous-coupling test while you're under the truck (see repairs). A seized coupling causes driveline wind-up on tight turns.
80W/90 EP gear oil, API GL-4 or GL-5 · ≈1.7 L each Fill to the level plug on level ground. Pinion seal weeps are common on old trucks.

Gear oil 90 EP/80W EP · ≈0.33 L per side (1991 data), or one-shot swivel grease STC3435 on later trucks Lucky8 lists the STC3435 sachet for the RRC ('87–'95). Owners regrease when they fit new seals (see repairs). Oil on the chrome ball means it's time for a seal.
Dexron IID ATF · ≈2.8 L system Leaks from the steering box are common, so watch the reservoir level for a few weeks.
DOT 4 ABS trucks (late soft-dash) have a pump and accumulator. Bleed per the manual and check that the pump doesn't run constantly.

No fluid. Leak-check the springs, valve block, compressor and reservoir [CONFIRM IN MANUAL for dryer service] An overnight sag at one corner or a compressor that runs constantly means there's a leak. Many owners convert to coils (see repairs).
Multipurpose lithium grease Grease the UJs and sliding joints. A clunk on take-up usually means a dry UJ.

P38A Last of the ladder-frame, live-axle Range Rovers — 4.0/4.6 Rover V8s, standard air suspension and a lot more electronics. The last Range Rover with a ladder frame and beam axles, wrapped in a 1990s electronics experiment. Cheap to buy, cheap to fix yourself, and ruinously expensive to pay someone else to love.

t: Cooling hose and thermostat refresh (GEMS V8)
x: An ageing cooling system on a 4.0 or 4.6. Cracked or soft hoses, a high or overfilling expansion tank, or a heater that blows lukewarm. On these engines, overheating is what leads to slipped liners and blown head gaskets. 12 mm Allen socket on a ½-in drive · hose-clamp pliers · 5-gallon drain pan · Atlantic British kit 9369SKA (1995–99 GEMS trucks)

t: EAS valve block reseal and compressor rebuild
x: The truck sags overnight, the compressor runs for a long time or keeps cycling, the reservoir is slow to fill, or there's an audible hiss from the valve block or silencer. O-ring kit · compressor piston/seal kit · soapy water · basic hand tools · Nanocom or Faultmate to read and clear EAS faults

One corner drops after parking, cracked or bulging bellows when the truck is at full height, or EAS faults that come back after you clear them. Jack and axle stands · line caps · eye protection · soapy water · diagnostic tool if faults are logged

Wet carpet beside the transmission tunnel that smells or tastes sweet, a misting windscreen, or a coolant level that keeps dropping. Screwdrivers · drill · grinding paste · new O-rings · Nissens 70220/70230 or equivalent matrix if replacing
Hot air on one side and cold on the other, a 'book' symbol on the climate display, or temperature that doesn't change. Multimeter · relays · pollen filters · Nanocom/Faultmate · replacement motors

'Select Neutral' or gearbox-fault messages during range changes, wrong gear indication, or the transfer box refusing to change range. XYZ switch alignment tool LRT-44-011 · multimeter · diagnostic tool

t: Front suspension bushes and ball joints
x: Vague steering, wander, clonks over bumps, uneven tyre wear. The front usually wears out first. Ball-joint press · breaker bar · bush kit (e.g. Polybush radius-arm-to-axle kit)

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: Forum reports say 245/75R16 or 255/70R16, roughly 30 to 30.5 inches. One owner runs 255/70R16 on standard suspension with no rubbing. Another found 245/75R16 clears at full lock at standard and high ride heights, but rubs at the lowest height and can touch the back of the arch at full compression. 265/75R16 (about 31.6 in) rubs when the axles cross up unless you lift the truck and fit an adjustabl

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Poor. The EPA rated a 2000 4.0 automatic at 12 mpg city, 16 highway and 13 combined, and the 4.6 at 11/14/12. The tank holds 100 litres (about 26 US gallons).

t: How much can a P38 tow?
x: 3,500 kg (7,716 lb) braked and 750 kg unbraked, according to published spec sheets for the 4.6 HSE.

Buy the better truck. Buyers' guides say choose on condition rather than displacement. The 4.0 is more likely to blow a head gasket and the 4.6 more likely to slip a liner, so cooling-system history matters more than size. The 4.6 has more power, a 4-pin rear diff and four-wheel traction control from new. It came only with the ZF automatic.

t: Do I have a GEMS or a Bosch engine?
x: Open the hood. A rectangular plenum with '4.0' or '4.6' embossed in the middle means GEMS, the earlier Lucas system. A cluster of intake tubes and no label means Bosch Motronic, which arrived mid-1999. The two use different parts, so check before ordering.

t: Does it have low range and locking diffs?
x: It has full-time four-wheel drive with a two-speed BorgWarner 4462 transfer box, switched electrically. Slow almost to a stop before changing range. There are no factory locking diffs; traction control brakes a spinning wheel instead (rear-only on early 4.0 and diesel trucks, all four wheels on the 4.6 and on later trucks). For bigger tyres, Ashcroft makes heavy-duty 4.10 ring-and-pinion sets for

t: Should I convert to coil springs?
x: It's a common way to simplify the truck. Terrafirma's standard-height kit TF223 is a bolt-in swap. Before you do it, note that air springs are cheap now and leaks are often just perished seals that are easy to fix. UK guides say coil conversions are becoming less popular as EAS parts get cheaper, and a healthy EAS gives you the extra off-road height.

Lucky8's 4-inch kit (Terrafirma heavy-duty springs, +2-in Pro Sport shocks, mounting plates and an EAS override harness) was developed on its own P38 project truck. Lucky8 recommends tyres up to 32.5 in with it. Owners also report about 2 in of lift from Arnott Gen III air springs with Terrafirma shocks. Bigger lifts usually need double-cardan driveshafts (Tom Wood's) to cure vibration, and adjust

t: Is the BMW diesel worth having?
x: It's the economy choice outside the US: a 2.5-litre BMW M51 six with 136 hp and 270 Nm. UK buyers' guides still recommend the petrol V8 and warn about diesel head gaskets (especially on remapped trucks), glow plugs and fuel-system parts. It was never sold in North America.

t: What maintenance gets skipped that I shouldn't skip?
x: Coolant hoses and thermostat: Land Rover's schedule says every 90,000 miles. Automatic gearbox oil about every 70,000 miles. The V8's mass airflow sensor at about 90,000 miles. Ignition leads, which wear quickly on the V8. The EAS compressor filter.

t: Why does the driver's or passenger's footwell get wet?
x: Usually the heater matrix O-rings, or a blocked drain under the heater box. Sometimes it's a leaking matrix. Clogged drains and failed seals can also let water reach the body computer under the seat, so fix wet carpets quickly.

t: Suspension Lift — Lucky8 — Terrafirma P38 4in kit, Terrafirma
x: Lucky8's Terrafirma-based 4-inch coil kit was proven on its P38 'Rhino' project truck and clears tyres up to about 32.5 in. Owners who want to keep air springs run Arnott Gen III springs with longer shocks.
A bolt-in standard-height kit takes the compressor, valve block and air springs out of the equation for remote travel.

t: Driveshafts — Tom Wood's (via Lucky8), Tom Wood's
x: Lifted P38s run steeper driveshaft angles, which causes vibration and wears out U-joints. Double-cardan shafts fix it.

t: Armor & Recovery — Terrafirma sliders TF816, Terrafirma front winch bumper TF007A, Terrafirma rear bumper TF070A
x: Steel sliders with tree bars, a winch-ready front bumper and a heavy-duty rear bumper to replace the plastic one.
Bigger tyres blunt the V8. Heavy-duty 4.10 ring-and-pinion sets restore acceleration and strengthen the diffs.

t: Water & Cooling — Terrafirma snorkel TF159, Allisport AS75 alloy radiator
x: A snorkel raises the air intake for wading and dust. An alloy radiator helps keep a hard-working V8 away from liner-slipping temperatures.

t: Bushes & Steering — Polybush radius arm kit (via Lucky8), Terrafirma steering damper
x: Fresh polyurethane radius-arm bushes and a Terrafirma steering damper tighten up a tired front end.
API SG/SH or ACEA A2:96, SAE 5W-40 or 5W-50 · ≈5.8 L drain & refill (6.6 L dry) Check the dipstick for mayonnaise and the expansion tank for oil. Either one points to head-gasket or liner trouble.
OE-type engine air element, plus the pollen/cabin filter pair Clogged pollen filters affect the climate control and can look like a blend-motor fault (see repairs).
Plug type and gap per manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Misfires on Bosch trucks often come from the leads and coils. Replace the plugs and leads as a set.
V8: OE-type EFI filter [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]. 2.5 DSE diesel: STC2827 Do the diesel filter at purchase on non-US 2.5 DSE trucks.
50/50 ethylene glycol antifreeze and water · ≈11.4 L Replace the hoses, thermostat and expansion-tank cap as a set (see repairs). There's no bleed screw. Warm the engine, let it cool, then top up.

Dexron III ATF · ≈11 L total fill. A drain and refill takes about 5 L An owner on rangerovers.pub measured about 5 L from a drain and refill. Two drain-and-fills refresh most of the fluid without the risk of a flush.
Dexron III ATF · ≈2.0 L drain & refill (2.4 L dry) Range-change faults ('Select Neutral') are usually electrical or an XYZ switch problem, not low oil. See repairs.
Hypoid gear oil, API GL-5 [CONFIRM grade IN MANUAL] · ≈1.6 L each drain & refill (1.7 L dry) Fill to the level plug on level ground. Check the pinion seals.
Sealed ball joints. There's no swivel oil or grease to change Unlike the Classic and Defender, the P38 front axle uses press-fit ball joints. Check them for play while the wheels are off.
Dexron III ATF (or Texamatic 9226) · ≈1.7 L Check the steering box and the PAS cooler pipes for weeps.
DOT 4 An ABS pump that keeps running, or ABS warnings, need diagnosis with a Nanocom or a similar tool.

System runs at about 10 bar / 150 psi. No fluid Park overnight at normal height and check each corner in the morning. Spray soapy water on the springs and valve block to find leaks (see repairs). Never work under a truck resting on deflated springs.
Poly-V serpentine belt Inspect the tensioner and idler pulleys while the belt is off.
Multipurpose lithium grease Grease the UJs and sliding joints. Worn UJs feel like a clunk on take-up.

L322 Monocoque body and all-independent air suspension; BMW-era engines at launch, Ford-era engines from 2005. A Munich-engineered, Solihull-built limousine that still walks up a rock garden on its tiptoes. Buy the paperwork, not the paint. The timing chains decide whether it's a bargain or a boat anchor.

The air suspension won't change height or adjusts erratically, often with no stored fault codes. The sensor pivots seize, and cracked rear sensor bodies let water in, which corrupts the readings. 10 & 13 mm spanners · penetrating oil · locking pliers · dielectric grease · LR020627 (FR) / LR020626 (FL) / LR032106 (rear, both sides)

Clatter on a cold start, more chain noise as the engine ages, or in the worst case an oil-pressure light. Nylon guide debris can block the oil pickup. M62 engine timing/setting tools · crank-locking bar · breaker bar · 32 mm deep socket (ground down) for solenoids · VANOS seal tool · kit TCKL322 or equivalent

t: Cold-start rattle: VANOS seals and non-return valves
x: A brief rattle on a cold start that goes away on a quick restart, on a BMW 4.4 whose guides may still be fine. VANOS seal tool · ground-down 32 mm deep socket · quality oil filter

A chime and a warning message, then the transfer case drops into neutral. Low range engages but high won't, or a 'trans failsafe' message appears. 5A fuse · contact cleaner · basic sockets · diagnostic tool

t: Differential and transfer case oil change (2003–2005)
x: An overdue service. Old oil breaks down and collects condensation, and water in the diffs or transfer case destroys bearings. Drain pan · fluid pump · socket/hex set · Atlantic British kit DTCM200A

Slow or harsh shifts, fluid weeping from the valve-body connector sleeve, or a high-mileage 'sealed for life' gearbox that has never been serviced. Atlantic British kit TRANSM300SKA (pan, sleeve, 7 qt ZF Lifeguard) · fluid pump · torque wrench · scan tool for fluid temperature
A rattle on cold starts from worn tensioner-to-guide contact. Ignore it and the chain can jump timing or snap. TCK5030 kit · TCK5030TOOL timing/crank tool set · crank holding tool · front seal tool

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: On 18-inch wheels, owners say 265/60R18 (about 30.5 in) fits with no problems, including off-road. 265/65R18 has been warned against because it can rub when the air suspension drops. On 20s, 275/55R20 clears the bump stops but rubs the liners at full steering lock. Check that a taller spare still fits in the well.

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: Thirsty. The EPA rated a 2004 BMW 4.4 at 11 mpg city, 15 highway and 12 combined; a 2008 4.4 or 4.2 Supercharged at 12/18/14; a 2011 5.0 at 12/19/15; and a 2011 5.0 Supercharged at 12/18/14. The tank holds 100 litres.
3,500 kg (7,716 lb) braked and 750 kg unbraked. A 2002 4.4 HSE weighs about 2,430 kg at the curb.

t: Which years and engines should I buy or avoid?
x: Owners and buyers' guides generally rate the 2007–2009 Jaguar-engined trucks best: Terrain Response, a locking centre diff and the six-speed ZF. Buy a 2003–2005 BMW 4.4 only with receipts for timing guides (or if you'll do them yourself). Buy a 2010–2012 5.0 only with evidence that the chain tensioners and guides have been updated.

t: Does it have low range and lockers?
x: Every L322 has full-time four-wheel drive with a two-speed chain-drive transfer case you can shift on the move. 2003–2006 trucks use a Torsen centre diff and open axles with traction control. From 2007 the centre diff can lock under Terrain Response, and an electronic rear locker was standard on Supercharged models and optional on others.

t: How do I lift an L322?
x: The usual way is longer ride-height sensor links. Atlantic British's RHSRAL322 rods make the air suspension think it's low, so it holds about 2.5 in of extra height all the time, enough for bigger all-terrains. Its listed fitment is 2005–2012 trucks.

t: Is the air suspension a deal-breaker?
x: No, but budget for it. Springs leak, compressors fail slowly and noisily, and 2003–05 height sensors seize. Genuine parts are expensive (a full air-ride restoration kit for 2003–05 trucks lists at about $2,450), but each part can be replaced on its own. Some long-term owners convert to coils after spring failures.

t: Are the gearboxes really 'sealed for life'?
x: No. Early petrol trucks use a ZF 5HP24, and Td6 diesels use a GM 5L40-E that Australian testers call so bad owners treat it as a service item. Both left the factory with 'sealed for life' stickers. Atlantic British recommends a fluid and filter service every 60,000 miles on the later ZF six-speed.

t: How do I tell which engine I'm looking at?
x: For US trucks, go by model year: 2003–2005 is the BMW 4.4, 2006–2009 the Jaguar 4.4 or 4.2 supercharged, and 2010–2012 the 5.0 or 5.0 supercharged. Parts suppliers split their catalogues the same way, so order by engine as well as year.

t: My BMW 4.4 rattles on cold starts — are the guides gone?
x: Not necessarily. Owners trace many short cold-start rattles to VANOS seals, solenoid non-return valves or a poor oil filter. One owner's rattle stopped after switching to a Mann filter. A rattle that keeps getting worse, or that shows up with low oil pressure, is a different matter. Stop driving and check the guides.

Yes. Club 4X4 calls it great off-road, and its cross-linked air springs are designed to mimic live-axle articulation. On any truck you're considering, check that low range engages and that Hill Descent Control works. The usual first mods for trail use are a sump guard, a sensor-rod lift and all-terrain tyres.
Longer height-sensor links trick the EAS into running about 2.5 in higher, with no new springs or software needed.

t: Underbody Armor — ProSpeed sump guard (via Lucky8)
x: A 6 mm alloy sump guard protects the sump, front diff, bumper and radiator, and bolts to the front subframe.
Rebuild the EAS once, properly, before a trip: compressor, rear springs and front strut assemblies.

t: Bushes & Control Arms — Polybush DA8897 full kit (via Lucky8), Atlantic British control arm kit CA-L322
x: New front arms and polyurethane bushes cure wander and clonks on high-mileage trucks.
The L322 wears through brakes fast. Full disc-and-pad kits make the 30,000-mile refresh simpler.

t: Engine Preventive Kits — Atlantic British TCKL322 timing kit, Atlantic British PCV tune-up kit 9205L322
x: Timing-chain and PCV kits for the BMW 4.4 deal with its two best-known weak spots before they strand you.

BMW 4.4 (2002–05): fully synthetic to ACEA A3/B3, ≈8.5 L refill · Jaguar 4.4/4.2 SC (2006–09): 5W-30, ≈7.7 L with filter · 5.0 NA/SC (2010–12): 5W-20 to WSS-M2C925-A, 8.0 L · 3.6 TDV8: 5W-30 to WSS-M2C913-B/-D (STJLR.03.5003), ≈9.5 L service fill · 4.4 TDV8 (2011–12, DPF): 5W-30 to WSS-M2C934-B / STJLR.03.5005, 9.0 L The DPF diesels must have low-SAPS oil to the exact spec. Owners warn against ove
BMW 4.4: PHE000050 (pair) · Jaguar 4.4/4.2 SC: PHE500021 · Td6: PHE000040 Cheap insurance on a truck with unknown history. Check the airbox for leaves and mouse nests while it's open.
Correct filter by model year [CONFIRM BY VIN] A clogged cabin filter makes the climate control work harder and can hide a damp footwell smell.
Jaguar 4.4 (2006–09): Champion LR005253 x8 · 5.0 V8 (2010–12): genuine set of 8 If the history doesn't show plugs, do them. On the 5.0, inspect the coil packs and plug-well seals at the same time.

2002–05: 50% extended-life coolant (Havoline XLC type), ≈13 L refill · 2010–12: 50% Castrol SF antifreeze, 15 L (5.0 NA) / 16 L (5.0 SC) / 14 L (diesel) Don't mix antifreeze types. On the 5.0, look for weeps at the plastic coolant pipes and the water-pump outlet; on the Jaguar V8s, check the heater and oil-cooler hoses.

ZF 5HP24 (BMW 4.4): Esso LT71141, ≈6.0 L refill · GM 5L40-E (Td6): Texaco ETL-7045E · ZF 6HP26 (2006–09 and 2010–12): Shell ATF M1375.4 / ZF Lifeguard 6 A pan drop only renews part of the fluid: one owner drained about 4 qt from a 10-qt 6HP26. On the 6-speed the filter is built into the plastic pan, so a new filter means a new pan; replace the leak-prone valve-body sleeve while it's off. Fill and

NV225 (2002–05 petrol, Td6 to 2006): Castrol BOT 26 FMB 1 75W-90, ≈1.0 L · Magna Steyr DD295 (2006 onward): Shell TF 0753, 1.5 L The DD295 has an electronically controlled multi-plate centre clutch, so only the friction-modified TF 0753 will do. Specialist Glenrands reports 1.1–1.2 L typically goes back in on a service, so buy 2 L. Replace the drain/fill washers (IYF500010 / IYF500030).

Front: Castrol SAF-XO 75W-90, 0.75 L refill · Rear non-locking: SAF-XO, 1.14 L · Rear electronic locker: Castrol SAF Carbon Mod Plus 75W-90 (LR019727), 1.55 L Identify the rear diff first: the electronic locker has a cylindrical motor on top with a cable. Pump in the exact quantity rather than filling to drips, which overfills and aerates the oil. Diff plugs often seize, so crack the fill plug bef
Texaco Cold Climate PSF 14315 · reservoir ≈1.6 L Look for weeping at the rack and pump hoses while the truck is up on stands.
Shell DOT4 ESL, or a low-viscosity DOT4 meeting ISO 4925 class 6 (2011 handbook) The low-viscosity spec matters for the ABS and stability system. Standard DOT4 is for topping up only.

BMW 4.4: primary LR051050 + A/C belt · 5.0: primary LR064185 + secondary belt Addicted Motors' 'must-do' L322 kit puts both belts on the list alongside the transmission service and front control arms.

Compressor, drier, valve blocks, air springs and height sensors Leave it overnight and measure each corner. Time how long the compressor runs. On 2003–05 trucks, height-sensor faults often store no code. Replace the compressor relay with the compressor: it's a known weak point.
BMW 4.4: WFL000021 · 3.6 TDV8: WJI500030 · Td6: WFL000070 On the 2006–09 Jaguar petrols the filter is part of the in-tank sender assembly, so it isn't a routine item.
Load-test the battery; check charging voltage Low voltage on an L322 throws a cascade of unrelated air-suspension and transmission warnings. Rule out the battery before you chase faults.

L405 All-aluminium monocoque that shed more than 400 kg versus the steel L322. An aluminium-bodied air-sprung limousine that will still claw up a rutted hillside if you ask nicely. Buy one with a service history thicker than its door cards, and a warranty for when it doesn't.

One front corner sitting low after standing, a hiss when the truck lowers to access height, the compressor working overtime, or air-suspension faults that come back after recalibration. Jack and stands · sockets and ball-joint separator · Arnott ASE-3756 (new electronic) or AS-3067 RH / AS-3068 LH (remanufactured, 2013–2018), or OE LR079515 RH · diagnostic tool with air-suspension calibration (e.g

Not a fault — it's the cheapest lift on the planet. The truck sits too low for bigger tyres or rough tracks, or scrapes its sills in ruts. Basic hand tools · Proud Rhino PR25DEF-1 (1 in), PR25DEF-1.5 (1.5 in) or PR25D5 (2 in) lift rods · alignment afterwards

Knocks or clunks from the front over broken surfaces and under moderate braking; vague steering; uneven tyre wear. Jack and stands · large sockets and breaker bar · ball-joint separator · LR072469 (LH) / LR072471 (RH) arms, or Lucky8 polybushed kit NFLCKPB · alignment afterwards

Unexplained coolant loss, sweet smell, weeping at the back of the engine or around the thermostat housing. Plastic pipes typically go around 100,000 km and water pumps around 80,000–140,000 km. Full socket set and torque wrench · coolant and drain pan · ARC050 kit (LR122709/LR109402 rear crossover, LR092992 Y-tube, LR028136 adapter, LR090630 bypass) or SCV85LAUCK kit with water pump and aluminium

t: 5.0 V8 timing chains, guides and tensioners
x: A rattle for a second or two on a cold start, later joined by cam-timing codes P0016, P0017, P0018 or P0019. JLR camshaft and crank locking tools · torque wrench · Lucky8 5LTCK genuine kit (chains LR032048, tensioners LR051008, blades LR051013, guides LR051011/LR051012, aux chain LR032087)

A metallic rattle or knock from the front of the engine at idle, often mistaken for timing chain; a louder-than-normal whine means dry snout bearings. Sockets and torque wrench · snout gasket · 5.0 supercharger repair kit (Lucky8 lists LR088564)

Stop/start that works only sometimes or not at all, rough or slow restarts, low-voltage warnings and odd infotainment behaviour. Battery tester · basic sockets · LR047630 / LR176847 auxiliary battery · diagnostic tool for BMS registration

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: On 20-inch wheels, the FullFatRR consensus is 285/50R20 (about 31.2 in). Two owners run them, one calls them probably the largest that won't rub in any height mode, and the spare still fits the well. 275/55R20 (about 31.9 in) is also fitted by 'quite a few' owners, though one member predicted it might just catch at full lock. Twenty inches is the smallest rim owners trust to clear the brakes, and

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: For the 2016 model year, the EPA rated the supercharged 5.0 V8 at 14 mpg city, 19 highway and 16 combined, the 3.0 supercharged V6 at 17/23/19, and the Td6 diesel at 22/28/24. PistonHeads reports about 30 mpg (UK) in real-world driving for the 4.4 SDV8.
Australian-market figures give 3,500 kg (7,716 lb) braked for the V8s, petrol or diesel, and 3,000 kg for the 3.0 V6s. Check your owner's manual and plate; the figure varies by engine and market.

What Car? calls the 3.0 TDV6 the sensible choice. PistonHeads rates the 4.4 SDV8 as 'a good and reliable engine' without the TDV6's crank issues or timing belt. In the US, the choice is the 5.0 V8 (thirsty, chain and coolant-pipe risks), the 3.0 V6, the Td6 diesel from 2016, or the later hybrids. AutoTrader.ca recommends a 2020-or-newer truck with the straight-six if budget allows.

t: Is the TDV6 crankshaft failure real?
x: Yes, but it isn't universal. Land Rover service bulletin SSM71816 (May 2014) blamed a 'low incidence' of crank failures mainly on wrongly located or rotating main-bearing shells. In a FullFatRR poll of L405 3.0 owners, 88% reported no issues. The usual advice is the correct oil, shorter oil-change intervals than the maximum, and a warranty that covers the engine.

Yes. Every L405 has permanent four-wheel drive with a Magna Steyr DD295 two-speed transfer case, a 50/50 split and a low range, managed by Terrain Response 2 with hill descent control. Change the transfer-box and diff oil at around 30,000 miles.

The easy way is height-sensor lift rods, which raise every air-suspension mode by 1, 1.5 or 2 inches with no electronics. Proud Rhino's rods take about 20–30 minutes to fit, and Lucky8 recommends an alignment afterwards.

t: Can I work on the air suspension at home?
x: Mostly, with the right scan tool. GAP's IID G4 tool lists air-suspension height adjustment and guided calibration for the L405. 2017–2022 trucks work with the standard tool, but 2013–2016 trucks need the optional adapter version. Struts and the compressor unbolt with hand tools, but the system runs at up to 10 bar, so depressurise it first, and the calibration afterwards needs the tool.

The 2018 facelift added the four-bar grille, new LED lights, thicker glass, Touch Pro Duo screens and the P400e plug-in hybrid. More importantly, PistonHeads says pre-2015 trucks had the most electrical and body faults. If budget allows, later is better.
Land Rover quoted 900 mm (35.4 in), 200 mm more than the L322, with up to 303 mm of ground clearance at off-road height.
Yes. Revealed at the 2013 LA Auto Show with deliveries from early 2014, it has a 3,122 mm (122.9 in) wheelbase and is 5,199 mm long — 200 mm more in each than the standard truck.

t: Suspension Lift — Proud Rhino 1" lift rods (Lucky8), Proud Rhino 2" lift rods PR25D5 (Lucky8)
x: Lift rods for the height sensors raise every air-suspension mode by 1–2 inches with no coding, and keep Terrain Response working.

t: Armour — Proud Rhino Rock Sliders PRRSL405K, Proud Rhino Bash Plate PRL405FBP
x: 3/16-inch steel, frame-mounted rock sliders that also shield the vulnerable EAS compressor, plus a front bash plate for the sump and radiator.

t: Winch & Bar — Proud Rhino Hidden Winch Mount PRL405HW, Proud Rhino A-Bar PRL405AB, Proud Rhino L405 Off-Road Package
x: A hidden winch mount that tucks behind the factory bumper on the chassis and tow point, and a frame-mounted A-bar that fits standard and LWB trucks.

t: Cooling (5.0 Sc) — ARC050 aluminium cooling kit (Lucky8), SCV85LAUCK upgraded cooling kit (Lucky8)
x: Swap the brittle plastic crossover pipes for aluminium before they strand you on a trail, ideally with the water pump and thermostat housing done at the same time.

t: Bushes & Arms — Polybush front lower control arm kit NFLCKPB (Lucky8)
x: Polybushed front lower arms tighten up a clunky, wandering front end on trucks that see rough tracks.

t: Roof Rack — Front Runner Slimline II kit KRRR009T (Lucky8)
x: A full-length 1,358 mm Slimline II tray that clamps onto the factory flush roof rails with no drilling.
A dealer-level scan tool for air-suspension heights and calibration, service resets and CCF edits. You need it for any serious home wrenching on an L405.

Petrol 5.0 V8 / 3.0 V6 SC: 0W-20 to STJLR.51.5122 (the launch handbook listed 5W-20 to WSS-M2C925-A), 8.0 L for the V8 · TDV6/SDV6 (DPF): 5W-30 to STJLR.03.5005 / WSS-M2C934-B, 6.0 L · SDV8 (DPF): same spec, 9.4 L The DPF diesels are fussy about oil, so only use oil approved to STJLR.03.5005. Don't overfill the SDV8: put in about 8.5 L, wait, then top up using the electronic level check.
LR011593 (two elements on the V8) Two elements on the V8. Replace both.
5.0 V8: set of 8 (LR032080 in Britpart's kit DA6099) Supercharged V8s with no proof of plugs get them now. Check the coil packs and plug-well seals while you're there.

1:1 Havoline XLC antifreeze and water · refill 6.83 L (5.0 NA), 8.83 L (5.0 SC), 8.93 L (V6 diesel), 7.13 L (V8 diesel) On the 5.0 SC, unexplained coolant loss usually means the plastic pipes under the supercharger (see the repair above), not the radiator.

Shell ATF L12108 · Land Rover lists it as 'filled for life' The filter is built into the pan (LR065238), so a service means a new pan. Drain and refill, then level-check at the specified temperature with a scan tool. Don't flush.
Shell TF 0753 (TL 7300), 1.5 L Use only TF 0753-spec fluid: the centre clutch depends on its friction modifiers. Put in a measured fill. Replace the M16 drain/fill washers (IYF500030).

Front: Castrol SAF-XO, 0.54 L wet fill · Rear non-locking: SAF-XO, 0.85 L · Rear electronic locker: Castrol BOT 720, 1.25 L These are much smaller fills than the L322 figures you'll find on forums. Use the L405 numbers. The electronic locker takes its own fluid.

Texaco Cold Climate PAS fluid 33270 (V8 diesel and V8 SC with Dynamic Response) Trucks with Dynamic Response have hydraulic active anti-roll bars. Leaks at the bar actuators or valve block are expensive, so look for them before you buy.
Shell DOT4 ESL, or low-viscosity DOT4 to ISO 4925 class 6 and LRES22BF03 Check pad and rotor thickness at all four corners. Heavy trucks with big wheels eat rear pads.
Compressor, struts, height sensors Measure each corner after the truck has stood overnight and listen for the compressor running too often. Front struts are the common failure (see the repair above).

Main battery plus an AGM auxiliary stop/start battery (LR047630 / LR176847) Weak batteries cause phantom faults on the L405. Register any new battery with a scan tool so the battery-management system uses the right charge strategy.
Cold-start listen and a scan for P0016–P0019 A cold-start rattle or cam-timing codes point to the timing chains. A rattle at idle points to the supercharger isolator. Know which before you buy.

L460 Fifth generation, revealed October 2021: seven-seat option, plug-in hybrids and a BMW-sourced 4.4 V8. The most capable limousine ever to ask you to install a software update before breakfast. It will still crawl in low range — just don't expect the aftermarket, or the DC-DC converter, to keep up.

t: Rear brake pads (electric parking brake service mode)
x: A pad-wear warning (one owner's P440e needed rear pads at 31,000 miles, another owner's at 16,000), or grinding at the rear. Jack and stands · sockets · pad spreader · scan tool with EPB service mode (e.g., GAP IID, which lists 2022–2025 L460 support) · new pads

'Low battery, please start engine' messages, a truck that is electrically dead after a few days parked, or alarm and keyless-entry glitches. Battery tester · lift or ramp (lithium battery under driver's seat on some trucks) · LR047630 / LR176847 auxiliary battery where fitted · diagnostic tool for BMS registration

'Stop – electrical fault detected' with a red battery light, the 12-volt battery not charging, and possibly loss of drive. Often no stored faults, and it may clear itself before coming back. JLR-capable diagnostic and programming tool · replacement DC-DC converter module

t: Transfer box and driveline oil change
x: Preventive. Owners suggest doing the transfer box at around 60,000 miles, along with the ZF gearbox and both differentials. Sockets and drain plugs/washers · fluid pump · Land Rover-specified transfer fluid (≈ 2 L)

None. Owners just don't trust a 20,000-mile interval, and the 2024 model-year D350 schedule dropped to 10,500 miles or 12 months. Sockets · filter housing tool · drain pan · new sump plug washer · correct-spec oil · scan tool for service reset (e.g., GAP IID)
No receiver, and you have a 7,716 lb-rated truck and a trailer. Sockets and torque wrench · trim tools · Lucky8 RRL460TOWKITVINFIRST combo or genuine VPLKT0326 hitch · towing module VPLYT0295

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: There is no forum consensus yet. Owners haven't published L460 all-terrain fitment the way L405 owners have, and the off-the-shelf sensor-link lift kits sold for the L405 don't list the L460. Factory wheels run from 21 to 23 inches, and one owner fitted L460 21s with 275/50R21 tyres to an L405. If you want sidewall, 20-inch wheels are the realistic floor: Lucky8 lists 20×9.5 ET30 wheels for the L4

t: What fuel economy should I expect?
x: For 2023, the EPA rated the P400 at 18 mpg city, 26 highway and 21 combined, and the 4.4 V8 at 16/21/18. The P440e plug-in hybrid was rated 51 MPGe on electricity and 21 mpg on petrol alone.

Land Rover USA quotes up to 7,716 lb for the P400 and the V8s, 6,614 lb for the current plug-in hybrid, and 5,511 lb for Range Rover Electric. Earlier P440e trucks were listed at 5,511 lb. Check the figure for your exact model year and powertrain.

t: Does it still have low range and a locking diff?
x: Combustion and hybrid models keep a twin-speed transfer box with high and low range. Upper trims get an Electronic Active Differential with torque vectoring, while the base SE has an open rear differential with torque vectoring by braking. Terrain Response 2, All Terrain Progress Control and hill descent control are standard.

2022–2023 P530s use BMW's N63 twin-turbo 4.4. From the 2024 model year, JLR fitted BMW's S68, also used in the 615 PS SV. Owners on FullFatRR call the S68 'significantly more refined.' It's too early for long-term reliability data on either in this truck.

t: How far does the plug-in hybrid go on electricity?
x: PHEVs use a 38.2 kWh battery (31.8 kWh usable) and a 105 kW motor. Land Rover estimates about 50 miles of real-world electric range. A 7 kW home charger fills it in about 5 hours, and a 50 kW DC charger gets it to 80% in under an hour.

Yes. Range Rover Electric is on order books in the US for the 2027 model year. It has an EPA-estimated range of 333 miles, twin 260 kW motors, 660 lb-ft, 800 V charging (10–80% in about 22 minutes on a 350 kW charger), a 35-inch wading depth and 5,511 lb of towing.

Only in the long-wheelbase body, and Land Rover USA says LWB seven-seaters aren't available as plug-in hybrids or EVs. Four- and five-seat layouts are also offered. Check recall 23V252000 on 2022–2023 seven-seaters for the second-row seat frame welds.

The early record is mixed. NHTSA lists more than a dozen recalls across the 2023 and 2024 model years, and the DC-DC converter, 12-volt battery drain and software glitches dominate the FullFatRR technical board. Buy one with a warranty, a clean recall record and connected software that actually updates.

t: Can I use a GAP tool on it?
x: Yes. GAP's IID G4 lists 2022–2025 L460s on the standard tool, for fault codes, live data, service resets, calibrations, air-suspension height adjustment and CCF edits. FullFatRR owners use it for proximity-locking and other CCF tweaks.

t: Can I get sliders or a bash plate?
x: Not easily. A 2025 FullFatRR thread found no off-the-shelf sliders or underbody protection, and members suggested a fabrication shop would charge €3,500–4,000 for tree sliders and plates. It's a gap the aftermarket hasn't filled the way it has for the L405.

x: The L460's electrics are hungry. Keep the right replacement and charging kit on hand rather than a random jump pack.

When Land Rover ended classic Defender production at Solihull in January 2016 after 67 years, chemicals billionaire Sir Jim Ratcliffe tried to keep it alive. Jaguar Land Rover said no. So Ratcliffe did what billionaires do: he founded a car company, Ineos Automotive, and named its first product after his favourite pub, The Grenadier in Belgravia, where the idea was first kicked around. The result

B58 petrol B57 diesel (non-US) 2,922 mm WB The five-door, five-seat original: ladder frame, Carraro beam axles, BMW six, three lockable diffs available. US gets the petrol B58 only. The old Defender's spirit with a BMW heart and Italian tractor axles. Huge capability, real quirks, and steering that only got properly sorted for 2026.

Service due, or an 'Engine Oil Low' message. Many owners do an early break-in change, then shorter intervals than the factory schedule. 32 mm socket · drain pan · BMW-type oil filter with O-ring and crush washer · oil: an owner quoted the manual as 6.5 L of 0W-20, ACEA C2 / BMW LL-17FE (check your own manual)

Service interval, or after dusty trail use. One owner changes it every second oil change (about 5,000 miles). PZ3 (Pozidriv #3) screwdriver · filter (a member says Mahle LX3985/1 matches OEM; not officially confirmed)

Weak airflow or musty smell. Note: one owner found almost no cabin heat in 15°F weather with the filter removed. Headlamp · curved pick · cardboard to lie on · OEM INEOS #100326881, or Microguard 3692 reported to fit (no charcoal layer); Mann CUK25001 reported not to fit

t: Spare carrier clearance after upsizing tires
x: With 285/75R17 or 255/85R17 tires, the spare hits or barely clears the small rear door. Socket set · washers · or Leitner Designs Grenadier tire relocation bracket

t: Tire rub on one side only: re-center the body on the frame
x: Bigger tires rub on one side but clear on the other, with the same wheels and offset on both sides. Floor jack · large sockets · torque wrench · factory torque specs

t: Door doesn't latch / door button sticks (recall 25V147)
x: Exterior door button stays pressed in, door doesn't fully latch, or the head unit shows a door-open warning that turns red with chimes once you're moving. VIN check at nhtsa.gov/recalls · dealer appointment
Usually none until it's serious. A loose or missing nut can let the steering rod ball joint come apart, and you lose steering. Flashlight · VIN check · dealer appointment
Electrical faults on accessories wired through the auxiliary switch panel relay, or none at all. VIN check · dealer appointment

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: From the factory the Grenadier rides on LT265/70R17 or LT255/70R18 (about 32 in.). INEOS Forum owners report 285/70R17 fits with no problem. 285/75R17 (about 34 in.) is the popular sweet spot: owners report no rub on stock suspension, but you'll probably need a couple of washers under the spare carrier to clear the small rear door. Owners have also run 295/70R17, 255/85R17 and 35x11.5R17 (the 35s

3,500 kg braked, about 7,700 lb (GearJunkie lists 7,716 lb). That's well above a Wrangler's 2,495 kg in Australian spec. Payload is about 1,680 lb in US figures, so a heavy trailer plus a fully loaded overland build will run into the GVWR before the hitch rating.

t: What fuel economy does it get?
x: Not much. The EPA rates the 2024 petrol Grenadier at 15 mpg city, highway and combined, and the Trialmaster at 14 mpg on premium fuel. The tank holds 90 litres (about 23.8 gal), which gives a range of roughly 350 miles in mixed use at the EPA figure, less with a roof tent and big tires.

t: How much weight can go on the roof?
x: 150 kg (330 lb) dynamic, meaning while driving, and 420 kg (925 lb) static, meaning parked. That's enough for a rooftop tent with people in it. Front Runner's Slimline II kit attaches to the grab-handle brackets with no drilling and weighs about 57 kg itself, so count it against the dynamic limit.

t: Can I get the diesel in the US?
x: No. In the US and Canada the Grenadier and Quartermaster come only with the BMW B58 3.0 petrol six, 282 hp and 332 lb-ft. The B57 diesel (245 hp, 406 lb-ft) is sold in Europe, Australia and other markets.

t: Does it have lockers, and how does the 4WD work?
x: It has permanent four-wheel drive through a Tremec two-speed transfer case (2.5:1 low), with a centre diff lock on a lever. Front and rear lockers come with the Rough Pack, which also adds BFG KO2 tires. It's standard on the Trialmaster and was a $2,850 option on base and Fieldmaster trucks at US launch. The locker switches are in the overhead panel.

t: What oil does the B58 take and how often should I change it?
x: An owner quoting the manual on the INEOS Forum lists 6.5 L of 0W-20 meeting ACEA C2 / BMW LL-17FE. Check your own manual, since the oil forums note the US manual is vague. One owner reports the manufacturer schedule as every 12,000 miles. Many owners do an early break-in change (500–1,000 miles on dealer advice) and then change it every 5,000–7,500 miles, especially if they tow.

t: Is the steering really that bad?
x: Before 2026, it's slow: a Bosch hydraulic recirculating-ball box with almost four turns lock to lock, which The Drive found wandered on the highway and was heavy when parked. Some owners like it off-road, and Owl sells a $2,150 pump kit and a Fox stabilizer. For MY2026 Ineos fitted a variable-ratio worm gear with more assist and a tighter on-center feel. GearJunkie called it 'a big leap forward'.

t: Which years should I buy or avoid?
x: There's no bad engine to avoid, since every US truck has the B58. The early US trucks (MY2024) carry all three recalls, so get proof they're closed. MY2026 brings the revised steering, HVAC and driver-assist tweaks plus more than 40 smaller changes. If you plan to drive a lot of highway miles, 2026 is the one to buy.

It's too new for a long-term verdict. The BMW six and ZF eight-speed are widely used and well proven elsewhere. Owner reports focus on electronics: modules, false warnings, software reflashes, sticky door buttons and water ingress, plus three US recalls. Most owners on the forums still sound happy, but a good dealer matters more than usual.

t: How capable is it off-road out of the box?
x: Very. It has 264 mm of ground clearance, 800 mm wading depth, and approach, breakover and departure angles of 35.5°, 28.2° and 36.1°, with solid axles and up to three locking diffs. GearJunkie noted there's no disconnecting sway bar, but the soft coils still articulate well.

Gives room for 285/75s and up, and restores ride height under bumpers, winches and roof tents. Eibach, the factory spring supplier, makes a Pro-Lift set (about +2.5 in. front, +1.2 in. rear). Watch driveshaft angles.

t: Steering — Owl — steering pump upgrade, Owl — Fox steering stabilizer
x: The pre-2026 steering is the Grenadier's most common complaint. Owners fit pump upgrades and dampers to improve on-road feel.
Tires bigger than about 33 in. crowd the small rear door, wiper and camera. A relocation bracket moves the spare out of the way.

t: Roof Rack — Front Runner (Dometic), Owl — Flat Earth rack
x: The roof is rated for 150 kg dynamic and 420 kg static, so it's made for a tent. Racks mount to the grab-handle points with no drilling.

t: Bumpers & Winch — Owl — Highline winch bumper, Agile Offroad
x: There's a factory winch option, but aftermarket bumpers add approach angle, protection and a proper winch mount.
A full-length skid plate protects the transfer case, tank and lines when the Carraro axles are articulating over rocks.

A Grenadier with a foot of extra frame and a bed that takes a Euro pallet, as long as you lift the spare out first. It's a seriously capable off-roader that happens to have a tailgate, and in America it carries a 25% chicken tax on top.

t: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
x: The Quartermaster has the same axles and front suspension as the wagon, and it comes on LT265/70R17 or 255/70R18 (about 32 in.). Wagon owners on the INEOS Forum report 285/70R17 fits without rubbing and 285/75R17 (about 34 in.) fits on stock suspension. Treat 35s as the outer limit. One Quartermaster owner recommends narrow 35s on near-factory offset wheels, such as 255/85R17 or 35×10.5. Because t

t: How much payload does it have?
x: It depends on market and engine. Ineos quoted 1,675 lb at US launch. In Australia it quotes 907 kg for the petrol and 832 kg for the diesel, against a 3,550 kg GVM. That's below most one-tonne utes and the 79 Series LandCruiser. Expedition Portal's optioned Trialmaster (winch, rack, dual batteries) had about 1,400 lb left.

3,500 kg braked (about 7,700 lb), the same as the wagon, with a 7,000 kg GCM and a 350 kg towball limit in Australian spec. With a heavy trailer and a loaded bed you'll reach the GCM and payload limits before the hitch rating.

t: Will a Euro pallet really fit?
x: Yes. There's 1,337 mm between the wheel arches, enough for a 1,200 × 800 mm pallet. You have to take the spare wheel out of the bed first.

It stands upright in the bed. Mounted underneath, it would cut into a departure angle that's already down to 22.6°. Ineos also offers a roof mount and a 15-litre lockable box that fits in the middle of the spare. Owners have moved it under the deck or under the rear axle.

t: Can I get the diesel in the US?
x: No. US trucks have only the BMW B58 3.0 petrol six (282 hp, 332 lb-ft). The B57 diesel (183 kW, 550 Nm) is sold in Europe, Australia, New Zealand and other markets.

t: Why does it cost so much more than the wagon in the US?
x: Mostly the 25% chicken tax on imported light trucks. At launch the Quartermaster cost $15,400 more than the Station Wagon. When new tariffs arrived in April 2025, total duty rose to 50%. Ineos said it would absorb most of that, but still raised the price 11%, to $94,500 including shipping.

t: How does it drive compared with the wagon?
x: It's much the same, with a longer turning circle: about 14.5 m against 13.5 m before 2026. Unladen it can feel jittery over small bumps, and it settles with weight in the bed. Expedition Portal found it quieter and more comfortable than the wagon. Top Gear noted the light rear end can lose grip on slippery climbs, which is where the lockers and all-terrain tires help.

t: What fuel economy does it get?
x: Australian test-cycle figures are 12.6 L/100 km for the petrol and 10.5 L/100 km for the diesel. Edmunds lists 14 mpg combined for the US truck. Towing a caravan, Caravan World saw the high 20s in L/100 km from both engines. The tank holds 90 litres. Caravan World says about 10% of Australian Grenadier buyers fit a Brown Davis long-range tank, which adds 78 litres.

The engines haven't changed, so the main question is steering. MY2026 trucks have the variable-ratio box, about a 5% tighter turning circle, better HVAC and a quicker way to silence the speed-limit chime. Earlier trucks can be fitted with Owl's steering pump upgrade, which Owl says fits both the Grenadier and Quartermaster. Whichever year you buy, run the VIN for recalls.

t: What camper and canopy options exist?
x: Dirtbox Overland sells a canopy camper made for the Quartermaster bed for $11,499, and Norweld makes full-length, compact and half canopies plus trays. Leitner Designs makes a full-length roof rack (375 lb on-road, 200 lb off-road). INEOS Forum owners have fitted Dirtbox caps. Ineos's own accessory list includes a canvas tonneau, a roll-top cover and a hardtop.

t: Canopy & Camper — Dirtbox Overland — Quartermaster canopy camper, Norweld — Quartermaster canopies
x: The bed is a pallet-width box with an upright spare in it. Canopies and canopy campers turn it into secure storage and a bed off the ground. Watch payload.

t: Suspension & Load Support — Owl — Eibach Pro-Lift springs (Grenadier and Quartermaster), Dirtbox Overland — rear air-bag kit
x: Restores ride height under a canopy and gear, and makes room for 34–35 in. tires. The springs and air bags fit both Grenadier bodies.

t: Roof Rack — Leitner Designs — Quartermaster ACS full-length rack
x: Puts the tent, solar panels or the spare up top and leaves the bed free. The Quartermaster rack bolts to the roll cage, not the gutters.

t: Steering — Owl — steering pump upgrade (Grenadier and Quartermaster)
x: Pre-2026 trucks have the slow, non-self-centring box. Owl sells a $2,150 pump upgrade that it says works on both the Grenadier and the Quartermaster.
Outside the US, the cab-chassis plus an aluminium tray gives a flat, wider deck with drawers and water tanks. That's how the Kaiju was built.

B58 petrol: 0W-20, ACEA C2 (dealers also cite C5 / API SP), BMW Longlife-17 FE+ · 6.5 L per the manual as quoted by owners; buy 7 L. B57 diesel: 0W-30 (the diesel manual lists Petronas Syntium 7000 E 0W-30) · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Hood in maintenance position, engine cover off. 32 mm socket on the canister cap on top of the engine, 17 mm drain plug with a new copper washer, 25 Nm. Owners re
Panel filter with white felt pre-filter (glued on some, clipped into the box on others) Captive PZ3 screws on the airbox. If the history is unknown, just replace it, because it's cheap.
OEM INEOS #100326881 Behind a hinged plate under the passenger footwell (LHD). The glovebox stays in. Arrow toward the cabin.
BMW B58 plugs · gap/spec [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] If the truck is near 48k and there's no record, do them now. Plug fitment below is listed for the BMW 340i B58; confirm against the INEOS parts catalogue.
[CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Non-US diesels only. Replace if there's no record, and more often on questionable fuel.

BMW LC-18 coolant (BMW 83195A42DF3 = Frostox HT-12), 50/50 with distilled water · capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Don't top up with generic green or older BMW GS 94000 coolant. Owners note many aftermarket brands don't list LC-18.

ZF Lifeguard 8 ATF · ≈10.6 L reported by an owner [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Do a drain and pan/filter change (the filter is built into the pan), not a flush. The Grenadier pan has a second, smaller pickup port, so aftermarket aluminium pans may not match. Fill level at the right temperature: use the Offroad › Temperatures screen and keep the truck level.

Fuchs Titan Sintopoid 75W-90 (75W-85 also acceptable) · 1.8 L, or 2.64 L if the oil cooler and lines are drained too O-ring-sealed drain and fill plugs, 15 Nm. Fill to spill isn't reliable because the cooler lines drain back, so measure what comes out.

SAE 80W-90 GL-5 · 2.1 L per axle (workshop-manual figure quoted on the INEOS Forum). Note: Agile Offroad's diff-cover instructions call for 75W-140. Remove the FILL plug first, because owners have snapped fill plugs after draining. 12 mm hex plugs (M22×1.5), 31 Nm; INEOS plug part GRA-5000-021220 (the O-ring isn't sold separately). The fill plug is magnetic. Same fluid with or without the lockers.
DOT 4 (SAE J1703) If the date is unknown, flush it, especially after water crossings.
[CONFIRM IN MANUAL] The recirculating-ball steering is hydraulic. Owners with big tires and heavy steering look at Owl's upgraded pump. Check for leaks at the box and pump.

Retorque suspension and body mounts; clear the body and safari-hatch drains Dealer first-service packages include a suspension retorque and drain clearing. Run the VIN for open recalls (door button 25V147, steering ball-joint nut 23V903, aux switch panel 23V828) before anything else.
[CONFIRM IN MANUAL] Dealers include a battery health test in the annual service. Trucks that sat on a lot often have a tired battery, which causes odd electrical warnings.
